532234|2026-03.headline: NALCO FY26 revenue rose 6.28% to Rs.17,843 crore and PAT 9.22% to Rs.5,816 crore, with FY27 alumina guidance of about 25 lakh tons.
532234|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as the best ever year on physical output, sales and financials, with revenue from operations up 6.28% to Rs.17,843 crore, EBITDA up 8.72% to Rs.8,613 crore and PAT up 9.22% to Rs.5,816 crore. Alumina realisation fell from about $580/t (FY25) to about $370/t (FY26), offset by higher volumes and a metal realisation rise to about $2,700/t. Management guided to lower alumina prices of $300-310/t for FY27 and LME averaging around $3,000-3,100/t as Middle East smelter curtailments unwind. The 5th stream refinery (2 lakh t) is scheduled for commissioning from June 2026, with the smelter and captive power plant project (0.5 mtpa) planned for ordering in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of Rs.135 crore in FY25; Q4 profit of Rs.11 crore

segments.name: Alumina
segments.commentary: FY26 sales volume about 23 lakh t vs 20.75 lakh t production in FY25; price effect of about Rs.2,659 crore offset by about Rs.1,714 crore volume benefit, net adverse impact about Rs.784 crore. Domestic sales rose to about 1.37-1.4 lakh t from 40,000 t, exports about 13.09 lakh t.

segments.name: Aluminium (metal)
segments.commentary: FY26 cast metal production about 4.71 lakh t (+2.61%), capacity 4.6 lakh t; FY27 plan 4.73 lakh t. Pricing is linked to LME with export premium fixed via six-monthly export tenders; no hedging. Q1 FY27 realisation guided at about $3,500-3,600/t for the quarter.

segments.name: Chemical (caustic soda / chlor-alkali)
segments.commentary: Chemical segment revenue fell about 12% from Rs.7,600 crore to Rs.6,694 crore as per the analyst's figures; management cited lower alumina-linked pricing. Caustic soda cost rose from about Rs.42,177/t average in FY26 to about Rs.45,000/t expected in Q1-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Coal (Utkal captive)
segments.commentary: Captive production about 4.0 mt in FY26 (+41.84%), target 4.8 mt in FY27 against total requirement of about 7.2 mt. Captive coal cost about Rs.1,500/t vs linkage about Rs.1,800/t and E-auction about Rs.2,100/t.

guidance_outlook: FY27 alumina production and sales planned at about 25 lakh t, around 2 lakh t above FY26; management said 2 lakh t is the minimum and could reach 3-3.5 lakh t depending on commissioning.
FY27 alumina realisation expected at $300-310/t average, with spot at $310-320/t; management cited surplus from Indonesian refineries and Middle East smelter curtailments.
FY27 LME average expected around $3,000-3,100/t once the Middle East supply disruption normalises; spot LME was about $3,550-3,600/t in April 2026.
Management expects FY27 PBT to stay above about Rs.2,000 crore per quarter run-rate if volumes hold and cost does not rise; alumina price decline seen as offset by metal prices.
Employee cost guided lower in FY27 as about 250 superannuations are offset by recruitment; pay revision impact of 10-15% expected from January 2027 (FY28 onwards).

Capex: about Rs.2,000 crore in FY26-27, Rs.4,000-5,000 crore in FY27-28, peaking at Rs.8,000-10,000 crore in FY28-30 for the 0.5 mtpa smelter (about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore) and power plant (about Rs.12,000 crore, to be shared 50:50 with NLC JV).
capex_capacity: 5th stream alumina refinery (2 lakh t): commissioning to start June 2026, taking 3-4 months to reach 50-60% of rated capacity; about one to two months delay possible. Capital work in progress about Rs.6,300 crore, of which about Rs.5,500 crore relates to the 5th stream and is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Proposed 0.5 mtpa aluminium smelter with 270 MW captive power plant: DPR and technology licensor under way; board approval targeted around Aug-Sep 2026; tendering 6-7 months; groundwork from around April-May 2027; completion targeted December 2030 to early 2031.
Power plant to be a 50:50 JV with Neyveli Lignite Corporation (MoU signed, advanced negotiations), with NLC's Talcher coal mine nearby for coal security.
Additional wire rod mill of about 60,000 t (roughly two years) and MI annealing furnace to lift rolled products from about 2,000 t/month to 2,500 t/month.
Utkarsh JV with Mishra Dhatu Nigam discontinued; the Board cited negative IRR on a Rs.4,500-5,000 crore capex plan.
Captive coal target 4.8 mt in FY27; EC clearance for the enhanced coal output expected in about three to four months.
demand_pricing: Middle East smelter curtailments (Qatalum, EGA, Dubal and one other, cut around 50%) reduced alumina demand; Middle East used to take about 40-50% of alumina exports.
Spot alumina tenders recently at $310-336/t; company is relying only on spot tenders with no long-term contracts at present. Recent long-term contract priced at 11-11.5% of LME versus 15-17% earlier.
Japan and Asian premiums rose sharply; NALCO's export premium is fixed for six months via tenders, with the next export tender expected within a month or two.
Domestic alumina sales target of 2.5-3 lakh t in FY27 (about 1.4 lakh t in FY26).

Input cost trend for Q1 FY27: CP coke about Rs.57,000/t (from Rs.53,000), CT pitch about Rs.57,000/t (from Rs.53,000), aluminium chloride about Rs.1.30 lakh/t (from Rs.1.21 lakh), HFO about Rs.70,000/t (from Rs.46,000). E-auction coal prices reported as flat over the last two months.
Aluminium cost of production about Rs.155,000-160,000/t (FY26 average about Rs.156,000/t); alumina cost about Rs.20,000-22,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 alumina and aluminium volume guidance and the 5th stream ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 alumina target about 25 lakh t (+2 lakh t), metal about 4.73 lakh t vs capacity 4.6 lakh t. 5th stream commissioning starts June 2026 with 3-4 months to stabilise; one-two months delay possible.

qa_highlights.question: How much alumina export volume was there and what share goes to the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 exports about 13.09 lakh t and domestic about 1.37 lakh t. Middle East historically took 40-50% of exports, now sharply reduced; no volume impact yet per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 0.5 mtpa smelter capex be phased and what are the numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about Rs.4,000-5,000 crore in FY28 (in management's FY27-28 wording), rising to Rs.8,000-10,000 crore in FY29-30 peak; total smelter about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore and power plant about Rs.12,000 crore, with JV share reducing NALCO's cost to about Rs.23,000-24,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the employee cost and other expenses jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said employee cost fell 18% to 15% YoY, with about 351 retirements and 358 inductions in FY26 saving about Rs.65 crore. Other expenses included about Rs.40 crore red mud pond provision and Rs.54 crore additional fly ash transport provision, which are non-cash.

qa_highlights.question: What are alumina and aluminium price expectations for FY27 and what is the margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Alumina $300-310/t average; LME about Rs.3,000-3,100/t on average. Management said the metal price gain (about $400/t vs FY26 at $3,000-3,100) would offset alumina decline; metal is about 73% of revenue vs 27% alumina.

qa_highlights.question: What is the coal mix and cost per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Total requirement 7.2 mt; captive 4.8 mt target FY27 (4.0 mt FY26); balance mainly FSA linkage from Coal India, with e-auction only 10-15%. Captive about Rs.1,500/t, linkage about Rs.1,800/t, e-auction about Rs.2,100/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the wage revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Pay revision from January 2027 expected to raise employee cost 10-15% (possibly 12-13%) in FY28; FY27 impact estimated around Rs.100 crore additional, per management. Per-tonne cost expected to fall with volume growth.

risks_watch: 5th stream alumina refinery (2 lakh t): commissioning from June 2026 with 3-4 months to stabilise; management flagged one to two months possible delay, and FY27 alumina volume upside depends on commissioning pace.
Alumina price pressure: spot at $310-320/t, management guiding $300-310/t average for FY27; no long-term contracts currently, and the long-term contract rate fell to 11-11.5% of LME from 15-17%.
Metal price normalisation: management expects LME to fall from about $3,550-3,600/t (April 2026) to about $3,000-3,100/t average, which is central to the margin offset argument.

Input cost inflation in Q1 FY27: HFO up to about Rs.70,000/t from Rs.46,000, CP coke and CT pitch up to about Rs.57,000/t, caustic soda rising to about Rs.45,000/t; management said cost of production would rise but stay within Rs.160,000/t.

Capex and execution: 0.5 mtpa smelter (about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore) and 270 MW power plant (about Rs.12,000 crore, 50:50 JV with NLC) depend on DPR, board approval around Aug-Sep 2026 and the NLC JV agreement; EC clearance for captive coal expansion expected in three to four months.
Wage revision from January 2027 expected to raise employee cost 10-15% in FY28; export premium is fixed for six months via tenders, and the next export tender is expected within a month or two.
key_quotes: Today is a historic day for NALCO. The Board of Directors have approved the financial statements for the financial year '25-'26, registering the best ever performance in every front.
So, both areas in alumina and metal, we have looked for the growth.
Two lakh is the minimum we are targeting. It can go to maybe 3 lakh or 3.5 lakhs also, depending on the commissioning process.
It is very difficult to predict now.
532234|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 physical and financial performance and on the metal price outlook, with management repeatedly calling results the best ever. Noticeably cautious and vague on alumina pricing beyond FY27 and on the timing and size of the 5th stream ramp-up, and on Middle East export volumes, where management said it was very difficult to predict.

rows.why: Management expects PBT to stay above about Rs.2,000 crore per quarter if volumes hold, with metal price gains (about $400/t above FY26's $3,000-3,100 assumption) offsetting the alumina price fall, but input cost inflation and the 10-15% wage revision from January 2027 are headwinds.

rows.why: 5th stream 2 lakh t alumina refinery is under construction with commissioning from June 2026, about Rs.5,500 crore of its Rs.6,300 crore CWIP expected to be capitalised in FY27, and management flagged only a possible one to two month delay.

rows.when: FY27 (alumina ~25 lakh t, metal 4.73 lakh t)

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new branded product or molecule launches discussed; the only new items are the wire rod mill (about 60,000 t, planned) and MI annealing furnace lifting rolled products from 2,000 to 2,500 t/month, which are minor.

rows.label: Alumina price reset to $300-310/t in FY27
rows.why: Management guided FY27 average alumina at $300-310/t versus about $370/t in FY26 and $580-595/t in FY25, with no long-term contracts and the long-term rate down to 11-11.5% of LME from 15-17%.

rows.label: Middle East alumina export demand loss
rows.why: Middle East smelters cut output around 50%, and the region historically took 40-50% of exports from FY26 exports of 13.09 lakh t; management said volume impact is very difficult to predict.

rows.label: Employee cost reduction in FY27, wage hike in FY28
rows.when: FY27 lower; January 2027 onward for wage revision
rows.why: About 250 superannuations guided to lower FY27 employee cost, while 10-15% pay revision from January 2027 adds about Rs.100 crore in FY27 per management and more in FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 physical and financial records and the metal price outlook, but cautious and vague on alumina pricing beyond FY27, the 5th stream ramp-up timing, and Middle East export volumes; analysts pressed on these points.

532234|2026-06.headline: NALCO Q1 FY27 total income rose about 39% YoY to INR 5,400 crore and PBT about 88%, with the 5th Stream refinery delayed to a late-2026 start.
532234|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the best-ever first quarter on revenue and profitability, with record bauxite, hydrate and wind power output. Total income rose from INR 3,930 crore to INR 5,400 crore, PBT grew about 88% and EBITDA about 78%. Raw material inflation of about INR 15,000-16,000 per tonne of metal (caustic soda, CP coke, HFO) was largely offset by spot alumina prices of about $370/t versus a Q1 realisation of about $323/t. The 5th Stream refinery (1 million tonne) has slipped by roughly 2-3 months, with mechanical completion now targeted for September-end 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Annualised Q1 about INR 1,600 crore (Q1 INR 395 crore)
financial_highlights.change: Lower; average CTC down from about INR 36 lakh to about INR 33 lakh
Up from about INR 20,000/t last year

financial_highlights.metric: Metal cost increase from raw materials
financial_highlights.value: About INR 15,000-16,000/t; Q1 metal cost about INR 1,70,000/t
financial_highlights.change: Last year average about INR 1,57,000/t; Q2 guided about INR 1,70,000-1,72,000/t

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material cost burden in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Attributed to higher raw material prices

financial_highlights.value: About INR 10,500 crore as on 30 June 2026

financial_highlights.change: Up from about $60/t roughly 5-6 months earlier

segments.name: Alumina
segments.commentary: Q1 realisation about $323/t; spot tenders in July-August about $370-380/t, with management guiding Q2 average near $370/t. Alumina sales target FY27 is 1.6 million tonnes versus about 1.4 million tonnes last year.

segments.name: Aluminium (metal)
segments.commentary: Production was at about 4.72 lakh tonnes last year, with FY27 guided to about 4.76-4.77 lakh tonnes and a possible 4.75 lakh tonne run-rate. Domestic prices are LME plus premium from export tenders, with the premium reset every 3-4 months. LME was about $3,200/t at the call.

segments.name: Captive coal
segments.commentary: Q1 output was 8.80 lakh tonnes after about 5 days of technical outage at the start of the quarter. FY27 target is 4.8 million tonnes, against about 4 million tonnes last year, with the EC expected in about 2-3 months. Captive landed cost is about INR 1,600/t versus e-auction coal at INR 3,500-3,600/t.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Record Q1 wind power generation was reported. A 1,080 MW power plant is planned as a 50:50 JV with NLC, with a 30:70 debt-equity structure.

guidance_outlook: 5th Stream refinery (1 Mt) mechanical completion by September-end 2026, then integrated trials. Stabilisation takes 3-4 months to reach 60-70%; about 2 lakh tonnes of alumina is still targeted in FY27.
Alumina capacity goes from 2.1 Mt to a rated 3.1 Mt from FY28, with 3.2-3.3 Mt targeted. Bauxite output is about 2.2-2.3 Mt today.
Captive coal target 4.8 Mt in FY27. Pottangi mine production expected from October 2026 after road work.
Metal cost of about INR 1,70,000-1,72,000/t in Q2. Alumina cost guided at INR 21,000-22,000/t. Alumina spot realisation expected at about $370/t, roughly $50 above the Q1 average.

Smelter expansion of 0.5 Mt with a 1,000+ MW power plant is targeted for Board approval around October-November 2026 and completion by December 2030. Total capex is about INR 24,000-25,000 crore to FY31.
FY27 capex target INR 1,500-1,800 crore, rising to about INR 2,500 crore in FY28 and then INR 4,000-7,000 crore per year thereafter.
Employee count is 4,848 as of Q1 end, with a 170-200 reduction each year over the next 3-4 years. A pay revision from 1 January 2027 may add about 15% to employee cost in Q4.
capex_capacity: 5th Stream refinery: 1 Mt alumina, about INR 5,600 crore cost, internally funded. Commissioning delayed by about 2-3 months from the June target.
Smelter expansion: 0.5 Mt aluminium, EGA technology licence to be signed about August 2026. DPR in 3-4 months, with package ordering in about 8-9 months.

Power: 1,080 MW JV with NLC (50:50), total cost about INR 12,000 crore, NALCO share about INR 6,000 crore with equity about INR 3,500 crore total and bank debt guaranteed by NALCO. Coal is sourced from NLC mines in Talcher.
Captive coal expansion: 4.8 Mt, EC expected in 2-3 months. Pottangi bauxite mine MDO appointed, but production is held up by local resistance over an 8 km access road.
Panchpatmali bauxite reserve about 110 Mt plus new mines of about 100-120 Mt, giving a 15-20 year balance life at about 8 Mtpa.
demand_pricing: Alumina spot prices rose on Rusal and Chinese refinery red-mud curtailments and higher New Guinea bauxite costs. About 60-70% of alumina goes to the Middle East.
Alumina realisation is now about 10-11% of LME, down from 14-15%. Management sees 11-12% as the long-run level.
Domestic aluminium premium rose to about $110/t from about $60/t, attributed to Middle East war supply disruption. Management expects it to hold or fall as the war eases.
Input costs: caustic soda about INR 45,000/t in Q1 rising to about INR 49,000/t in Q2, CP coke INR 66,000-70,000/t (vs INR 44,000 last year), HFO INR 75,000/t (vs INR 46,000 last year).
Industry metal deficit of about 0.88 Mt is cited, with LME forecast at $3,000-3,200/t for the rest of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 5th Stream refinery commissioning delayed by about 6 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Mechanical completion slipped by 2-3 months. Over 50 packages are in progress and mechanical completion is targeted for September-end, followed by water runs and then production. Output of about 2 lakh tonnes of alumina is still targeted in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall, and will it stay low through FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Average CTC fell from about INR 36 lakh to INR 33 lakh due to superannuation of high-paid staff and entry-level hiring. Last year's provisions for leave and gratuity and lower PRP accruals also contributed, and the trend should continue for the next three quarters. Q4 will rise because of the pay revision.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost inflation erode margins as aluminium prices soften?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal cost rose about INR 15,000-16,000/t from raw materials. Management said higher alumina prices (about $370/t against a $320 expectation) should offset this, and Q2 metal cost is guided at INR 1,70,000-1,72,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any LME-linked alumina term contract for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The term contracts earlier this year priced at about 10% of LME and were cancelled. Management will only tender when it gets better percentages, around 12-14% of LME.

qa_highlights.question: Coal stocks and monsoon risk for the refineries?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive coal covers about 60-70% of smelter power needs at Angul. Refinery coal stock is only 2-3 days against a 10-15 day norm because of rake priority to power plants. Management expects improvement after summer.

qa_highlights.question: How will the smelter and power capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex to FY31 is about INR 24,000 crore, with the JV's 30:70 debt-equity split. NALCO's cash reserves of about INR 10,500 crore and internal accruals of about INR 3,500 crore a year are expected to fund the smelter without new borrowing.

risks_watch: 5th Stream refinery mechanical completion by September-end and ramp-up to 60-70% over 3-4 months. Any further slip affects the 2 lakh tonne FY27 target.
Refinery coal stock at 2-3 days against a 10-15 day norm during monsoon, dependent on rake allocation.
Pottangi mine start-up depends on the 8 km access road amid local resistance. Target is October 2026.
Domestic premium of about $110/t may fall as Middle East supply normalises. Spot alumina at about $370/t may also soften.
Captive coal EC approval expected in 2-3 months to reach 4.8 Mt.
Pay revision from January 2027 adds to Q4 employee cost. The 0.5 Mt smelter Board approval is expected in October-November 2026.
532234|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volumes, realisations and cash generation, with Q1 presented as a best-ever quarter. Cautious on timelines, with the 5th Stream delay and the Pottangi access road both acknowledged as uncertain. Some answers were evasive or deferred to follow-up, notably the coal linkage/e-auction split and the premium breakup.
key_quotes: Our target is by September end, we have to complete mechanical completion of all these packages, do the integrated trial first.
Premium has increased. Our earlier premium was around $60. Now it has gone up to around -- we did the tender last around $110.
We have a balance of INR 10,500 crores now every year, seeing our profitability and the PAT, we are adding INR3,500-plus crores, because we are expecting earning the PAT of INR 6,000-plus crores.
So, we need not go to the market for borrowing for our smelter expansion, see, our cash reserve and our future earning potential.

532259|2026-03.headline: APAR Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR6,603 crores; PAT of INR254 crores was INR285 crores before INR31 crores of one-offs.
532259|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR6,603 crores, with domestic sales up 33.6% and exports up 13.3% YoY. Reported PAT of INR254 crores (3.8% margin) included about INR31 crores of one-offs (gratuity/leave encashment, ECB mark-to-market, and a legal provision); management says the operating PAT was about INR285 crores, up around 14%. FY26 revenue was INR22,902 crores (+23.3%), EBITDA INR2,067 crores (9% margin) and PAT INR977 crores (4.3% margin). Management flagged a near-term slowdown from the Middle East war, metal and freight cost spikes, polymer shortages and project deferrals, while reiterating medium-term growth and raising FY27 capex to about INR1,500 crores.

segments.name: Conductor
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR3,764 crores (+29.9% YoY); EBITDA INR44,919/MT vs INR41,430 a year ago; premium products 49.3% of revenue. FY26 revenue INR12,712 crores (+32.7%), crossing INR10,000 crores, EBITDA INR43,012/MT vs INR36,683; order book INR7,671 crores at March 31; order inflow INR11,450 crores in FY26.

segments.name: Oil (specialty and transformer oil)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 5.6% YoY with volumes roughly flat; EBITDA INR5,656/KL vs INR5,873/KL, including about INR15 crores of forex provision. Exports were 36.3% of Q4 revenue vs 41.7%. FY26 revenue INR5,373 crores (+6%), EBITDA INR5,943/KL vs INR6,145/KL. Domestic transformer oil +12.2% for FY26.

segments.name: Cables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,903 crores (+35% YoY); EBITDA INR202 crores at 10.6% margin (+34.5%). FY26 revenue INR6,220 crores (+25.8%), EBITDA INR633 crores at 10.2% margin; cables overtook oil as the second-largest segment. Order book about INR1,800 crores.

guidance_outlook: Conductor medium-to-long-term EBITDA guided at INR35,000-36,000/MT plus tailwinds; no explicit FY27 guidance given.
Cable volumes targeted to grow about 25% a year; conductor volumes about 10% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the capex raise cable volumes, and does domestic competition affect margins?

532259|2026-06.headline: Apar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29.1% to INR6,591 crore and PAT rose 77.7% to INR467 crore, a record quarter.
532259|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 29.1% YoY to INR6,591 crore, with EBITDA post open-period forex up 62.7% to INR814 crore and margin at 12.4% versus 9.8%. PAT rose 77.7% to INR467 crore (7.1% margin), which management called the highest quarterly sales and profit in company history. Oil division was the largest incremental contributor, helped by inventory gains on rising fuel prices, partly offset by a ~INR94 crore provision. Conductor volumes fell 6.7% as customers deferred manufacturing clearance on conventional conductors amid the aluminium price spike, while premium mix rose. Management declined to answer guidance, forecast or funding questions because of a pending shareholder approval for securities issuance.

qa_highlights.question: Why was oil EBITDA about INR25,000 per kL, and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to low-cost historical inventory being sold at higher market prices as fuel prices rose. It would not say whether such margins recur, and noted provisions were made as of 30 June per accounting standards.

qa_highlights.question: Why were US exports weak, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a Section 232 disruption in the prior quarter halted US orders, and most US deliveries are on DDP terms, so revenue recognition lagged. It said recent approvals and two large utility contracts support future shipments.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the conductor backlog is executable and what is its geographic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding the two large orders, most backlog should execute in about a year, with some spill-over. Exports (56.8% of INR10,190 crore) are spread across North and South America, Europe, Africa, and Asia.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is HVDC and premium products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HVDC ordering so far is small; one US utility order includes a high-voltage line, and most HVDC ordering is still to come. No specific premium share in the book was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a difference in margin between domestic and export conductors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export margins depend on product specification and do not always run lower. Domestic conventional products earn lower margins than export ones because of quality standards. Blended EBITDA per ton was given; the split was not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume and realisation split for cables and conductors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave revenue growth only, not volume, and said US sales by geography are not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How are metal-price swings affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said primary sales fell due to customer stocking and deferral, while secondary sales held up and fundamental demand is intact.

qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 45 to 50 days, broadly stable; conductor debtor and inventory days improved QoQ.

532259|2026-09.headline: Apar Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 21.3% YoY to INR6,931 crore and EBITDA 57.8% to INR787 crore, with a record INR12,025 crore order book.
532259|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR6,931 crore (+21.3% YoY, +5.2% QoQ) and EBITDA after forex was INR787 crore (+57.8% YoY, margin 11.4%, +270 bps), with PAT up 77.8% to INR447 crore. Roughly INR800 crore of conductor and cable sales on DDP terms were in transit at quarter end, which depressed US revenue (down 29.7% YoY) and conductor/cable dispatches. Conductor volumes fell 9.2% YoY on delayed TBCB clearances and metal-driven customer deferrals, while the oil division's margins were boosted by contract buying and volumes fell about 20%. Management expects Q3 and Q4 conductor volumes to beat H1 and the in-transit revenue to be recognised in Q3.

Credit rating upgraded one notch from AA- to AA

Q2 orders include a first Z-shaped conductor order from a Scandinavian utility, a KPCL OPGW order of about INR960 crore (48-fibre), and a 144-fibre OPGW order in Central America.

Commodity inflation: copper up about 50% and aluminium up about 35% in the quarter; aluminium MGP at a four-year high; steel prices also up sharply. Freight to Europe and LatAm rose 2-3x, now showing signs of easing.
Management attributes volume declines to TBCB awardees delaying manufacturing clearances, with a 36-month execution limit and heavy penalties on delay.
Chinese competition remains severe because of the SHFE-LME arbitrage; Apar is focusing on utility rate contracts in the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28, and what is the Singapore investment about?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic capex is about INR1,500 crore over 12-15 months with INR500 crore spent; overseas expansion is still being closed. The PSPL resolution is an enabling one for investment in the Singapore subsidiary, with details to come later.

qa_highlights.question: Is cable margin moving to 11-12%, and what is the data centre margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 11-12% and delivered 11% in Q2; US data-centre cables carry higher margins than Indian ones because of higher specifications, while Indian data-centre competition is intense.

qa_highlights.question: Will conductor volumes recover, and has the TBCB delay eased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the decline to be arrested in Q3 and H2 volumes to be stronger than H1, because of year-end project completion deadlines and penalties.

qa_highlights.question: Is oil Q2 margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says some gain came from buying on contract versus spot; these are not normal margins, and the company will keep limiting volume to quality business.

532281|2026-03.headline: HCLTech Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3.3% QoQ to $3,682M with FY27 guidance of 1%-4% cc growth, weighed by two US clients and a soft software quarter.

532285|2026-03.headline: Geojit's FY26 profit absorbed planned investments; distribution income up 10% and equity MF net inflow share rose to 0.40 from 0.33.
532285|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as the first year of "Geojit 2.0", a shift toward recurring income (mutual fund distribution, advisory, PMS, insurance) with investments in sales headcount, IT and brand. Net sales headcount rose by about 700 to 3,768, including 650 in sales, at a cost of about INR29 crores, and brand spend rose by about INR15 crores. Profitability was hit by these investments, with about INR54 crores of transformation expenses booked and ROE reduced as brokerage income fell. Management said the next two years would carry similar investment costs, and it stopped field hiring for the current year because of the West Asia conflict.

532285|2026-06.headline: Geojit Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR160.4 crore and PAT to INR19.8 crore, but management guided to continued cost pressure and no hiring for several quarters.
532285|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR160.40 crore, up 11% YoY, with PBT of INR25.99 crore (up 4% QoQ) and PAT of INR19.83 crore (up 14% QoQ). Employee cost rose INR18 crore on sales force expansion, DIFC hiring, tech team additions and higher incentives, though management said employee cost would normalise after a lower insurance-incentive quarter. Customer assets reached INR1.11 lakh crore (up 15% QoQ), mostly from market appreciation, with recurring assets at INR26,000 crore. Management said margin benefits from FY26 investments would take a couple more quarters, and that hiring has been paused except for replacements due to Middle East conflict and market conditions. Leadership succession was also confirmed, with Jones George becoming MD from 1 October.

532285|2026-09.headline: Geojit Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 2.5% YoY to INR 165.82 crores, but cost growth and weak cash-market broking kept profitability subdued.
532285|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 165.82 crores, up 2.5% YoY and 3.38% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 36.7 crores and PBT of INR 20.62 crores. H1 revenue rose 6.72% while H1 EBITDA was INR 78.23 crores, with management attributing the margin pressure to higher employee and technology costs alongside subdued cash-market transaction income. Recurring revenue AUM rose to INR 26,737 crores in H1 from INR 23,230 crores at end-FY26, and asset management AUM (PMS plus AIF) grew 39% from March to INR 2,018 crores. Customer assets were broadly flat at INR 1.12 lakh crores as market correction in September offset inflows.

532286|2026-03.headline: Jindal Steel Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,647 crores (INR 10,093/t) on ASP up INR 4,743/t QoQ, with FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt.
532286|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery: consolidated gross revenue rose 28% QoQ to INR 19,399 crores and adjusted EBITDA reached INR 2,647 crores, helped by a rise in HRC and TMT rebar prices and Angul volume ramp-up. Sales volume grew 15% QoQ to 2.62 Mt as the Angul expansion took steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa. A one-time impairment of INR 1,433 crores (standalone) and INR 834 crores (consolidated) was booked on the Australian WCL asset after the shaft was closed. Management said the major capex programme is essentially complete and the focus shifts to asset sweating and deleveraging.

segments.name: Steel (India, Angul/Raigarh/Patratu)
segments.commentary: FY26 production 9.25 Mt (+14% YoY) and sales 8.68 Mt (+9% YoY). Q4 production 2.65 Mt (+6% QoQ, +26% YoY) and sales 2.62 Mt (+15% QoQ, +23% YoY). Flat/long mix was 52:48 in Q4 and 49:51 for FY26.

segments.name: Raw materials / overseas mines
segments.commentary: Iron ore sourcing about 60% outside purchases and 40% captive, with pricing described as stable. Mozambique is EBITDA positive, South Africa operating but not EBITDA positive, and Australia is closed with minimal cash burn.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi power plant commissioned (two 525 MW modules); ramp-up to complete within H1 FY27. Surplus power to be sold but described as not material to financials.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 11–11.5 Mt and sales at 10.5–11 Mt.
Q1 FY27 coking coal prices expected to rise by USD 20–25/t sequentially; iron ore movement of plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month.
Slurry pipeline (Barbil–Angul) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; savings of about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps up.
Port facility to be commissioned; DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) expected towards end of FY27; PP2 also remaining.
Capex guidance of INR 7,500–10,000 crores for expansion and sustenance capex; remaining programme capex INR 11,545 crores.
Leverage expected to normalise by Q2 FY27; value-added flat mix expected to move from about 50% toward 70%.
Start-up costs of INR 125 crores in Q4 are said to be finished and not recurring.
capex_capacity: Steelmaking capacity raised to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa after BOF2 and BOF3 (3 Mt each) at Angul; iron-making capacity increased by 6.6 Mt through BF2 (4.6 Mt, operational) and DRI2 (2 Mt, under construction).
Cold rolling complex of 1.2 Mtpa commissioned at Angul to support value-added product mix.
Coal pipe conveyor from Utkal C thermal coal mine to Angul is operational; slurry pipeline from Barbil to Angul close to completion.
Total planned capex programme INR 47,043 crores: INR 25,924 crores spent up to FY25 and INR 9,574 crores in FY26, leaving INR 11,545 crores.
Thakurani-A1 iron ore block declared preferred bidder; Saradhapur Jalatap East coal block awarded at end of last year.
Rail rake programme of about 79 rakes: 72 acquired, remainder expected within 2–3 months.
demand_pricing: Management expects India steel demand growth of about 9–9.5% and cites FY26 finished steel consumption of 164.2 Mt (+8% YoY) and Q4 consumption of 44.6 Mt (+10% QoQ).

Realisations lag because the order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations. Management said the market is holding firm despite a slight dip in recent weeks.
Management declined to give a Q1/Q2 realisation upside estimate, saying the market is hard to predict.
Flat sales focus is on infrastructure first, then building and construction, downstream products and automobiles. HSM grades developed for niche products are ramping in the current quarter.
Management said the Q4 sales run rate reflects seasonality, so no large sequential volume pickup is expected.
Safeguard duty on flat steel imports reduced to 11.5% from 12% effective 21 Apr 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will steel and realisation gains continue into Q1, and have contracts been reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts on earlier prices continue and ASP rose strongly in Q4 because of the spot/contract lag; the market is holding firm, though slightly softer recently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company shift to asset sweating rather than further capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the capex programme is essentially complete and the focus is on sweating assets, with INR 7,500–10,000 crores allocated to expansion and sustenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is value-added share falling and what is the target mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the priority during ramp-up is utilisation, with mix optimisation starting in H1 FY27 and stabilising in H2. Flat mix is about 50:50 today and is expected to reach about 70% flat over time.

qa_highlights.question: What were the start-up costs this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q4 start-up costs at INR 125 crores, most of which were booked in Q3, and said these will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the slurry pipeline savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slurry savings are about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps. Full utilisation is not expected this year, but per-tonne savings do not depend on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further write-downs on overseas assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no further write-downs are expected, based on an independent valuation. Australia has minimal cash outflow, and Mozambique is EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: What are the raw material cost moves into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal is expected to rise USD 20–25/t QoQ in Q1. Iron ore is expected to move by about plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month and is hard to predict.

risks_watch: Value-added product share fell to about 61% from 66% QoQ, and management says mix will move back toward normal levels only over time.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20–25/t in Q1 FY27 could compress margins if steel prices soften; a dip in steel prices was acknowledged.
FY26 EBITDA per tonne fell to INR 10,482 from INR 11,712 in FY25 even as volume rose.
DRI-2 is due towards end FY27 and PP2 is also pending; slurry pipeline commissioning is due in Q1 FY27.
Leverage (1.66x net debt/EBITDA) is expected to normalise only by Q2 FY27.
Management gave no EBITDA margin or revenue guidance for FY27, only volume guidance.
Overseas mine EC capacity increase is pending with no date given.
532286|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volumes, demand and the end of the capex cycle, with management repeatedly calling the market healthy. Evasive on pricing, margins, revenue and the timing of DRI-2 and raw material moves, and it referred several questions to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Our focus is on sweating the assets and getting returns out of them.
I think you are going to see a little bit of movement in the first two quarters of this year and then a stabilization in the second half of the year.
It is a cost. Cost cannot be reversed.

financial_highlights.change: +28% QoQ vs INR 15,172 crores in Q3 FY26
Per-tonne down from INR 11,712 in FY25
Net debt was INR 8,876 crores in FY22

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,433 crores standalone (USD 159 mn); INR 834 crores consolidated (USD 93 mn)

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Slurry pipeline savings of INR 750–1,000/t of steel from Q1 FY27 and start-up costs (INR 125 crore in Q4) not recurring support margins, offset by coking coal up USD 20–25/t and FY26 EBITDA/t down to INR 10,482 from INR 11,712.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Major capex programme 'essentially complete' with BOF2/BOF3 (3 Mt each) and BF2 already live, taking steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa; only DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) under construction for towards end FY27, which falls at the edge of the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt vs FY26 sales of 8.68 Mt (+21–27%), with BOF2/BOF3 live and production guided at 11–11.5 Mt; but management said Q4 run-rate reflects seasonality and no large sequential pickup is expected.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said focus is on sweating assets with INR 7,500–10,000 crore allocated to expansion and sustenance capex against INR 11,545 crore remaining programme; no new greenfield capex signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 ASP rose INR 4,743/t QoQ and contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations, but management declined to give any realisation upside estimate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coking coal expected up USD 20–25/t QoQ in Q1 FY27 and steel prices showed a slight dip in recent weeks, so margin compression is possible; no EBITDA guidance was given to measure against.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: HSM grades for niche products are ramping in the current quarter and flat mix is to move from about 50% toward 70% over time, though no specific product dates were given.

rows.label: Leverage normalises by Q2 FY27
rows.why: Net debt INR 16,019 crore at 1.66x net debt/EBITDA and D/E 0.43x; management guided normalisation by Q2 FY27 as capex winds down.

rows.label: Slurry pipeline commissioning
rows.why: Barbil–Angul slurry pipeline to save about INR 700/t of iron ore (INR 750–1,000/t of steel) as it ramps, with savings not dependent on utilisation.

rows.label: Contract prices lag spot
rows.why: Order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations, but market dipped slightly in recent weeks.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, demand (9–9.5% growth) and the end of the capex cycle, but cautious and evasive on realisations, margins, coking coal and iron ore moves, and DRI-2 timing; analysts pushed on pricing, write-downs and mix.

532286|2026-06.headline: Jindal Steel Q1FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 2,667 crore, INR 11,937/ton, with ASP up INR 7,500/ton despite 15% sequential volume drop.
532286|2026-06.overview: Q1FY27 revenue fell about 8% QoQ on a plant maintenance shutdown (BOF refractory change), with sales volume down 15% sequentially. ASP rose about INR 7,500/ton on stronger steel prices and richer mix, and value-added share rose from 61% to 66%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,667 crore (INR 11,937/ton, up INR 1,843/ton), while PAT was INR 844 crore and finance cost rose to INR 548 crore as Q4FY26 expansion assets entered the P&L. Management guided to net debt/EBITDA below 1.5x in Q2FY27 (Q1: 1.71x) and a sequential cost recovery from the shutdown reversing, with the slurry pipeline targeted for commissioning around August.

segments.name: Flat products
segments.commentary: NSR moved about INR 7,000/ton QoQ higher per management. HRC prices were firm through the quarter, though management cited HRC down about INR 800/ton versus Q1 average in recent pricing.

segments.name: Long products
segments.commentary: NSR moved about INR 4,500/ton QoQ higher per Sandeep Modi. TMT rebar prices fell about INR 8,000 per index in recent weeks on monsoon seasonality, while rails, rounds, specialty angles and quench-and-tempered plates held prices.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume guidance of 10.5-11 million tons maintained; management expects to recover about 300,000 tons of hot metal lost in Q1.
Q2FY27 cost structure expected to improve on no shutdown, operating leverage (about INR 2,000/ton in Q1) not repeating, and coking coal up a further $12-15/ton.
Slurry pipeline (18 MTPA design) expected to commission in first half of August, subject to monsoon; about INR 700/ton iron ore cost benefit from Q2 per management.
Cost reduction campaign targeting at least INR 1,000/ton, mainly electricity, fuel, coke, oxygen and yield (98% to 98.5%).
Angul blast furnace hot metal to ramp from 11,000 t/d to 12,000 t/d in September and 13,000 t/d by December.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1.5x in Q2FY27.
FY27 capex about INR 8,500 crore; about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1. Ongoing capex envelope of INR 7,000-10,000 crore per year on value-added products.
capex_capacity: Cumulative expansion spend INR 37,457 crore of announced INR 47,043 crore; FY27 plan about INR 8,500 crore, about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1.
Crude steel capacity installed 15.6 MTPA; FY27 output expected at about 11-11.5 MT, with 12.5 MT possible via blast furnace readjustment.
Angul: two blast furnaces (BF1 at 10,000 t/d rated, running about 11,000 t/d; BF2 rated 13,000 t/d), one DRI plant (5,000 t/d), EAF and BOF 1/2/3 (BOF 2 commissioned Sep-25, BOF 3 Mar-26).
Raigarh: two blast furnaces at 6,800 t/d combined (100% utilised), 10 DRI plants, three EAFs; Raigarh hot metal cited as 3.6 MT.
Slurry pipeline: 18 MTPA capacity, 60% Fe and 35-40% water; pellet plants of 6 MT existing plus 6 MT under addition, plus a 5 MT sinter plant, to absorb about 17-18 MT/year.
Plate capacity about 2 MT/year going to 2.5 MT; hot strip mill (commissioned FY24) rated 5-5.5 MT of HRC.
demand_pricing: Indian crude steel production down about 6% QoQ to 42 MT and finished steel consumption down about 7% to about 41.5 MT in Q1 on monsoon seasonality.
Management expects construction recovery from end-August after monsoon; HRC firm, TMT weak.
Imports of HRC via advance licences cited as a pressure on commodity flats; management says value-added grades are insulated.
Coking coal: $15/ton further increase expected; blend optimisation and coke imports from Indonesia cited as offsets.
Iron ore prices set largely by NMDC and OMC, which management treats as uncontrollable.
Share of high-EBITDA products targeted to rise; product EBITDA ranges from about INR 7,000 to INR 25,000/ton per management.

qa_highlights.question: What are the new management's key priorities and expansion plans at Angul?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: utilise 15.6 MT capacity and shift mix to value-added grades; growth funded from earnings at INR 7,000-10,000 crore capex per year, with no commodity capacity additions and no new borrowing to expand.

qa_highlights.question: Current NSR movement and Q2 price outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flats about INR 7,000/ton higher QoQ and longs about INR 4,500/ton higher QoQ; recent HRC about INR 800/ton lower and TMT about INR 8,000 lower, expected to recover post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 volume fall and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Shutdown was needed to replace BOF refractory after heat life of 9,000-10,000; about 300,000 tons of hot metal lost; FY27 volume guidance of 10.5-11 MT maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of QoQ cost increase of about INR 5,500/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore about INR 500/ton, Middle East conflict impact $12-13/ton, coking coal about $23/ton, and operating leverage from the shutdown about INR 2,000/ton.

qa_highlights.question: Quantified cost savings over next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least INR 1,000/ton cost reduction; slurry pipeline about INR 700/ton; Vishal Chandak pointed to 18-20% ROCE targets to back-calculate project EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA/ton not rising with value-added share?
qa_highlights.answer: Product-wise EBITDA is not disclosed; about 50% of portfolio is high-EBITDA, with aim to convert 1.5-2 MT of low-EBITDA volume to value-added.

qa_highlights.question: Concerns about frequent senior management changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said eight new board-level faces were brought in, including CFO, CHRO and VP HR; about 1,800-2,000 upper-middle managers are stable.

risks_watch: Long product (TMT) price correction and monsoon-driven demand weakness; timing of post-monsoon recovery.
Coking coal and Middle East-related input cost pressure, with $12-15/ton further coking coal increase expected in Q2.
Slurry pipeline commissioning slippage beyond August due to monsoon or trials.
Blast furnace ramp to 12,000 t/d in September and 13,000 t/d by December; Q1 rain-related electrical grid failure cited.
Net debt/EBITDA reaching below 1.5x in Q2FY27 from 1.71x.
Rising finance and depreciation costs from newly capitalised assets.
Jharkhand MoU (2.5-2.7 MT blast furnace) conditional on iron ore block allocation; no investment committed.
Senior management turnover, with eight new senior appointments.
532286|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term value-engineering strategy and team quality, but cautious and hedged on near-term pricing, coal and monsoon-related timing. Several answers were deflected or qualified (for example, on cost savings quantification and slurry timing), and management repeatedly stressed uncontrollable input costs.
key_quotes: We are not going to burden our balance sheet with the borrowings. We do not want to take loans; we do not want to borrow the funds to expand in the commodity area.
Our first and foremost focus is that we should reach to the 100% capacity utilization.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 2,667 crores. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA per ton increased by INR 1,843 per ton, taking it to INR 11,937 per ton.
we remain confident of achieving the ratio below our stated threshold of 1.5x during Q2FY27

financial_highlights.change: Per ton up INR 1,843 to INR 11,937/ton
Increase on capitalisation of major expansion assets in Q4FY26
Stronger steel prices and richer mix

rows.why: Shutdown ends so operating leverage (about INR 2,000/ton in Q1) reverses and slurry pipeline adds about INR 700/ton from Q2, with a cost reduction target of at least INR 1,000/ton, offset by coking coal up a further $12-15/ton and TMT prices down about INR 8,000 per index.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: FY27 volume guidance of 10.5-11 MT is held, which needs about 300,000 t of lost hot metal recovered after a 15% QoQ volume drop in Q1 and a 6% QoQ fall in Indian crude steel output.

rows.why: FY27 capex is held at about INR 8,500 crore with only about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1, and management says growth will be funded from earnings with no commodity capacity additions and no new borrowing; Jharkhand 2.5-2.7 MT blast furnace MoU is conditional with nothing committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident only on net debt/EBITDA below 1.5x in Q2 FY27 (from 1.71x) and kept volume guidance unchanged, while cutting its price outlook for TMT and HRC by INR 800-8,000/ton.

rows.why: TMT prices are down about INR 8,000 per index and HRC about INR 800/ton versus the Q1 average, coking coal is set to rise a further $12-15/ton, and the slurry pipeline could slip beyond August.

rows.why: Net debt is INR 15,927 crore against 1.71x leverage in Q1, and management says it is confident of getting below 1.5x in Q2 FY27, which needs a quarter of recovered volume and EBITDA.

rows.why: Q1 volume fell about 15% QoQ on the BOF refractory shutdown, about 300,000 t of hot metal is to be recovered, and operating leverage of about INR 2,000/ton does not repeat in Q2.

rows.label: Post-monsoon construction demand recovery
rows.why: Management expects construction to recover after the monsoon, but TMT prices are down about INR 8,000 per index in recent weeks and HRC imports via advance licences are pressuring flats.

532286|2026-09.headline: Jindal Steel posted record Q2 FY27 gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore (+44% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR 2,504 crore (+34% YoY) on 2.38 MT sales.
532286|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore and record sales volume of 2.38 million tons, with domestic sales about 92% of volume. Adjusted EBITDA rose 34% YoY to INR 2,504 crore, but adjusted EBITDA per ton of INR 10,529 was sequentially lower on higher raw material, power, fuel and freight costs. Net debt fell to INR 14,786 crore and net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.51x from 1.71x. Management guided to 11 MT gross steel output in FY27 with H2 net steel of about 6 MT, and said the switch from propane to coal-gas syngas protected productivity during the West Asia supply disruption.

financial_highlights.change: down INR 1,141 crore from INR 15,927 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,228 crore in Q2; INR 3,187 crore in H1

financial_highlights.change: apples-to-apples basis; management says over 65% when excluding low-priced TMT

segments.name: Flat products (HRC and plates)
segments.commentary: Plates production exceeds 220,000 tons per month across both locations; management targets a 65:35 flat-to-long mix, up from about 60:40 currently. Hot-rolled coil output is being shifted to value-added grades such as high and medium carbon.

segments.name: TMT / long products
segments.commentary: TMT output was cut to about 120,000 tons per month from 220,000 tons earlier, with volume redirected to plates and HRC. TMT now goes mainly to major projects.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports run at about 100,000 tons per month, mainly HRC, plates, with some rails and structurals.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Pellet output is about 33,000 tons per day (Barbil 18,000-20,000 and Angul 14,000), all consumed in-house. A new pellet plant is targeted for commercial production by June 2027.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: JSOL (100% subsidiary) turnover and EBITDA are rising as major projects commission; Mozambique coal EBITDA improved YoY on better coal prices.

guidance_outlook: Net steel production target of about 6 MT in H2 FY27 (about 3 MT per quarter, planned at 0.96 MT per month); gross steel about 11 MT for FY27.
Record production expected in Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), with Q4 to exceed Q3.
FY27 sales volume guidance lower end of about 10.5 MT; management says 9-9.5 lakh saleable tons per month is needed and that they are comfortable.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20-25/ton expected for Q3; a possible further USD 20/ton from diesel and oil if the West Asia conflict prolongs.
Slurry pipeline (192 km, Barbil to Angul) commissioned; commercial supply from about 2-3 days from 23 Oct, saving about INR 700/ton on freight at 20,000 tons per day.
Blast furnace at Angul (about 10,000 tons per day) to ramp to 10,500 in about 7 days, 11,000 in November and 12,000 in December.
Coal gasifier expansion (3 more gasifiers, 35,000 NM3/hr each) and DRI-2 (2 MT) targeted for commissioning by June 2027.
Utkal B2 coal mine clearance expected in FY27; Roida iron ore mine restart expected by about December 2026 to January 2027.
Annual growth capex guided at INR 7,500-10,000 crore; net debt-to-EBITDA to stay below 1.5x through the cycle.
capex_capacity: Blast furnace at Angul ramping to about 10,000 tons per day, targeting 12,000 tons per day by December 2026.
Slurry pipeline: 192 km, commissioned, first iron slurry dispatched, continuous operation planned.
Captive coal mines: about 15 MT total capacity across Raigarh and Angul; captive coal meets about 50-55% of requirement, targeted at 65-70%. Gare Palma about 4 MT.
Kasia iron ore mine at 22,000 tons per day, ramping to 30,000 tons per day.
Coal gasification: 3 additional gasifiers (105,000 NM3/hr combined), over 95% indigenous content, commissioning by June 2027.
Total capex plan of about INR 47,000 crore with INR 8,000-9,000 crore remaining, including DRI-2 and performance-linked payments.
demand_pricing: Average HRC moved from INR 51,000 to INR 60,000/ton during Q2; TMT from INR 52,000 to INR 59,000/ton; structurals INR 60,000-65,000; rails above INR 70,000.
Spot prices around INR 60,000/ton for HRC and TMT as of late October.
Coking coal cost rose about USD 12-15/ton in Q2, within prior guidance; management says prices are stable now.
Propane to coal-gas switch saves about INR 70/kg in reheating furnaces (propane about INR 100/kg vs syngas about INR 30/kg). Management says the company will not revert to propane.
Q2 is seasonally weak for TMT; Q3 expected to be stronger on festive-season construction demand.
Europe steel deficit of about 28 MT cited; EU CBAM and quota remain open issues for exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4.8 MT H1 production run-rate achievable and will flat mix stay at 70:30 in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of about 3 MT per quarter; mix target is 65:35 flat to long, not 70:30, to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight saving does the slurry pipeline give, and any extra cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 700/ton on freight with no additional cost; around 500 of 700 daily iron ore trucks to be removed.

qa_highlights.question: Coking coal and West Asia cost impact for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal up USD 20-25/ton expected in Q3 by Sandeep Modi; West Asia impact on fuel about USD 4-5/ton, steady. Another USD 20/ton possible if conflict prolongs.

qa_highlights.question: Water availability from Brahmani for Angul at higher volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Only 31 MLD being used against 59.1 MLD sanctioned; usage to fall at least 15% next year as Barbil slurry supplies water.

qa_highlights.question: Power sales and their EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said power sales are miniscule relative to the INR 1 lakh crore revenue ambition; no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Pellet plant and merchant pellet sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No merchant pellet sales now; all 33,000 tons/day consumed in-house. New pellet plant commercial production by June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and spot price detail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined exact spot prices, citing policy; gave approximate ranges as above.

risks_watch: Coking coal and diesel cost pressure from the West Asia and Russia-Ukraine supply disruptions; management flagged possible USD 20-25/ton in Q3.
Execution on the Angul blast furnace ramp, Roida mine right-of-way, and Utkal B2 approvals.
Possible delays to DRI-2 and coal gasifiers, which management says could slip from June 2027 due to imported equipment.
Other expenses rose about 13% QoQ on freight and power/fuel; management expects normalisation in Q3.
Water availability at Angul given the Brahmani river reservoir level, though management says consumption will be lower.
EU quota and CBAM outcomes that determine export access.
