rows.why: Net steel H2 about 6 MT (about 3 MT per quarter at 0.96 MT/month) and Q3 record production expected with Q4 above Q3; saleable run-rate of 9-9.5 lakh tons/month needed, record Q2 volume of 2.38 MT.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management held annual growth capex at INR 7,500-10,000 crore and said total plan of about INR 47,000 crore has INR 8,000-9,000 crore remaining, so no new capex beyond the existing framework was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 sales volume is guided only to the lower end of about 10.5 MT and management held the 11 MT gross steel target rather than raising it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coking coal up USD 20-25/ton in Q3 with another USD 20/ton possible if West Asia conflict prolongs, plus DRI-2 and gasifier timing risk, against FY27 volume already at the lower end of 10.5 MT.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Mix shift to value-added grades (57% VAP, over 65% ex-low-priced TMT) and flat-to-long target of 65:35 from about 60:40, with HRC being shifted to high and medium carbon grades; TMT cut to about 120,000 tpm from 220,000.

rows.label: Slurry pipeline freight saving
rows.why: Commissioned with commercial supply from 23 Oct, saving about INR 700/ton on freight at 20,000 tpd, with about 500 of 700 daily iron ore trucks to be removed.

rows.label: Net debt-to-EBITDA below 1.5x
rows.why: Net debt fell INR 1,141 crore QoQ to INR 14,786 crore and leverage improved to 1.51x from 1.71x, with management guiding to stay below 1.5x through the cycle.

rows.label: HRC and TMT price strength
rows.why: HRC rose from INR 51,000 to INR 60,000/ton in Q2 and spot is about INR 60,000; Q3 is expected to be stronger for TMT, but management declined to give exact ASP and spot is not a locked-in call.

tone.note: Management was confident on the blast furnace ramp, slurry freight savings and the balance sheet, but cautious on coking coal cost headwinds and evasive on exact ASP, spot prices, power sales and subsidiary numbers; analysts pushed on the H1 run-rate, flat mix and water availability at Angul.

532300|2026-03.headline: Wockhardt FY26 revenue INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (~51% growth); Zaynich US FDA approval is the key catalyst, with peak sales guided at $1.5-2 billion globally.
532300|2026-03.overview: Management hosted an investor meet on 4 June 2026 (disclosed 11 June) after the US FDA approval of Zaynich (cefepime-zidebactam), described as the first Indian-discovered research product approved by the FDA. FY26 revenue was INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (margin about 18.6%, up from about 5.4% three years earlier) and profit before tax INR238 crore. Management framed the next phase as scaling growth: US launch of Zaynich via an operationally light model, India and emerging-market launches, and biosimilar diabetes expansion. Most numbers were given verbally; no quarterly figures or formal guidance were disclosed in the presentation.

segments.name: Pharma core (India, UK, Ireland)
segments.commentary: About 75% of business; UK is top-five with 18% covered-market share and focuses on specialty injectables. India driven by diabetes, orthopedics, pain and regenerative medicine (Emrok, Miqnaf).

segments.name: Biosimilars / biotech (diabetes)
segments.commentary: Grew 27% in FY26; human insulin output scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x. Two products commercialised, five in pipeline (aspart, RN 30/70, degludec, degludec aspart, semaglutide); registered in 30 emerging markets.

segments.name: Novel antibiotics (Zaynich, Emrok, Miqnaf, Odrate)
segments.commentary: Specialty (biosimilars plus novel antibiotics) is 23% of business. Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO India approvals; US launch planned with leadership hired and a commercial operating partner; European approval expected by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: 28% of turnover, growing 35%, supported by partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia. Plans to launch Zaynich in seven to eight high-carbapenem-resistance markets within 18 to 24 months.

guidance_outlook: Zaynich global peak sales of $1.5-2 billion per year, with US roughly 40% of global revenue; country-wise split not given.
Revenue ramp expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick pattern), with breakeven in 12 to 18 months in the Zaynich business; first 12-18 months may see a slight loss, per the Chairman.
Zaynich US price expected at roughly $1,200-1,500 per day, with India pricing about 75-80% below US; Europe and US pricing described as price-neutral versus existing antibiotics.
Long-term target of about 20-25% share of resistant cases globally; India possibly higher.
Biosimilar business expected to double in 24-36 months; capacity to double in 12-15 months; five pipeline products to launch about two years out.
Capex of INR200-300 crore over next three years, primarily for biologicals capacity; R&D spend to stay at similar percentage of sales.
Foviscu DCGI filing expected in two to three months; approval timing not predictable. Odrate is about four years away and Phase 2 waiver not expected.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of INR200-300 crore over the next three years, mainly for biologicals capacity.
Biosimilar capacity to double within 12-15 months.

Zaynich manufacturing: US supply from an FDA-approved European site; India supply from Indian facility; emerging markets to be supplied from either India or Europe depending on timelines (Europe could save six to nine months).
Company has 11 manufacturing facilities and two R&D centres in-house.
Management said US, Europe and emerging markets filings are submitted or in progress, with European approval expected by end of 2026.
demand_pricing: US cUTI is the largest of about 1.2 million US gram-negative hospital infections (about 600,000 cUTI cases); management cited about 20-25% readmission rate for cUTI.
India: about 600,000-700,000 gram-negative infection patients, with 35-45% estimated carbapenem resistance (ICMR surveillance caveated by regional variation).
Phase 3 vs meropenem: composite cure rate 96.8%, about 20% higher than meropenem per management.
Management said new anti-infectives in the US market total about $1 billion; the company does not plan to create new demand but to take share, with price neutrality.
Competition: cefiderocol (Fetroja) cited as the closest competitor; management claimed Zaynich has a better efficacy and safety profile, without numerical head-to-head data.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from Zaynich over the next 6 to 24 months, and capex and commercial costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman expects slow initial revenue growth, a hockey-stick curve after 12-18 months, INR200-300 crore capex over three years, and no capex for sales build-out, only revenue cost. Breakeven expected in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Does Zaynich qualify for the 10% PLI and what is the China strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Government funding recognised but immaterial versus R&D spend. China: Chinese patients in trial were insufficient; a small China study is ongoing and a partner may be sought.

qa_highlights.question: Will Zaynich be made in Europe for the US and in India for emerging markets?
qa_highlights.answer: US supply from an FDA-inspected European site as a de-risking step; India supply from India; emerging markets from India or Europe depending on timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Wockhardt exit US generics and will it re-enter?
qa_highlights.answer: US generics were about 5% of the portfolio and loss-making, amid the 2012-13 FDA import alert. Management said it is re-entering with innovative products sourced from European manufacturers, with India production for India.

qa_highlights.question: Patent life and exclusivity for Zaynich, Emrok and Miqnaf?
qa_highlights.answer: Zaynich patent runs to 2038 in India with further filings planned; Miqnaf patent to early 2033 in India. QIDP status gives five extra years in US; minimum 10-year market exclusivity in US and Western markets.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and patient targets for FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: US price about $1,200-1,500 per day, typically $10,000-15,000 per course; India priced about 75-80% below US. Long-term share of 20-25% of resistant cases, with no FY28-29 patient numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Peak sales of Zaynich?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $1.5-2 billion per year globally at peak, not cumulative, with US around 40% of global revenue.

risks_watch: Commercial execution: a new US sales model for antibiotics with a commercial operating partner, 6,000 US hospitals to segment, and a first-time anti-infective launch for the company.
Losses or breakeven in the first 12-18 months from US launch costs; Chairman's comments on profitability were clarified as Zaynich-only.
Regulatory timing: European approval expected by end-2026, emerging market filings to follow; DCGI approval for Foviscu not predictable.
Label scope: US approval is for cUTI; HAP/VAP and other indications need a further trial, so off-label use is a question.
Zaynich Phase 2 waiver for the aztreonam combination (Odrate) not expected; Odrate timing about four years.
Hospital segment profitability and ROCE targets were not answered (hospitals deemed out of scope; ROCE question deflected).
532300|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on Zaynich and the R&D pipeline, with forward-looking claims (peak sales, market share) given without detailed assumptions. Evasive or deflective on ROCE, hospitals, Foviscu timing and China specifics, and on country-wise revenue split.
key_quotes: Wockhardt, as you know, in the last few days, is now the first Indian company to have an Indian research product approved with the US FDA, Zaynich.
So, it is in your financial terms you say investment, I mean, asset-light and capital-heavy.
We will stick to only antibiotic research for next 10 years.
Peak sales per year.

financial_highlights.change: about 35% in last year per Q&A

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides a Zaynich launch that is a slight loss for the first 12-18 months, with bottom-line breakeven in 12-18 months, so launch costs weigh on margins even though FY26 EBITDA margin was about 18.6% (up from about 5.4% three years ago).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management guided biosimilar capacity to double within 12-15 months, with human insulin output already scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x, backed by INR200-300 crore capex over three years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Biosimilar and biotech grew 27% in FY26 and emerging markets (28% of turnover) are growing 35%, with Zaynich US launch planned, though Zaynich revenue ramp is expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick after 12-18 months).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR200-300 crore over three years, mainly biologicals, is already firmly planned; utilisation was not disclosed, so further capex beyond this is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or margin guidance for FY27 was given, and the Zaynich peak sales of $1.5-2 billion are long-dated, so an upgrade depends on early US launch traction that has not yet been reported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution risk is high: first-time anti-infective launch in the US via a commercial partner, a 6,000-hospital segmentation task, Foviscu DCGI timing not predictable, and an expected Zaynich loss in the first 12-18 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Zaynich US launch now; European approval by end-2026; five b
rows.why: Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO approvals with leadership hired and a commercial partner in place; European approval is expected by end of calendar 2026, and emerging-market launches in seven to eight markets are planned within 18-24 months.

rows.label: Zaynich emerging-market launches in 7-8 high-CRE markets
rows.why: Management plans launches in seven to eight high carbapenem-resistance markets, with emerging markets already 28% of turnover growing 35% and partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia.

rows.label: Biosimilar business doubling
rows.why: Management expects the biosimilar business to double in 24-36 months after growing 27% in FY26, with 2 products commercialised and 5 in the pipeline registered in 30 emerging markets.

rows.label: Foviscu DCGI approval
rows.when: filing in 2-3 months; approval timing unpredictable
rows.why: Filing is expected in two to three months, but management would not predict approval timing, so this is a binary timing risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on Zaynich peak sales of $1.5-2 billion, the biosimilar doubling and the 20-25% resistant-case share, but was evasive on ROCE, hospitals, Foviscu timing, China and the country-wise revenue split, while analysts pressed on Zaynich revenue, losses and capex.

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the CDMO contribution in Q1 and what growth to expect from the Viatris partnership over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Aggarwal said Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) booked only about ₹5-6 crore in Q1, with growth reflecting in Q2 and Q3. He said about ₹100-130 crore is expected from these two products, not the full ₹200 crore in year one, and that it would build over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: What are export margins for CDMO and own-brands, and how will the ₹250 crore cash and Synthimed stake be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gross margin is about 55%. The ₹250 crore cash will be deployed as capex over about 2.5 years (warehouse, existing capacity, Jammu). No plans to divest the Synthimed stake this year; Synthimed budgeted EBITDA is about ₹750 crore and Q1 results are on track.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18% EBITDA margin sustainable, and could it rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18% is fully sustainable and could reach 21-22% if sales grow quarter on quarter. It denied calling Q1 a turnaround, citing litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business for about 1.5 years that are now over.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY29 revenue guidance of ₹1200 crore not being raised, and when does growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not revise at this stage and will revisit by year-end. Growth is H2-weighted via Arrotex Macrogol in Q2 and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4. FY27 expectation is about ₹900 crore, with export sales of about ₹750 crore, roughly 45% from CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the API business sold and what R&D capability was retained?
qa_highlights.answer: The API business was sold to Synthimed in FY24 for net about ₹2000-2100 crore, used to repay group debt of about ₹1250-1300 crore. Retained R&D in Panchkula handles regulatory compliance, tech transfer and global filings, with new land bought for a further R&D facility.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and will there be a capacity shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen and granules ran at about 70% in Q1 on pilot batches. Management expects 90% utilisation of the FY29 plan over time and sees no capacity dearth. Capex for new molecules will follow only after filings are complete.

risks_watch: CDMO ramp-up timing: Viatris volumes are guided to double in Q2 from a ₹5-6 crore base, and Arrotex Macrogol and Ibuprofen and granules contributions depend on Q2-Q4 execution.
Margin trajectory: management targets above 20% EBITDA margin from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally), against 17.91% in Q1; a shortfall would challenge the 21-22% view.
Capacity and capex: ₹250 crore capex over about 2-2.5 years, Jammu and Samba EU-GMP/PIC/S audits in progress, and the new CDMO deal needs ₹50-75 crore capex; delays could cap FY28-29 revenue.
Revenue guidance: FY27 about ₹900 crore and FY29 ₹1200 crore; management says it will revisit by year-end, so the next quarter's run-rate matters.
Synthimed stake: ~7.8% holding, no divestment planned this year, tag-along right on any PE exit; monetisation timing is open.
Customer concentration and unnamed partners: two new overseas CDMO deals and 3-4 existing customers are under discussion but not named; 'the war' is cited as slowing signings.
Several questions were deferred (market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, new registrations, packaging differentiation), so follow-ups via IR are pending.
key_quotes: Yes, yes, 18% is fully sustainable and we plan if the sales we are able to increase quarter-on-quarter they might go up to 21 to 22%.
Sir, not at this stage. Maybe after if we are able to achieve our, overachieve our results this financial year, we may revise this.
So that ₹250 crores will be deployed in capex over a period of 2.5 years approx.
We don't want to spend a single penny in R&D before we sign off any agreement with our customers.
532305|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and the export mix, stating 18% EBITDA margin is fully sustainable and describing the quarter as an excellent start. Cautious on guidance, declining to revise the ₹1200 crore FY29 target and avoiding firm commitments on the 20% margin timing, the new partnerships and the CDMO revenue split. Evasive on several detailed questions, including market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, partner names and new registrations, which were deferred to follow-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin 17.91% (up from 5.33%) with own-brand exports at 57.20% of sales vs 48%, export gross margin ~55%, and management guiding above 20% from Q3 FY27 and 21-22% if sales grow sequentially; not yet proven and Q1 margin was helped by exit of litigation and other costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About ₹250 cr capex over 2-2.5 years for new warehouse, existing-facility capacity enhancement and Jammu, plus a ₹50-75 cr capex for a potential new CDMO deal, but the capacity additions are not dated to a specific quarter and utilisation is only ~70%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to ~₹900 cr and export sales ~₹750 cr (~45% CDMO), with Viatris volumes guided to double in Q2 from a ₹5-6 cr base and Arrotex Macrogol in Q2, but Q1 CDMO contribution was small and FY27 implies a step-up from ₹186 cr in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex already raised to ~₹250 cr and a ₹50-75 cr CDMO-specific capex is pending a new customer deal, but Ibuprofen/granules utilisation is ~70% and management said no capacity dearth, so a fresh board-level capex is conditional on signing new deals.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to revise FY29 ₹1200 cr target and will revisit only by year-end; the CDMO revenue split and partner signings are still unconfirmed, with only ₹5-6 cr CDMO booked in Q1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CDMO ramp is back-end loaded (Ibuprofen/Clarithromycin in Q3-Q4, ~₹100-130 cr from Viatris over two years vs ₹200 cr year-one expectation) and 'the war' is cited as slowing new signings, so FY27 ₹900 cr could slip if Q2-Q3 run-rate lags.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Arrotex Macrogol push in Q2, Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4, and 5-6 R&D molecules for FY27-29 (Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin, Empagliflozin candidates) with dossiers rising from 2,100 to ~2,500 by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Viatris CDMO volume doubling in Q2
rows.why: Viatris volumes guided to double in Q2 from ₹5-6 cr booked in Q1, with Viatris CDMO expected to contribute ~₹100-130 cr over about two years.

rows.label: New overseas CDMO partnerships
rows.when: not expected to contribute this year
rows.why: Two new overseas CDMO deals and partnerships with 3-4 existing customers are under discussion, unnamed, and management said they are not expected to contribute this year.

rows.label: Synthimed stake monetisation
rows.why: Stake ~7.8%; management said no divestment planned this year, though tag-along right exists on any PE exit and Synthimed budgeted EBITDA ~₹750 cr.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 18% margin being sustainable and on the export mix, but cautious on guidance: it declined to revise the ₹1200 cr FY29 target, gave no firm date on the 20% margin, and deferred questions on market size, Q1 utilisation, partner names and registrations; analysts pushed o

532309|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PBT from continuing operations hit INR 119 crore, but one-offs (incl. ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal) drove much of it; underlying FY26 EBITDA margin 11%.
532309|2026-03.overview: GE Power India reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 316 crore (up from INR 266 crore YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR 1,269 crore (up 21%), led by Core Services (+14%) and Upgrades (+24%). Profit before tax and exceptional items from continuing operations was INR 119 crore in Q4 versus a loss of INR 15 crore a year earlier, and INR 340 crore for FY26 versus INR 22 crore, with management flagging sizeable one-offs in both periods. Order intake fell sharply to INR 877 crore for FY26 from INR 2,183 crore, and order backlog declined to INR 1,628 crore from INR 2,662 crore, mainly due to termination of FGD-EP contracts. Management is pushing a service-led, short-cycle strategy, has settled with BHEL and Jaypee, and has signed a Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy, with a recommended dividend of INR 7 per share (70% of face value).

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% YoY and core orders rose 32% YoY; Core Services order backlog up about 40% YoY. Management says about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book executes in FY27 (12-month cycles).

segments.name: Upgrades
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by upgrade volumes in Q4; Vindhyachal and Wanakbori complex upgrade orders of INR 591 crore were booked in FY25.

segments.name: New Build / FGD EPC (AQCS)
segments.commentary: In close-out mode; FGD-EP contracts of Jaypee Bina and Nigrie (INR 775 crore) were terminated, driving backlog decline. Seven operational acceptances and four unit completions achieved in FY26.

segments.name: Durgapur manufacturing (discontinued)
segments.commentary: Being demerged to JSW Energy; asset of about 660 acres, reported losses in recent quarters. Five-year JSW supply and capacity agreement signed to protect core services manufacturing needs.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give numeric FY27 guidance; CFO said the FY26 underlying EBITDA base (11%) is set and FY27 margins should be at par or better, without a range.
About 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book (INR 1,628 crore) expected to execute in FY27, implying roughly INR 1,380-1,470 crore; this is a management estimate from the call, not formal guidance.
Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy: filed with NCLT; target completion in calendar 2026, and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026 at the latest.
Core Services target addressable fleet of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore; company holds about 18% share and aims to grow it before considering other areas.
Management says the ECL impact from the BHEL settlement is fully recognised as of 31 Mar 2026, so no similar reversal is expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Durgapur manufacturing facility to be demerged to JSW Energy; a five-year agreement with JSW covers reserved manufacturing capacity and supply for core services boiler components.
Management aims to build an alternate supply chain for boiler components within about 18 months to become independent of JSW after the five-year agreement.
Three PG tests completed for key new-build units and multiple synchronisations and facility closures achieved in FY26.
Eighteen new first-of-its-kind service products ordered during FY26; first-time generator repairs, turbine upgrades and control system solutions delivered.
demand_pricing: Management says thermal plant PLF and availability are rising, increasing services demand; target addressable market quoted at INR 3,500-4,000 crore.
Q4 order intake of INR 254 crore was below the prior-year INR 285 crore (which included INR 52 crore O&M); FY26 orders fell 60% YoY on the FY25 FGD-EP and complex upgrade wins.

FGD mandate: per the July 2025 notification, Category C plants (over 200 GW) were removed and Category A (about 8 GW, mainly Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra) must install FGD; Category B is optional with no tariff pass-through if they opt in. Management says the mandate has limited near-term order impact.
Management is pursuing 13 countries for boilers, including Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Indonesia, while stating its perimeter remains India-only for GEPIL and non-GEPIL assets.

qa_highlights.question: Does GEPIL participate in gas turbine, HRSG or combined-cycle business?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said no; HRSG and gas-plant business belong to GE Vernova's gas business and fall outside GEPIL's objects, which are steam and thermal only.

qa_highlights.question: Of the order book, how much is executable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aashish Ghai said short-cycle orders typically complete within 12 months, so about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book is expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will backlog grow after the current book runs off, and is the business widening beyond core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is new-build close-out. Core backlog is up about 40% YoY; the company plans to grow its 18% share of the INR 3,500-4,000 crore fleet before expanding to other areas.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 450 crore loan and what yield does it earn?

qa_highlights.question: Where are supply-chain constraints (raw materials, labour, rare earths) and channel stock?

qa_highlights.question: Why is management cautious for the next two quarters, and what are the risks to demand?

532343|2026-06.headline: TVS Motor Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% to INR 13,896 crore and operating EBITDA rose 41% to INR 1,779 crore, with margin at 12.8%.

Operating EBITDA margin expanded 30 bps to 12.8%, helped by price increases and cost actions despite a sharp commodity spike linked to the West Asia conflict. International sales hit a record 4.68 lakh units (+33%), and EV sales grew 86%. Management guided Q2 as better than Q1 and expects FY27 industry growth in double digits, with capacity expansion to 8.3 million 2W units by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is TVS gaining share against a competitor discounting in scooters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a broad scooter range, frequent feature upgrades, durability and JD Power rankings. It said dealer stock is kept below 30 days and that retail financing supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commodity headwind and how much has been passed on?

qa_highlights.question: Is EV profitability improving?

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall capacity and investment plan?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Norton strategy, investment and volume ambition?

532343|2026-09.headline: TVS Motor Q2 FY27 revenue rose 44% to INR17,103 crores and PAT 52% to INR1,377 crores, alongside approval of a consumer finance demerger.
532343|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record volume (1.9 million units, up 27%), revenue, EBITDA and profit, with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 13.0%. Management said domestic 2W ICE and EV and 3W all grew faster than industry, and international sales hit a record 5.39 lakh units (up 35%). The Board approved a demerger of the consumer finance and related undertaking (including the TVS Credit Services stake) into a separate listed holding company, with shareholders receiving mirror shareholding; completion is expected around July 2027 appointed date after 8 to 10 months of approvals. Management guided to single-digit industry growth in H2 with base effects, and cost pressure expected to ease in Q3 and Q4.

segments.commentary: ICE plus EV 3W volume about 26,300 units, up 65% from 16,000 vs industry 23%. EV penetration of 3W about 44% in Q2 and about 48% in September.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record 5.39 lakh units in H1, up 35% YoY; Q2 international 2W ICE up 33% vs industry 27%. International EV sales about 6,930 units in Q2 vs 1,726 last year. Africa was the key driver.

segments.name: TVS Credit (consumer finance)
segments.commentary: Book size INR33,818 crores, up 22% from INR27,807 crores; PBT INR330 crores, up 19% from INR277 crores. Network over 65,000 touch points; 14 lakh new customers in the quarter; customer base about 2.7 crores.

segments.name: Norton (e-bike)
segments.commentary: Manx R and Atlas launches under way in Europe (dealers in UK, Italy, France; Germany and Spain coming); India launch expected in coming months; US preparations underway. Current-quarter e-bike loss is lower than the prior quarter, though brand and launch costs rose.

qa_highlights.answer: EV industry grew about 75% in H1; capacity now 60,000-65,000 units/month, with 80,000 planned. Ronin is expected to go beyond 15,000 units per month, with new variants and a large capacity investment under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structure of the consumer finance demerger and what holdings will TVS Motor keep?
qa_highlights.answer: Demerged undertaking includes the TVS Credit Services investment and some non-core investments, moved to a new company with mirror shareholding. TVS Motor keeps no stake; the TVS Credit business is not being merged into the new entity.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the demerger listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Post shareholder approval and NCLT process, around 8 to 10 months. The appointed date is July 2027, after the NBFC consolidation mandated by RBI (approvals expected by March or April 2027).

qa_highlights.question: What is the valuation and net worth of TVS Credit?
qa_highlights.answer: No valuation is set in a demerger. Net worth is about INR6,500 crores before the proposed INR1,200 crore equity infusion. Management declined to give ROE and ROA figures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for industry growth in H2 and pricing?

qa_highlights.question: Are EV e-bike losses coming down outside Norton?

532348|2026-03.headline: Subex Q4 FY26 revenue rose 3% QoQ to INR 72.96 crores, with EBITDA margin at 14.5% and FY26 order intake up 24%.
532348|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 72.96 crores versus INR 70.79 crores in Q3, with EBITDA of INR 10.58 crores (14.5% margin) and normalized PAT of INR 11.51 crores. Management said FY26 full-year total income grew 6% YoY, partly supported by interest income, and that FY25 is not like-for-like because non-core businesses were exited. Order intake grew 24% in FY26 and management highlighted AI deal wins, though it acknowledged top-line growth lagged its ambitions. Middle East exposure, the geopolitical backdrop and slow new-purchase decisions were flagged as the main near-term risks, with revenue conversion expected to improve as implementations finish.

segments.commentary: Management indicated license gross margin is near 90-100%, implementation gross margin 40-45% (up to 60% depending on complexity), MS above 50% and AMC above 70%. These are gross margins before R&D, GTM, G&A and lease costs.

segments.name: Products
segments.commentary: Four core products: Revenue Assurance, Fraud Management, Partner Settlement (wholesale billing) and Enterprise Asset Management. FraudZap is the newer AI fraud product, with one paid customer that onboarded three Telcos through an intermediary.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Management said about 31% of revenue comes from the Gulf region, and that APAC and Europe are steady. Africa is seeing momentum and the Americas will get heavy investment in FY27.

Management expects revenue conversion to improve quarter by quarter as implementations of FY26 wins finish, with an uptick expected around the middle of FY27 if there are no delays.
INR 100 crores per quarter revenue was described internally as a target ('war cry'), with no timeline committed.
Management plans to pursue tuck-in acquisitions in FY27, which the board is actively discussing.
Management said the goodwill impairment test is complete and auditors found no impairment needed on carrying value of about INR 190 crores.

Management is working on running agents on CPU or a laptop-sized 'agent in a box' to get around the GPU constraint; it said it is also looking at neuromorphic hardware.
GenAI-based software development is being embedded across the MCLC to lift developer productivity and reduce engineering cost.

532356|2026-03.headline: Triveni FY26 revenue rose 10.6% to ₹6,291 crore and PBT reached ₹378 crore, while Q4 revenue dipped on PTB order slippage.

The distillery segment staged a sharp turnaround on record volumes and lower maize costs, while sugar crush fell 8.8% to 8.25 million tonnes. segments.commentary: Record production and sales volumes with FY26 revenue net of excise of ₹1,550 crore. Realisation averaged ₹61/litre (lower due to FCI rice mix), and grain made up 56% of ethanol sales (maize about 33%). Management said conversion and raw-material costs fell significantly.

532388|2026-03.headline: IOB posted FY26 net profit of about Rs 5,208 crore (up 56.16%) and advances growth of 24.16%, with GNPA down to 1.42%.
532388|2026-03.overview: Indian Overseas Bank reported a strong Q4 FY26 and full-year FY26, with total business up 20.76% to Rs 6,78,614 crore and advances up 24.16% to Rs 3,10,423 crore. Net profit rose 56.16% to about Rs 5,208 crore, ROA reached 1.23% and ROE 20.42%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.42% and NNPA at 0.21%. Management guided to 14-16% industry credit growth, flagged ECL front-loading of about Rs 3,000 crore (Rs 1,750 crore already provided), and said it sees no West Asia stress so far.

532395|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue grew 12.4% to 1,159 crores and EBITDA rose 24.6% to 178 crores, but reported PAT fell 4.3% to 72 crores after a 142 crore Q4 revenue deferment.
532395|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a strong operating year with a Q4 shortfall: reported Q4 revenue was 273 crores, EBITDA 34 crores and PAT 0.4 crores. The shortfall was attributed to a 142 crore Q4 revenue recognition deferment (EBITDA impact above 40 crores), 11.17 crores of exceptional items linked to the divestment, and a higher tax charge versus FY25. Management signed a definitive agreement on May 26, 2026 to sell the heavy engineering, energy and automotive practice to Akkodis for USD 30.63 million, with closure expected in Q2 FY27. FY27 consolidated revenue is guided at about 1,377 crores (52% growth on the retained base), and the company reiterated its 9,000 crore FY30 revenue target.

Defense pipeline includes large programs such as swarm drones and CLRTS; company says it is shortlisted for most of them.
ESAI/Xida: 3.5 million dollar order from Qualcomm; management sees a 10x revenue possibility in data centres and test equipment for hyperscalers and semiconductor firms.

Make in India policy shifts have required changes to some OEM proposals; all such items subject to government approval.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9,000 crore FY30 revenue target (about 10x from FY26) still achievable organically?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said moving from design-based revenue to design-cum-manufacturing drives a 10x to 20x uplift, and it is holding the 9,000 crore target, with momentum expected once Devanahalli and Hyderabad are ready.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins reach 20%+ in FY27, and what is the post-FY27 order book and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-core verticals were margin-dilutive and targeted 150 to 200 bps YoY margin improvement in core verticals, which already average 20%+; no specific post-FY27 order book figure was given beyond pipeline comments.

qa_highlights.question: Will the engineering business transfer immediately, and is the FY30 PAT target the full potential?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a slump sale to the Akkodis India entity with people and contracts transferred and one year of handholding; guaranteed consideration of USD 23.4 million plus an earnout of USD 7.4 million tied to FY27 targets.

qa_highlights.question: How is expansion funded beyond Akkodis cash, and is equity dilution planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 disinvestment is expected to fully fund DAC, DAL, MAC and acquisitions; management said there are no plans for equity dilution or incremental long-term debt.

qa_highlights.question: Does reaching 9,000 crores by FY30 imply about 90% CAGR from FY28, and could higher margins lift PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should saturate around 25-27% and revenue would scale through serial production; acquisitions buy roughly two to three years to obtain certifications and manufacturing skills.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total capex programme?
qa_highlights.answer: DAC 1,200 crores, MAC 300 crores, DAL 120 crores, and acquisitions about 600 crores, for a total of 2,100 to 2,250 crores, described as self-funded.

Closure of the Akkodis divestment (Q2 FY27) and the expected 175 crore extraordinary gain; the gain drives the ESOP provisioning plan.
Execution risk on acquisitions (about 600 crores, four companies planned), government approvals, and the Make in India policy shift affecting OEM proposals.
Supply chain dependence on single or monopolistic hardware suppliers, which caused the Q4 deferment.

532395|2026-06.headline: Axiscades Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 42% YoY to ₹346 crore, but reported PAT loss of ₹14.8 crore; normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore.
532395|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter of the divestment-led transition: Engineering Services is shown as discontinued operations (₹163 crore revenue), leaving continuing operations at ₹183 crore, up 94% YoY. Reported EBITDA for the combined business was ₹27.9 crore, with one-offs of ₹13.1 crore (including ₹9.62 crore receivable provision on an aged defence transaction and ₹3.5 crore hedge provision) and ₹21.81 crore divestment transaction cost below EBITDA. Management says normalized EBITDA was ₹41 crore (11.8% margin) and normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore. Guidance was reaffirmed: FY27 continuing revenue of ₹1,377 crore, EBITDA of ₹270 crore and PAT of about 50% of that, with acquisitions and divestment proceeds central to delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Why divest the profitable aerospace services business when the company wants to build aerospace manufacturing, and could both have been done together?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to shift from services to product and solutions, citing OEM consolidation in services and a sale price that let proceeds fund Power 930 without equity dilution. KP Mohanakrishnan conceded doing both together was hypothetically possible but said the strategy chose product-based growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the Rs 10 crore receivable provision, Rs 3.5 crore hedge provision and Rs 22 crore deal cost booked?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shashidhar SK said the ~Rs 21 crore transaction cost sits in discontinued operations as an exceptional item, visible in the notes. The hedge unwinding of Rs 3.5 crore sits in continuing other expenses. Provisions of about Rs 6.5 crore (Ministry of Defence order) and Rs 3.14 crore (a defence PSU) were also cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalized PAT outlook for FY27 on Rs 1,377 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukund Santhanam reiterated FY27 EBITDA of Rs 270 crore and PAT broadly around 50% of that, about Rs 135 crore, possibly higher as divestment proceeds pay down debt and cut interest. He confirmed the analyst's view that Q2-Q4 would ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Status and timing of acquisitions, and what happens in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Two acquisitions (aerospace AS9100 manufacturer, XiDA business transfer) are targeted to close this quarter, with a third aerospace deal targeted by Q4. Management said most acquisitions will be in place by FY27-end and later ones will be smaller in scale than this year's.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Rs 4,557 crore defence assured visibility take to execute, and what is the wider pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharadhi Babu said the visibility is to be covered before FY30, about 3 years, with possible spillover into a fourth year. The total pipeline is about Rs 24,000 crore across unmanned systems, missiles, radar and DEW. Management also reiterated 75%+ defence growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Power 930 target (FY30 PAT Rs 960 crore) still intact, and is the acquisition-led plan at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukund Santhanam said the Power 930 targets remain firm, with FY30 PAT of Rs 960 crore. He acknowledged acquisitions are binary, saying aerospace and XiDA are at advanced stages while other deals are still at non-binding offer stage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the year-wise CapEx plans and how will they be funded before divestment proceeds arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give year-wise CapEx, saying spend will be timed to inflows (Q2 and Q3 FY27, then FY28 and FY29) and to partner readiness. A short-term bridge facility will fund the gap, with actual drawdown not more than Rs 100-150 crore. Shashidhar SK also said Rs 200+ crore of gain is expected in Q2 and the bulk in early Q3.

Management guided to margin pressure in Q1 and likely Q2 FY27 from crude-linked and palm oil input inflation of roughly 7-9%, offset by price hikes and share gains.

532424|2026-06.headline: GCPL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY on 9% underlying volume growth, EBITDA up 14% with 19% margin; India gross margin hit by war-linked input costs.
532424|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY with underlying volume growth of 9%, EBITDA rose 14% at a 19% margin, and net profit grew 11%. India gross margin fell sharply as LPG, kerosene and LABSA roughly trebled during the war-driven spike, with India cost impact near 6% over plan. Africa (GAUM) delivered an exceptional quarter with constant-currency growth around 25% and EBITDA margins moving to mid-teens, while Indonesia returned to stable growth at about 10%. Management says it is on track for full-year guidance and expects to exceed it on revenue, and possibly on EBITDA and volume.

segments.name: India Household Insecticides (HI)
segments.commentary: Management says GCPL gained overall HI market share in Q1 FY27 for the first time in almost a decade, driven by incense sticks, not premium segments. June was very weak due to rain and poor fill rates; July first half also poor.

segments.commentary: Speedboats grew about 3% in Q1 per analyst calculation; salience about 15% and management expects roughly 100-150 bps rise per quarter. Air care in India hit by LPG-linked fill rate falls of 20-25%.

segments.name: Africa / GAUM
segments.commentary: Constant-currency growth about 25%, driven by FMCG (air care at double-digit market share in South Africa within six months of launch) and hair extensions cost improvements. FY26 growth split was about 50:50 FMCG and hair.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Growth about 10% on a slower base, step-up in air media, and early El Nino benefit; Stellar business growing faster.

segments.name: Soaps (India)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew positively in Q1; management expects early single-digit growth in Q2 and Q3, soap margins at normative levels.

segments.name: Muuchstac (acquired DTC brand)
segments.commentary: Growth of about 70-80% from acquisition run rate; EPS accretive from day one, profitable digital-first brand.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: Committed INR500 crore capital; additional INR200 crore rights commitment referenced by analyst. Product-market fit achieved in Tamil Nadu; expansion to rest of South India under way.

532424|2026-09.headline: GCPL Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY (15% constant currency) on 8% underlying volume growth; net profit up 14% to INR523 crore.
532424|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY (15% in constant currency) with 8% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 12% and net profit rose 14% to INR523 crore. Standalone sales grew 13% on 7% underlying volume growth, after an estimated 150 bps hit from trade inventory correction, which also mildly hit standalone EBITDA. GUAM (Africa) and Indonesia were the strongest international contributors, while input inflation was among the highest in many years and was offset by pricing, cost savings and A&P optimisation. Management held FY27 guidance of high single-digit standalone UVG and double-digit consolidated revenue and EBITDA growth, and said revenues are running ahead of plan.

segments.commentary: Value growth of 8%, with soaps stable despite significant price increases and grammage reduction against a favourable comparator. Premium liquids, Cinthol body wash, hair colour (share gains) and perfumes/deodorants (strong double-digit growth) contributed; volume growth lagged value growth.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Sales +20% with 8% underlying volume growth and EBITDA +12%, aided by El Nino-driven mosquito infestation tailwind; LPG prices doubled. Newer portfolio (LV, Pocket) sustained double-digit underlying volume growth.

Soaps category seeing trade inventory correction, price-volume recalibration and grammage cuts; detergents growth described as strong, with powder-to-liquid shift and formalisation benefit.

qa_highlights.answer: India CEO search is in a robust process, prioritising Godrej values and entrepreneurial mindset over speed. Godrej Spic is now national. Pet care is still in learning phase; management will give milestones next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Personal Care volume growth well below 8% value growth, and which parts are weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Soaps saw trade inventory correction (large SKUs typically build inventory) and price-volume recalibration after steep price increases; margins still below normative. Hair colour gained share strongly. Detergents growth is in line with trend.

qa_highlights.question: How should Q3/Q4 India margins and EBITDA be viewed given commodity lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation expected slightly higher in Q3 vs Q2. Company will focus on consolidated EBITDA YoY growth rather than margin, aiming to hold double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth; India may see some up-and-down quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are H2 volume risks from inflation or season in detergents and HI?
qa_highlights.answer: Detergents not impacted by inflation on volume; HI season looks fine as El Nino impact was mainly in H1. Management expects to sustain volume trend lines.

qa_highlights.question: Is the decline in India standalone A&P spend structural or cyclical?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: soaps and detergents category spend has fallen and the company is balancing spend to keep share of voice at target, while the rest of the portfolio gets higher reach at lower cost via media agency practices. Management gave roughly equal weight to the two factors.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are Indonesia and GUAM growth beyond this year, and what is GUAM's mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Indonesia: a few bps of this year's growth is attributed to better weather; management is building more growth flywheels and expects double-digit international volume growth. GUAM: growth is broad-based, from core hair and new categories like Mega Growth Mousse and Darling styling products; hair colour has grown double digit in volume for 7-8 quarters. No split of core vs new given.

532440|2026-03.headline: MPS FY26 revenue rose 5.7% to INR 768 crore and EBITDA 11.8% to INR 236 crore; FY27 EBITDA guided to comfortably exceed INR 300 crore.

Corporate Learning revenue fell 16.5% for the year but returned to positive year-on-year growth in Q4. The target path is 0.5% to 1% to 2% over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 1,500 crore FY28 revenue target still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is intact and in line of sight. FY27 INR 300 crore EBITDA is organic and excludes new acquisitions; any further M&A would sit on top. Tighter FY28 guidance to come at end-Q3 or Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions, and has Unbound been paid for?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbound is mostly fully paid, with only small closing amounts left. Pipeline is active, with a Western Higher Ed carve-out the most advanced. Management will disclose material deals in the ordinary course.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a margin in the 30%-35% range, with expansion as revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is Unbound's revenue and EBITDA, and how will it move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The 50-day consolidation gave INR 11-12 crore revenue at 18.5%-19% margin. Monthly run rate was USD 700,000-800,000. FY27 expected USD 750,000-950,000 per month, starting near 15% EBITDA margin and exiting at 25%-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Given AI disruption, what protects the business model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI compresses commoditised production work but raises demand for trusted AI in medicine, scholarly publishing and regulated learning. It sees agentic AI as a tailwind, with verification as the gating constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin dip and ex-AJE headcount rise, and what drives FY27 growth and the FY28 path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AJE headcount moved offshore to India while Research headcount rose ahead of expected growth, causing a timing-related ex-AJE margin softness in Q4. Growth drivers are the four Research product layers, Education, and the accessibility line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Corporate Learning investment shift, and why did clients rise while revenue per client fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Work has moved from compliance content to AI, AR/VR and simulation-led performance enablers. Unbound added a long tail of smaller institutional accounts, which lowered average revenue per client without any anchor client billing less.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA split and main risk to the INR 300 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a ballpark split of Research 55%, Education 35%, Corporate 10%. It sees no company-specific risk, only broader geopolitical and macro risk. Management disputed the analyst's constant-currency framing.

532443|2026-03.headline: Cera Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.2% from 18.3% on brass costs and trade discounts.
532443|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, led by volume (about 12%), with management citing early retail recovery from Q3 and continued project strength. EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 98 crore (15.2% margin) from INR 106 crore (18.3%), driven by brass input costs, elevated trade discounts and pre-operating costs for Senator and Polipluz. Price increases were taken in March (11% effective) and April-May (surcharge then 8% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware), with management targeting a 14-15% EBITDA margin. Morbi gas disruptions were cited as an opportunity, with Cera running inventory and internalising outsourced SKUs. FY26 revenue was INR 2,050 crore, and FY27 guidance is 18-20% growth.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said discounts rose through the downturn and cannot be cut immediately; control starts from Q1 FY27. Q4 margin rose to 15.2% from 10.2% in Q3, and management expects 14-15% to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sanitaryware capacity utilisation, inventory and supply outlook for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware utilisation was 70% in March; one kiln was closed. Management said inventory covers about 2-3 months of forecast demand, and tiles are expected to be impacted in Q1 because they are fully outsourced.

qa_highlights.question: What are the employee cost trends and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 included about INR 5 crore of wage code provision, and Q4 had a INR 10 crore exceptional write-back on gratuity and PL liability. Employee cost is expected to rise about 10% in FY27. Capex is guided at about INR 43-45 crore including office space of about INR 15 crore.

532443|2026-06.headline: Cera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.5% (volume-led) to INR 486 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.1% on one-time factors management says reverse from Q3.
532443|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 19.5% YoY to INR 486 crore, with Sanitaryware up 14%, Faucetware up 25% and growth mainly volume-driven. 532457|2026-03.headline: Gulshan Polyols Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 121% YoY to INR 65 crore on 11.9% margin, driven by ethanol; FY26 PAT INR 107 crore.
532457|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 550 crore (up 7% YoY) and EBITDA INR 65 crore (up 121%), with margin up 612 bps to 11.9%. Ethanol drove the improvement on higher utilisation and softer maize and rice input costs, while grain processing stayed weak at a 2.1% margin. Q4 PAT was INR 38 crore (up 435%) and FY26 PAT INR 107 crore (up 334%). Management said the ethanol order book fell to 18 crore litres from 21 crore litres last year, below the 23 crore litres it had applied for, and it expects top-ups in the next tenders.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,609 crore, EBITDA INR 201 crore, margin 12.5%; management says it is over 60% of revenue and profit. Installed capacity about 810 KLPD.

segments.name: Grain processing (sorbitol, starch, fructose)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 610 crore, EBITDA INR 13 crore, margin 2.1%, held back by pricing. Management targets about 5% EBITDA margin (about INR 40 crore) on INR 800 crore revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 93 crore, EBITDA INR 23 crore, margin 24.2%; described as a steady cash-flow contributor.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR 2,600-2,800 crore: ethanol INR 1,800-1,900 crore, grain INR 800 crore, mineral INR 100 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 10-12% and PAT margin at 5-6%.
Utilisation target of 80-90% across key divisions; up to INR 3,000 crore revenue possible at 100% utilisation with the current setup.
Ethanol order book to rise from 18 crore litres to at least 22 crore litres within FY27, via tenders expected in June (C2 and C3 cycles).
Management expects to sustain current ethanol margins for the next two to three years while FCI rice remains available.

Debt-free by FY29 except the Assam plant long-term loan, which runs to FY32. PLI: MP for seven years, Assam for three years; total PLI about INR 30 crore per annum; INR 5 crore capital subsidy expected in Q1 FY27.

Capex of about INR 500 crore on a 100-acre Narsinghpur (MP) site, to start in FY28 and spread over two to three years; target EBITDA margin of about 15% and ROCE of about 22%. Long-term vision of INR 5,000 crore revenue within about four years.
capex_capacity: Ethanol installed capacity about 810 KLPD; licensed capacity of 26 crore litres per annum against an 18 crore litre order book, leaving headroom to scale up to full utilisation under an E30 mandate.

New capex (about INR 500 crore, specialty and import-substitute chemicals, mostly grain-processing based) to start in FY28; funding is a mix of debt, equity and possible fundraising; Board approval pending.
Possible capacity enhancement of sorbitol and fructose; no ethanol capex planned yet, though capacity may be enhanced over time.
Maize pricing about INR 19-20/kg in the north during Rabi season; the company keeps about 20 days of inventory.
demand_pricing: Ethanol order book of 18 crore litres (about INR 1,250 crore revenue) for ESY 2025-26; the company had applied for 23 crore litres and received 18 crore, against 21 crore litres last year. About 50% already fulfilled by March; about 9 crore litres expected over the remaining two quarters.
Long-term OMC off-take of about 13 crore litres per year through 2032.
Realisations: DDGS INR 21-22/kg (maize) and INR 25-27/kg (rice), adding about INR 10/litre to ethanol economics. Ethanol EBITDA about INR 10-11/litre on a 12% margin.
Sorbitol exported to over 45 countries; export exposure is small at about INR 100 crore. Management says 80-90% of suppliers are domestic.

Maize outlook: INR 19-20/kg in the north now, INR 22 in MP; in H2 FY27 MP may fall to INR 18-19 and Assam/Muzaffarnagar may be around INR 22. Positive EBITDA break-even for ethanol at maize about INR 24/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and how will it be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol order book is 18 crore litres (about INR 1,250 crore), expected to rise to at least 22 crore litres in FY27 through C2 and C3 tenders due in June.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the company for E30 blending and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity of 26 crore litres gives 8 crore litres of unused headroom; management is ready to run at up to 100% once the mandate is given. Government is considering E25, E27 and E30. Management expects FCI rice supply to hold for two to three years, keeping margins steady.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 ethanol volume decline versus the previous year and quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: The ESY 2025-26 allocation fell to 18 crore litres from 21 crore litres, and about 50% was fulfilled by March. Additional allocations are expected in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is any subsidy included in Q4 results?
qa_highlights.answer: No subsidy was received in Q4; the result is operating profit only. A INR 5 crore capital subsidy for Assam is expected in Q1 FY27, and PLIs are expected by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for grain processing in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the worst is over and targets about 5% EBITDA margin on about INR 800 crore revenue (about INR 40 crore EBITDA) in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and expected returns?
qa_highlights.answer: A mega project of about INR 500 crore on the Narsinghpur land, with capex in FY28-29 funded by debt and equity. Target EBITDA margin is about 15% and ROCE about 22%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory build up in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sugar-based ethanol is available only until about March-April, so OMCs lift more from sugar in Q4 and inventory builds. This is a recurring seasonal pattern that has evened out in the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why are non-current investments higher (INR 47 crore versus INR 16 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus funds were invested in mutual funds to meet bank commitments on minimum working capital utilisation levels.

risks_watch: Ethanol volumes depend on tender allocations; the company received 18 crore litres against 23 crore litres applied for, and the gap must be closed in the June tenders.
Dependence on FCI rice availability (about 40% of feedstock); a change in government supply would affect the cost advantage.
Maize and rice prices, DDGS realisations and seasonal Kharif pricing (INR 18-22/kg) affect ethanol economics.
Grain processing margin remains at 2.1% and depends on import costs and China competition.
Capex funding for the INR 500 crore project is undecided; equity fundraising is possible.
Working capital build-up in Q4 (ethanol inventory) and the company's stated aim of reducing working capital intensity.
Mutual fund investments of INR 47 crore were made to meet bank minimum-utilisation commitments.
532457|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on ethanol demand, blending policy and margin sustainability. Evasive on the exact order-book shortfall and on capex funding and timing, which are still under evaluation. Several growth targets are stated without a supporting bridge.
key_quotes: Our ethanol business is now the primary driver of the company, contributing over 60% of both revenue and profitability.
So, definitely, I feel the worst is over for the grain processing division.
So, I don't ever see that demand will be more than supply.
Current order book is definitely lower than what we had applied for and expected.

rows.why: About INR 500 crore Narsinghpur capex is guided to start in FY28 over two to three years, but Board approval is pending and funding is undecided, so timing is not firm.

rows.why: Ethanol order book of 18 crore litres is targeted to rise to at least 22 crore litres in FY27 via June C2/C3 tenders, and about 8 crore litres of licensed headroom (26 crore vs 18 crore) is unused.

rows.why: Management says up to INR 3,000 crore revenue is possible at 100% utilisation, and ethanol volumes could rise if the June tenders top up the 18 crore litre order book toward 22 crore litres, but the FY27 guide is only 2,600-2,800 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Order book of 18 crore litres is 5 crore litres below the 23 crore applied for, and only about 50% was fulfilled by March, so the June tenders must close the gap or volumes fall short of plan.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Specialty and import-substitute chemicals are part of the INR 500 crore Narsinghpur project, but it only starts in FY28 and no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Ethanol order book top-up to 22 crore litres
rows.why: Order book fell to 18 crore litres from 21 crore litres last year, against 23 crore applied for; management expects at least 22 crore litres within FY27 and about 9 crore litres still to be fulfilled over the remaining two quarters.

rows.label: Maize cost relief in H2 FY27
rows.why: MP maize may fall to INR 18-19/kg from INR 22 and Assam/Muzaffarnagar around INR 22, versus ethanol EBITDA break-even at about INR 24/kg, so the cost tailwind is conditional on prices holding.

rows.label: Debt-free by FY29 ex-Assam term loan
rows.why: Total debt is about INR 313 crore today, and management says the company could be debt-free by FY29 except the Assam loan running to FY32, though the INR 500 crore capex funding is undecided.

tone.note: Management was confident on ethanol demand, E30 readiness and FY27 margin sustainability, but evasive on the order-book shortfall (18 vs 23 crore litres applied for) and on capex funding and timing; analysts pressed on those gaps.

532457|2026-06.headline: Gulshan Polyols Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR646 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA rose 135% to INR91 crore, a 14.2% margin.
532457|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of about INR646 crore was the highest quarterly turnover in company history, up 8% YoY. EBITDA of INR91 crore grew 135% YoY, with margin at 14.2% versus 6.5% a year earlier, and PAT of INR54 crore rose about 307% YoY. Ethanol was the main driver with an 18% segment EBITDA margin, while grain processing improved from weak levels and mineral chemicals stayed steady. Management called Q1 exceptional on favourable raw material prices and high DDGS prices, and kept FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling a conservative stance.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR426 crore and EBITDA INR81 crore (18% margin); largest contributor to revenue and profit. Installed capacity about 26 crore litres per annum; order book about 19 crore litres.

segments.name: Grain processing (starch, sorbitol, derivatives)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR170 crore and EBITDA INR8 crore in Q1. FY27 guidance is revenue about INR800 crore at about 5% EBITDA margin; no capacity expansion this year.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR24 crore and EBITDA INR5 crore (23% margin). Described as stable; no significant capacity expansion planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of about INR2,600 crore, unchanged.
Ethanol revenue about INR1,700-1,800 crore on supplies of about 22 crore litres (Q&A cited 21-22 crore litres generating about INR1,800 crore).
Grain processing revenue about INR800 crore; mineral processing about INR100 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA margin about 10-11% and PAT margin about 5-6%; management said it expects to end the year above these margins but is guiding conservatively.
Ethanol debottlenecking to lift utilisation to 100-110% of existing capacity by FY28, with capacity up about 15-20%.
On-site plant at Trident expected to be operational by end of FY27, adding some revenue.
capex_capacity: Majority of recent capex is complete; FY27 focus is on utilisation and cash flow, with only ethanol debottlenecking planned.
Major expansion into specialty and import-substitute chemicals, grain-based derivatives, expected from FY28; products still under evaluation and not yet named.
Starch capacity to be ramped to 100% utilisation by end of FY27; no starch expansion this year.
Capital subsidy of INR5 crore received from Madhya Pradesh in Q2, adjusted against plant and machinery capex.
Ethanol plants at Assam and Madhya Pradesh; four plants in total grinding about 3,000 tonnes of grain per day.
demand_pricing: Government support for ethanol: E20 achieved; E30 targeted by 2030. Management said higher blending beyond 20% may slip 6-12 months because of protests, but E20 will not be rolled back.
Ethanol feedstock mix: about 40% FCI rice, about 50% maize, about 10% broken rice/DDGS.

Maize prices currently INR23-25/kg across plants (Assam 23, Muzaffarnagar 23, Gujarat 24, MP 25); Q1 raw-material costs were favourable and Q2 is seasonally pressured until the Kharif harvest in October-November.
Maize DDGS priced at about INR20-22; stable for about two quarters. DDGS contributes about INR10 per litre of ethanol cost.
Grain processing: domestic starch and derivative prices improved as exports began from Gujarat; sorbitol exported to more than 40 countries. Management expects a sharp YoY improvement in the segment.
Inventory cap of 30-45 days of grain because of storage and working-capital limits, so raw-material volatility is only partly hedged.
Talks on opening ethanol exports to neighbouring countries (Japan, Indonesia mentioned in press); not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong Q1 ethanol margin a one-off, given FY guidance of about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was exceptional on favourable raw material prices and record DDGS prices. Q2 is seasonally weak, and H2 (Q3-Q4) is usually stronger; guidance is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Will E30 timelines slip given protests?
qa_highlights.answer: E20 will not be rolled back. E30 is set for 2030, and blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6-12 months. Steady-state ethanol demand is not expected to be affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ethanol order book and how confident is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: About 19 crore litres already received, with about 2 crore litres more expected. Management is confident of 21-22 crore litres for FY27, generating about INR1,800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw-material price volatility managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking is capped at 30-45 days of grain. Management will stock up during the April and October harvests, and the full-year margin is expected to average out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term ethanol growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise 15-20% through debottlenecking, targeting 100-110% utilisation of existing capacity by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the grain processing underperformance and what is the recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recovery has started with a big YoY margin improvement. Starch capacity is to reach 100% by year-end, with FY27 grain processing EBITDA margin about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export exposure and hedging approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about INR18 crore, or 5-6% of quarterly turnover. The company does not hedge FX and relies on a natural hedge from equivalent imports.

qa_highlights.question: Were any government subsidies recognised in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Grants and incentives are accounted for on a receipt basis, and nothing was received in Q1. INR5 crore MP capital subsidy was received in Q2 and adjusted against capex.

risks_watch: Q2 seasonal pressure on maize and grain costs before the Kharif harvest; margins may fall short of Q1 levels.
Possible 6-12 month delay to blending beyond E20 because of protests, which could slow incremental ethanol allocations.
Grain processing (starch) remains low-margin, around 5% EBITDA guided, with a recovery still to be proven.
Specialty chemical expansion from FY28 has no named products or capex figure yet.
Ethanol export opening is still at talk stage; timing is uncertain.
Reliance on OMC purchase orders for the 2 crore litre balance not yet received.
key_quotes: So, we are just talking on more conservative guidance we have given for the year, and I hope that we are doing better, we ultimately perform better than what we are guiding.
The increasing blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6 months to 1 year until these unnecessary social media noise settles down.
R&D process is going on, but we will not be able to give out any name until it has been finalized by the board.
There has been protest, but that is really temporary. The government will not roll back for sure.
