532461|2026-03.headline: PNB Q4 FY26 net profit rose 14.4% YoY to INR5,225 crore; GNPA fell to 2.95% and FY27 NIM guided at 2.6-2.7%.
532461|2026-03.overview: Punjab National Bank reported Q4 FY26 net profit of INR5,225 crore (up 14.4% YoY) and operating profit of INR7,500 crore (up 10.7% YoY), with FY26 operating profit growth of 9.2% above its 8-9% guidance. Asset quality improved: GNPA fell to 2.95% from 3.95% and NNPA to 0.29% from 0.40%, with FY26 slippage ratio at 0.60%. Domestic NIM was 2.61% in Q4 and global NIM 2.47%, below earlier guidance of 2.8-2.9%, and management cut FY27 global NIM guidance to 2.6-2.7%. Management said the Q4 employee cost fall reflected a INR2,121 crore positive impact from AS-15 yield hardening, which flatters profit, and it framed the ECL transition from April 2027 as manageable.

financial_highlights.change: +10.7% YoY vs INR6,776 crore; FY26 +9.2% vs 8-9% guidance
stable across all four quarters of FY26

segments.name: Retail (ex-IBPC)
segments.commentary: Retail book excluding IBPC grew 18.2% YoY; total retail outstanding about INR2.80 lakh crore including IBPC of INR34,049 crore, which management plans to cut by a further INR18,000-20,000 crore.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 19.9% YoY and management cited ~20% QoQ growth; Q4 MSME slippage INR1,106 crore vs INR995 crore a year earlier. Standard MSME advance yield is 9%.

segments.name: Agriculture (priority sector)
segments.commentary: Agri priority sector advances grew 16.2% YoY; Q4 agri slippage INR1,069 crore vs INR1,400 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate share of loan book is about 46-47%, targeted to fall to 42% short term and 40% long term; corporate standard yield is 7.55%. Sanctioned over INR4 lakh crore of corporate credit lines in FY26, with INR1.18 lakh crore pending disbursement.

guidance_outlook: Global NIM guided at 2.6-2.7% for FY27, versus 2.8-2.9% earlier; management will revisit the guidance in October after Q1 and Q2 review.
NII growth guided at about 7% for FY27 alongside 12-13% credit growth; management called it conservative and said it may revisit in October.
Management expects Q1 and Q2 FY27 NIM to improve QoQ, with cost of deposits falling about 5 bps from the special-scheme repricing and incremental deposit cost falling 2-3 bps a month.

ECL transition from 1 April 2027: management said capital (CRAR 17.74%), the INR2,045 crore floating provision and 97% PCR are sufficient; final ECL impact to be quantified in about two quarters (by July).
Plans to open 250 branches in FY27 (primarily South and West) after adding 144 in FY26; LCR to be maintained around 125%.
Credit cost guidance for FY27 is below 0.4%, as referenced by an analyst; no change was disputed on the call.
capex_capacity: Added 144 branches in FY26 and plans 250 more in FY27, mainly in Southern and Western regions.
New zonal office in Bengaluru operationalised.

No fresh capital raise planned: FY26 had INR8,000 crore authorisation (INR4,000 crore CET1 and INR4,000 crore AT1) but no issuance; INR5,890 crore of AT1 and Tier 2 bonds mature in the current year and will not be replaced.
Wage revision due 1 November 2027, so no FY27 provision was taken for it.
demand_pricing: Total SMA-0/1/2 book is INR41,534 crore (3.30% of advances): SMA-0 INR24,643 crore, SMA-1 INR13,970 crore, SMA-2 INR2,922 crore; retail 8.21%, agri 3.06%, MSME 6.43%.
Q4 FY26 fresh slippages INR2,674 crore vs INR2,904 crore a year earlier; FY26 slippages INR2,758 crore vs INR3,001 crore in FY25. Recoveries of INR15,501 crore in FY26 (2.4x slippages).
Digital sanctions exceeded INR1 lakh crore on a gross basis; INR20,873 crore disbursed digitally in Q4 to 4.8 lakh customers, about one in three loans.
Deposit rates remained sticky; management said cost of deposits has not fallen as expected despite the repo cut, and the Dec-2025 cut hit fully in Q4 versus 26 days in Q3.
Yield on standard domestic advances is 8.23%, above the 7.55% corporate yield.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall sharply QoQ to INR3,747 crore and what is the AS-15 effect?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Raman Grover said AS-15 provisions of INR1,150 crore, INR700 crore and INR700 crore were booked in Q1-Q3; in Q4 no further provision was needed due to bond yield hardening, so INR736 crore is held as prepaid AS-15 and INR1,814 crore was booked to employee cost. Total positive impact cited as INR2,121 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the tax rate rise to about 26.16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 tax was booked at the 25.168% rate plus disallowances, giving an effective 26.16%; Q3 had a reversal of about INR506 crore of earlier provisions, which lowered the Q3 rate to 19.44%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was NIM guided down to 2.6-2.7% and can it return to 2.8-2.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Chandra said deposit rates stayed elevated and bond yields are high, so management chose a conservative 2.6-2.7% range, to be reviewed in Q3 FY27 after watching Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How do 12-13% credit growth and 7% NII growth reconcile with NIM expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NII guidance is conservative given the uncertain corporate book; RAM share is ~54% and targeted to reach 56-57% this year, with corporate falling toward 40% long term, which should lift yields.

qa_highlights.question: Was the ILFS and Sterling Biotech write-back accounted for, and why did standard asset provisions reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Sterling Biotech (a technical write-off) was factored into operating profit. ILFS is still held under standard provision and may be released in Q1 or Q2. The INR727 crore standard-asset provision release reflects RBI's modified large borrower framework effective 1 January 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact and effect on run-rate credit cost and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the final number awaits about two more quarters; the earlier draft estimate was INR9,000-10,000 crore shortfall. Management said the INR2,045 crore floating provision and 97% PCR can absorb it and that ROA will stay above 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the West Asia conflict's impact on MSME and exporters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has seen no challenge in the book so far and held two webinars with exporters and importers in affected areas.

risks_watch: ECL transition from April 2027: final impact unquantified, with management reviewing in about two quarters (by July) and the INR9,000-10,000 crore draft shortfall figure not confirmed.

Q4 NIM was 2.64%, down from 2.76% in Q3, which management attributed mainly to the December 2025 repo cut passing through to benchmark-linked loans. The bank set aside an additional INR 700 crore general/standard provision, stated as not affecting net profit or capital, and Q4 profit was supported by a INR 1,567 crore write-off recovery (including a INR 658 crore Sterling Biotech settlement) and a lower employee cost due to a discount-rate change. segments.commentary: Treasury book reduced by about INR 25,000 crore to fund loan growth; AFS reserve fell about INR 800 crore QoQ to a negative INR 1,008 crore balance, per the call.

532482|2026-09.headline: Granules pivots to four growth engines; plans ~2,000 crore organic capex over 3-4 years after warrant-funded move to net cash.
532482|2026-09.overview: Management, at an IIFL-hosted "Granules India 2.0" webinar, framed FY27 onward as a shift from building capabilities to scaling them, after a return to growth in FY26. Four growth engines were named: controlled substances, complex generics/early market entry, oncology, and peptide CDMO (Senn Tides). The CFO said the company is now in a consolidated net cash position following September 2026 preferential warrant proceeds, and plans about 2,000 crore of organic capex over three to four years. Management was candid that gross margin gains (about 15 pp over four years) have not yet fully flowed to EBITDA, and that the peptide business is currently loss-making. No quarterly financial figures for Q2 FY27 were given in the call.

segments.commentary: Two sole first-to-file ANDAs filed (generic Lumryz and generic Dyanavel, combined US market above $350 million, potential 180-day exclusivity); four to five further first-to-files planned for FY30-34 commercialisation.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Shifted from broad conventional oncology generics to selected molecules; two products filed, one extended to about 15 countries; about six more filings planned this year and early next year. Commercialisation begins FY29.

segments.commentary: Acquired about 18 months ago; currently EBITDA-negative with target to turn profitable in FY27. Targets about $50 million revenue run-rate in three years and above $100 million in five years. About one-third of about $20 million revenue is development-based.

segments.commentary: Management plans a meaningful Latin America and other international presence by FY30 using B2B and B2C channels.

532483|2026-06.headline: Canara Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 2.19% YoY to ₹4,856 crore, with NII crossing ₹10,000 crore and CET1 at 12.91%.
532483|2026-06.overview: Management reported global business up 14.37% YoY to ₹29.05 lakh crore, with advances up 17.97% and deposits up 11.63%. NII rose 13.39% YoY to ₹10,215 crore, the first time above ₹10,000 crore. Asset quality improved: gross NPA 1.57% (down 112 bps YoY), net NPA 0.36%, PCR 94.76%, and credit cost 0.49%. Profit was supported by ₹1,947 crore of other income, largely PSLC sale gains, against ₹654 crore from investment sales, while treasury gains fell sharply YoY. Management flagged an incremental ECL provisioning requirement of about ₹10,000-12,000 crore, to be absorbed over two years.

financial_highlights.metric: Other income (per analyst's figure, Q1 vs Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs ₹393 crore in Q4 FY26; Q1 FY26 was ₹1,684 crore PSLC income

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances ₹7,64,675 crore, up 21.20% YoY. Retail RAM ₹3,19,893 crore, up 35.88%, with housing ₹1,29,036 crore (+17.85%) and vehicle ₹27,315 crore (+26.34%).

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances ₹1,68,815 crore, up 15.12% YoY. MSME and agri carried most of Q1 slippages (₹697 crore and ₹727 crore respectively).

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loan book ₹2.59 lakh crore: agri gold ₹1.51 lakh crore and retail gold ₹1.07 lakh crore. LTV around 60-65%.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and associates
segments.commentary: Around 5 subsidiaries and 5 associates; Canara HSBC Life and Canara Robeco listed last year. Management said they contributed about ₹320 crore of profit to the parent this year.

guidance_outlook: NIM guidance of 2.50-2.60% retained; management said it could exceed 2.60% but kept the range given headwinds.
Credit cost expected to rise by about 4-5 bps on a run-rate basis after ECL transition, per management (initially said up to 10 bps).
ECL: incremental provision of about ₹10,000-12,000 crore (about 1.2-1.25% of RWA), to be absorbed over 2 years versus the 5-year RBI window; dry run by October.
FCNRB: guidance of USD 2.3-2.5 billion; USD 775 million raised in July so far, with a target above USD 1 billion for the month.

ROA guidance of 1.01-1.05%; management said 1.01-1.02% would be acceptable. Deposit growth guidance of 9-10%, with management aiming for 11-12%. Plans to open 250 branches this year (34 opened so far).
Credit pipeline of about ₹50,000 crore: 45 accounts sanctioned but undisbursed (about ₹18,000 crore) and 47 accounts (about ₹32,000 crore) in hand.
capex_capacity: Branch network 10,131; plan to open 250 new branches in FY27, 34 opened so far.
Digital spend earmarked above ₹3,000 crore, about 8% of total IT cost, with a substantial share toward AI.
Credit pipeline of about ₹50,000 crore across 92-100 accounts.
demand_pricing: Advances growth was helped by ECLGS 5.0: about ₹18,000 crore eligible, ₹11,000 crore-plus sanctioned and ₹10,000 crore-plus disbursed, with ₹5,000-6,000 crore still to come. Management said the spill-over could support growth in coming quarters.
Corporate pricing has improved by about 10-20 bps in some cases; management said incremental lending is being done above the average yield.
Yield on advances was 8% against 6.90% on investments. Yield on advances fell 29 bps QoQ, while cost of deposits fell 27 bps.
Bulk deposit cost was 6.58% last month and is falling about 20-30 bps a month. FCNRB is being raised at about 6.50%.
CASA ratio is 29.70%; SA individual deposits up 12.48% and retail term deposits up 9.10%. CD ratio rose from 75% to 80%.
Corporate book: 86% rated A and above. RAM yield is about 50 bps above corporate yield, per management.
Fee income: YoY growth of 5.35%; YTD fee income is down less than ₹200 crore versus Q4, because some commissions were booked in Q4.
Q1 slippage ₹1,781 crore: agri ₹727 crore, MSME ₹697 crore, retail ₹326 crore, gold ₹20-30 crore. Total SMA is below 3%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SMA-2 rise from ₹1,394 crore to ₹3,482 crore, and what is the ECLGS 5.0 assessment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to 2-3 government-guaranteed consortium accounts that oscillate between SMA-0, 1 and 2; one account moved to SMA-2 and has since returned to SMA-0. Total SMA is below 3%. ECLGS 5.0: ₹18,000 crore eligible, ₹11,000 crore-plus sanctioned, ₹10,000 crore-plus disbursed.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the other income jump (PSLC, treasury), and what drove provisions of ₹3,780 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury gains fell YoY (Q1 FY26 ₹1,617 crore, Q1 FY27 ₹654 crore from investment sales) because arbitrage was absent and yields had hardened. PSLC income is concentrated in Q1 and part of Q2 (₹1,947 crore in Q1). Provisions rose on income tax, and ₹300 crore was provided for PLI staff incentives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact and how will it be absorbed?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental provisioning of ₹10,000-12,000 crore including about ₹2,000 crore for M2M on investments. CET1 would fall by about 1.2-1.25%, against a regulatory minimum of 8% CET1. Provision to be absorbed over 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path for NIM and CASA, and the blended cost of bulk deposits?
qa_highlights.answer: Bulk deposit cost was 6.58% last month and is falling about 20-30 bps per month. Management is replacing bulk deposits with retail deposits and FCNRB, and says NIM will stay in the 2.50-2.60% range for now.

qa_highlights.question: Are yields stabilising, and how is incremental lending priced?
qa_highlights.answer: RAM share rose from 58% to 59%. Sub-7% legacy loans are being reset higher at repricing; corporate pricing is up 10-20 bps in some deals. Management said yields have largely stabilised, but this depends on MPC decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost impact of ECL and the monsoon risk to the agri book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a run-rate increase of about 4-5 bps after ECL. The agri book is not large, and distress-district dispensations from SLBC/DLTC and Fasal Bima would help manage any stress.

risks_watch: ECL transition: incremental provisioning of ₹10,000-12,000 crore, plus possible M2M losses on the investment book, which management could not quantify precisely.
Treasury and PSLC gains are one-time in nature and fell sharply in treasury YoY, so the profit mix may not repeat in coming quarters.
Profit growth of 2.19% YoY trails advances growth of 17.97%, and NII growth of 13.39% also trails advances growth.
Repo-linked assets (53% of portfolio) and possible deposit-rate competition could keep pressure on NIM.
SMA-2 movement and the agri/MSME stress: monsoon risk to the KCC book, and continued consortium account oscillation.
Fee income YTD is down less than ₹200 crore versus Q4; the YoY growth is 5.35%.
532483|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on headline growth, asset quality and capital, with management saying every guidance metric was beaten. Noticeably more cautious on NIM, the ECL impact, and sustainability of PSLC and treasury gains; several answers relied on qualitative reassurance rather than hard figures.
key_quotes: So whatever the performance we have given, we have bettered everywhere on count of guidance whatever we have given.
Even if we are not raising any capital, we will be very peacefully selling through new norms of ECL.
Repricing is also, I mean, I think it is plateau. It is all done.
So, I guess, there will be not much effect. And KCC portfolio also not very huge at our bank, you see.
Yes, our dependency on bulk deposit is more considering our CASA percentage is less than 30%, around 29.70%.

rows.why: NIM at 2.52% sits inside the retained 2.50-2.60% guidance, with bulk deposit cost falling 20-30 bps a month from 6.58% and management saying NIM could exceed 2.60%, but repo-linked assets (53% of book) and ECL drag cap the upside.

532483|2026-09.headline: Canara Bank Q2 FY27: record quarterly net profit of ₹5,175 crore (+8.40% YoY) with Gross NPA down to 1.33%, while ECL transition provisioning now seen at ₹12,000–15,000 crore.
532483|2026-09.overview: Management reported total business crossing ₹30 lakh crore (+15.88% YoY), advances +19.46% and deposits +13.13%, with NII up 20.39% and NIM at 2.53% annual / 2.55% quarterly. Asset quality improved further: Gross NPA 1.33%, Net NPA 0.30%, PCR 95.34% (+175 bps YoY), annualised slippage 0.58% and credit cost 0.47%. Treasury turned into a loss versus the prior year, with MTM about ₹600 crore lower QoQ for the quarter, and management flagged the RBI ECL transition as a ₹12,000–15,000 crore one-time provision requirement. CASA at 29% was the only guidance miss, which management attributed to ₹55,000 crore of FCNR(B) deposits.

financial_highlights.change: FY27 guidance was 1.50% GNPA and ~0.40% NNPA
Agri ₹687 cr, MSME ₹777 cr, Retail ₹327 cr, Corporate ₹13 cr, Gold ₹40 cr

financial_highlights.change: Q2 FY26 MTM profit was ₹762 crore

segments.name: Retail

segments.commentary: Total gold loans ₹2.82 lakh crore (agri ₹1.74 lakh crore, non-agri ₹1.08 lakh crore). Incremental gold yield rose to 9.10% from 8.96% QoQ; gold slippages ₹40 crore.

segments.commentary: Incremental corporate yield 7.72% vs 7.68% in Q1; ~₹47,000–50,000 crore of sanctioned-not-disbursed plus hot leads (₹30,000 crore hot leads, ₹17,000 crore sanctioned) in power, green energy, BESS, data centres and HAM roads.

segments.commentary: Investment book 80% HTM and ~20% AFS/FVTPL; AFS losses ~₹1,300 crore for the quarter go to AFS reserve, not P&L; FVTPL <4% of book. Yields hardened 44 bps in the quarter, ~₹600 crore MTM hit (QoQ basis).

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Canbank Factors stake sale done: ₹14 crore investment, expected ~4x return. Canara HSBC Life and Canara Robeco AMC are listed in the plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance (set at start of year): total business +10–11% (delivered +15.88%), advances +11–12% (delivered +19.46%), deposits +9–10% (delivered +13.13%), CASA 30–32% (delivered 29%), NIM 2.50–2.60%, ROE 16.5%, EPS ₹20, ROA 1.01–1.05%; management said it does not plan to revise guidance and will try to better it.

NIM expected to sustain around 2.55% and the 25 bps repo hike is in the book; 53% of the book is repo-linked and already repriced. FCNR(B) leverage spread of only 40–50 bps is expected to be compensated from Q3.

ECL transition one-time provision now estimated at ₹12,000–15,000 crore (up from ₹10,000–12,000 crore), including HTM; management sees up to ₹14,000–15,000 crore if yields stay hardened, with possible return to ₹10,000–12,000 crore if oil prices and geopolitics ease. Impact about 1–1.2% of CRAR/CET1 basis; spread over 1–2 years (5-year option allowed, but not expected).

Management does not expect the ECL provision to materially hit ROA; it said ROA could settle near 0.80% if provisions are not passed on, but would be above 1% if passed through. No decision yet on passing through.
Management expects to complete ECL model dry run within the current quarter (before 31 March 2027 deadline).
capex_capacity: Capex/capacity disclosure is absent: no capex plan, branch or technology spend figures were given; management said it is investing heavily in digital advancements (QR, school fee modules, internet payment gateways) without quantification.
Balance sheet capacity: CRAR 17.19% and CET1 12.80% vs regulatory minimums of 11.5% and 8.5%; management said RWA density is falling quarter-on-quarter.
ECL model build: dry run with technology partner Coforge expected within the current quarter, ahead of the 31 March 2027 deadline.
Liquidity: LCR 115% as of 30 September 2026; FCNR(B) raised $5.8 billion (~₹55,000 crore), of which $3.2 billion funded advances and the rest replaced bulk deposits.

Lending pipeline: ₹17,000 crore sanctioned but not disbursed plus ₹30,000 crore hot leads (~₹47,000–50,000 crore) in power, green energy, BESS, data centres and HAM roads; ECLGS disbursement ₹13,000+ crore.
demand_pricing: Retail demand robust with festive season; housing growth 17–18% and total retail ~21%; vehicle loans +25%; management says festive mode already started before Dussehra.
Gold loans: competition rising from large NBFCs; management says Canara prices below NBFCs (which borrow from banks) and sees gold yields rising further as rates harden.

Deposit cost: bulk deposits held at ~₹4.38 lakh crore (vs ₹4.37 lakh crore in Q1). FCNR(B) raised $5.8 billion (~₹55,000 crore), of which $3.2 billion funded advances and the rest replaced bulk deposits; overall cost of deposits lower by ~1%.
Drought: 3 states declared drought-affected (part of Karnataka and Maharashtra cited); exposure ~₹13,900 crore; restructuring to be handled via SLBC dispensation.
Digital fee income: UPI MDR not yet quantified; ai1Pe PSP platform has limited traction; management sees little fee upside currently.

qa_highlights.question: What are incremental yields on corporate and gold loans, and will NIM improve from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate incremental yield 7.72% (vs 7.68% Q1); gold 9.10% (vs 8.96%). Management expects NIM to hold around 2.55% with 53% of the book already repriced and MCLR resets to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bulk deposit flat if FCNR(B) was raised; what is the NIM offset?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) fully replaced bulk deposits and saved ~100 bps on the replaced portion (6.5% vs 7.5%) plus CRR/SLR cost benefits. Bulk held at ₹4.38 lakh crore; the FCNR leverage spread (40–50 bps) should be offset from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL one-time provision and how will it hit net worth and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimate ₹12,000–15,000 crore including HTM (RBI allows 5 years). Management prefers to spread over 1–2 years; expects PCR to rise to 96–97% and profit >₹20,000 crore to absorb it without denting ROA.

qa_highlights.question: Will the drought affect recoveries and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Drought exposure is ~₹13,900 crore; SLBC restructuring/moratorium expected. Total stress including SMA-0 is 2.42% (₹33,340 crore); >₹5 crore tickets stress 0.30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury/MTM impact and AFS reserve position?
qa_highlights.answer: AFS losses ~₹1,300 crore go to reserve; FVTPL loss ~₹600 crore QoQ swing (Q1 +₹555 crore, Q2 -₹55 crore). Yields hardened 44 bps in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Canbank Factors sale and recovery trend on written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Canbank Factors sale done (₹14 crore cost, ~4x expected). Written-off pool ~₹18,000 crore and dwindling; recoveries exceed slippages each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: SMA position and LCR?
qa_highlights.answer: SMA 0–2 for ≥₹5 crore is 0.51% (₹7,043 crore); SMA 2 is 0.21% and SMA 1 0.09%. LCR 115% at 30 Sep 2026.

risks_watch: ECL one-time provision of ₹12,000–15,000 crore (up from ₹10,000–12,000 crore); a dry run is due this quarter and the phasing decision (1–2 years vs 5-year option) is deferred to the last quarter.
Bond yield path: management said yields could harden further, with HTM also subject to provisioning; a 44 bps hardening in Q2 drove the treasury swing.
Whether ECL provisions are passed on to customers: ROA could settle near 0.80% if not passed on, above 1% if passed through; no decision yet.
Gold loan competition from large NBFCs; management expects no yield pressure but acknowledged rising competition.
CASA at 29% vs 30–32% guidance; FCNR(B) leverage spread of only 40–50 bps to be offset from Q3, and the bulk deposit replacement may need to continue.
Drought exposure ~₹13,900 crore across 3 states; restructuring depends on state-level SLBC dispensations.

Our Housing loan in excess of 17%, 18% is growing. Total retail, 21%, vehicle loan, 25%.

532488|2026-03.headline: Divi's Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT rose to ₹963 crores (vs ₹864 crores YoY) and PAT to ₹751 crores, while management guided only to "stable" margins.
532488|2026-03.overview: Divi's reported Q4 FY26 consolidated total income of ₹2,986 crores, PBT of ₹963 crores and PAT of ₹751 crores, including a ₹90 crore forex gain. For FY26, total income rose to ₹11,067 crores from ₹9,712 crores, PAT to ₹2,568 crores from ₹2,191 crores, after a one-time ₹74 crore Labour Code charge. Management said volumes in generics were stable with some pricing pressure, while West Asia-related disruption raised raw material, solvent and freight costs and forced some suppliers to declare force majeure. Management declined to quantify FY27 margins, guiding only to stable margins and double-digit revenue growth.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹2,916 crores in FY25; after ₹74 crore Labour Code exceptional charge

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Volumes stable and healthy through Q4 and FY26 per management, but slight pricing pressure; generic API contracts have variability clauses with reviews as often as every 3 months. FY26 product mix was 45% generics.

segments.name: Custom Synthesis (CS)
segments.commentary: FY26 product mix was 55% CS. Management cited a strong project pipeline across Phase II/III, validation and qualification stages; late life-cycle management volumes may decline as products mature.

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Several fragments validated in the quarter with more in pipeline; capabilities include protected amino acids, solid-phase and liquid-phase synthesis, and 3,000-litre SPPS capacity.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: Iodine-based contrast media in commercial sales to innovators, supplied in multiple tonnes; Gadolinium compounds still at qualification as customers' products are in Phase II/III.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹946 crores in FY26, up from ₹781 crores in FY25.

Freight-related cost pressures expected to continue in the near term and have been factored into planning.
FY27 capex expected to be roughly constant unless a major CS or new project emerges (CWIP about ₹2,000 crore odd).

Capital allocation to CS and peptides, with long-term supply agreements; management guides toward a 2-year range from capex to revenue, but acknowledged timelines from 6 months to 3 years.

Generic pricing under competitive pressure; customers understanding of market conditions has supported ongoing price discussions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind on raw material availability, and how is methanol sourcing being managed for H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the conflict affected only about one month of FY26 and there were no production stoppages, but sourcing is difficult across solvents and other materials; availability is being reviewed quarterly, with securing supply for the next 3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a margin figure, saying it is difficult to project but expected to remain stable; capex for FY27 expected to be constant unless a major CS project emerges.

qa_highlights.question: Why was constant currency growth only about 6% despite capacity additions?

532493|2026-03.headline: FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores in line with guidance; order book INR2,141 crores standalone and FY27 top-line growth reaffirmed at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is EW (Tejas, Su-30) and LCH content in the order inflow projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Angad and some LCH subsystems are included in the 4-year projections. Tejas Mk1A is additional, around INR500-600 crore. Management said none of the EM wall or counter-UAV revenue is in its numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to positive cash at the end of FY26, which kept overdraft utilisation in Q1 minimal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uttam execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall execution is about 5 years, with total completion before FY32 and possibly by FY31; Phase 1 of 12 numbers is due by September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What margin guidance is available for new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to margins, citing product mix and lifecycle economics. It expects margins to be as healthy as the current business, or nearly so.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 6-7x five-year revenue target based on the defence business only?
qa_highlights.answer: The order visibility excludes space, apart from the existing book. Management said the 6-7x is against the combined FY26 base of INR1,057 crore, since the demerger has not yet happened.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue decline and was there deferred revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited inspection and specification-proof delays, development-cycle issues and supply-chain issues that pushed some programmes out of Q1. It expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger and said quarterly numbers are internal estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital moderate further in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant change versus FY26 is expected; Q1 and early Q2 are seasonally better and pressure rises in Q3 and Q4. Management ruled out equity dilution for working capital.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 revenue of INR182 crore was described as modest; management attributes shortfall to inspection, specification-proof, development-cycle and supply-chain delays and expects Q3 and Q4 to carry the year, so watch whether H2 execution delivers the INR1,350 crore FY27 target (+/-INR25 crore).

Execution load on the INR2,205 crore Uttam Radar order: Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027 and roughly 25+ numbers per year thereafter; supply chains are stretched and management flagged cross-border supply risk.

Working capital: management expects Q3 and Q4 pressure to build and no significant change versus FY26; it ruled out equity dilution for working capital, so monitor receivables and operating cash flow at the end-Q3 update.

Order inflow visibility rests on unawarded programmes (AMCA AAAU where the company is L1 with contract expected in about a month, QRSAM, Su-30 Virupaksha/Angad, Tejas Mk1A EW, P-75I); none of the EM wall, counter-UAV, chip, export or BrahMos NG upside is in numbers.

Space and Weather demerger from April 1, 2027: details on leadership, plans, satellite launch and the INR300-plus crore first-year revenue guidance remain to be shared over the next few quarters; watch for structure and shareholder-ratio clarity.

Long-term 5-year 6-7x revenue ambition and INR8,000-9,000 crore order intake ambition were questioned by analysts (ICICI Securities on cumulative execution); management said it would clarify one-to-one, so treat as unverified until tracked.
key_quotes: The revenue and profitability were moderate -- modest, I should say, primarily due to temporary delays in customer approvals and closing some of the last stage technical issues, which are expected to normalize in the coming quarters.

So we have to keep that distinction in mind or AEW&C Mk-2, where we are part of the supply chain or the supply chain for Mk1, where we will have, I think, at least 25%, if not more, of the designated supply chain
But we don't want to commit to you on the margins because there are a lot of factors which will come into play from incremental products, number one.
Till we have accretive nonorganic opportunities, we will not dilute for working capital.
Our quarterly numbers are our internal numbers, which we are constantly fine-tuning.
532493|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book and long-term ambitions, particularly the Uttam Radar win and FY27 guidance, but openly cautious and defensive on Q1 performance, attributing the modest revenue to temporary approval and technical delays. It was evasive on new-product margins, declining to commit beyond "as healthy as the current business, if not as healthy," and on quarterly numbers, which it called internal estimates.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: FY27 revenue is guided at about INR1,350 crore (+15-20% on FY26's INR1,057 crore) and FY28 at about INR1,600 crore (+15-18%), backed by the INR4,300 crore order book, though Q1 revenue of INR182 crore was modest.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex amount or utilisation figure was disclosed; the Uttam execution load (25+ numbers a year) and the 6-7x five-year ambition could prompt a capacity announcement, but this is not guided.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.why: Management expects Q3 and Q4 working capital similar to FY26, with pressure building in those quarters, and has ruled out equity dilution to fund it.

532497|2026-03.headline: Radico Khaitan Q4 FY26: EBITDA margin hit record 19% (+565 bps YoY) on IMFL volume +4%; FY27 guidance of 120-125 bps margin expansion reiterated.
532497|2026-03.overview: FY26 crossed two milestones: net revenue above INR 6,000 crore and EBITDA above INR 1,000 crore. Q4 IMFL volume rose 4% YoY to 9.52 million cases, with Prestige & Above (P&A) volume up 28%, while regular volume declined on a higher base and policy changes in Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka. Gross margin reached 48% (+450 bps YoY, +150 bps QoQ) and EBITDA margin 19% (+565 bps YoY), the highest ever for the company. Net debt fell by INR 329 crore in the year, and management expects to be debt-free in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: New product launches for FY27 in P&A and luxury, and how the 125 bps margin will absorb commodity costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on consolidating three to four luxury/P&A launches nationally (Virasat, Kashmyr to 20 states from 10), more Magic flavours, and Tequila under D'YAVOL by year-end. Margin: 60 bps from price increases plus over 200 bps from premiumisation and operating leverage cover cost push; guidance is annualised.

qa_highlights.question: Will marketing spend unlock given fewer launches?
qa_highlights.answer: No stated unlock; marketing kept within 6-8% of sales depending on launches and flagships. Higher top line means higher absolute marketing spend.

qa_highlights.question: Karnataka pricing, West Bengal, Bihar prohibition?
qa_highlights.answer: Karnataka second price rationalisation expected but not announced; West Bengal too early, open market now; Bihar to be watched with upside if prohibition eased.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 125 bps margin guidance inclusive of India-UK FTA benefit, and what about export impact from US tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 125 bps is inclusive of all factors, with pluses and minuses; US tariff at 10% not material for luxury, US market softer.

qa_highlights.question: How will 20% P&A volume growth be supported in capacity and outsourced supply?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-65% bottling outsourced; Radico supplies all raw material; capex INR 150-175 crore; capacity not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation growth and regular segment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume-value delta expected at 300-400 bps; regular volume guided at 3-5% for FY27 after 30% FY26 growth.

qa_highlights.question: Global strategy and GenZ / low-alcohol plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans for low-alcohol or RTD for now; focus on white spirits and flavours. International share 8-9% and falling as domestic grows faster.

qa_highlights.question: Maharashtra JV and UP market position?
qa_highlights.answer: JV self-sufficient with cash generation, no further investment; aiming about 10% MML share. Radico is No.1 in UP IMFL with about 24-26% share.

532497|2026-06.headline: Radico Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 1,684 crore and EBITDA Rs 348 crore (20.7% margin, record); P&A volumes up 36%.
532497|2026-06.overview: Radico reported record quarterly IMFL volume of 10 million cases (up 3% YoY), revenue of Rs 1,684 crore and EBITDA of Rs 348 crore. Premium and above (P&A) volumes grew 36%, while regular volumes declined on a higher base after the Andhra Pradesh route-to-market change and policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Gross margin rose 610 bps YoY to 49.1% and EBITDA margin rose 536 bps YoY to 20.7%. Management reiterated about 20% EBITDA margin for FY27 and raised P&A volume growth guidance to over 25% from 20%, and said it is on track to become net debt free by Q2 FY27.

segments.commentary: Volume grew 36% in Q1; FY27 guidance raised to over 25% volume growth from 20%. Flavored vodka is 75% of Magic Moments volume, up from 65%.

segments.commentary: 3.25 million cases, +43% YoY, over 60% category share; vodka share of Indian IMFL rose from 4.6% in Q1 FY26 to 6.1% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Luxury portfolio
segments.commentary: FY26 luxury turnover about Rs 475 crore; management says it is on target for 25% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Non-IMFL
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin about 11% to 11.5% in Q1, versus 6% to 7% in the recent inflationary period; management calls this sustainable.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Brands sold in over 100 countries; exports are about 5% to 6% of volume, with a higher share of value; 63 global travel retail outlets and 50 to 63 airports (target 100).

Morpheus whisky launched in 10 to 12 states; early traction but still in seeding phase.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained at 20% EBITDA and how does ENA cost exposure matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 20% EBITDA margin for FY27 and said more clarity will come later in the year. Mix shift to P&A is expected to support margins, reducing ENA sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20.7% margin sustainable, and what are IMFL and non-IMFL margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-IMFL margin is about 11% to 11.5% and IMFL is 23%+. Non-IMFL margins historically ranged 8% to 11%, fell to 6% to 7% during inflation, and management considers current levels sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan once debt free?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex is Rs 150 to 170 crore; the remainder is for the Board to decide. Acquisitions only if they make sense for shareholders; management says Radico has always grown organically and sees no brand acquisition opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Magic Moments 43% growth a trade-loading one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied trade loading, citing strong credit control, and said the growth is tertiary-driven, with month-on-month traction continuing.

qa_highlights.question: How will the India-UK FTA affect pricing and competition in luxury?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to comment. Management says single malt is taste-driven, and retail prices may fall only 7% to 8% if passed on; no pricing changes planned yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will A&P spend increase given P&A growth well ahead of peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Ad spend has been held at 7% to 8% of sales; management says spend is focused on direct marketing, in-shop and digital, and that P&A has outpaced the industry for 10 years.

532497|2026-09.headline: Radico Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 1,746 crore and EBITDA margin 20.4%, with P&A volume up 36% and FY27 P&A volume guidance raised to 30%.
532497|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the strongest quarter in company history, with IMFL volume above 10 million cases (+7% YoY), revenue of Rs 1,746 crore and EBITDA of Rs 356 crore at a 20.4% margin (+462 bps YoY). Prestige & Above (P&A) volume hit a record 5.28 million cases, up 36%, while the Regular category declined about 15% after the Andhra Pradesh route-to-market change and Maharashtra and Karnataka policy changes. Gross margin was 48.0%, up 440 bps YoY but down 109 bps QoQ, with packaging inflation costing about Rs 27 crore. The company upgraded FY27 P&A volume growth guidance to 30% and kept EBITDA margin guidance at around 20%. Leadership changes: Dilip Banthiya joined the Board as Executive Director and CFO, and Saket Somani was elevated to Deputy CFO.

segments.name: Prestige & Above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Record 5.28 million cases, up 36% YoY. Vodka grew about 49% and non-vodka P&A about 20%, against an industry P&A growth of about 5.8-6%.

segments.name: Regular
segments.commentary: Volume declined about 15% YoY, driven by the high Q2 FY26 base after the Andhra Pradesh route change and Maharashtra and Karnataka policy changes. H1 Regular volume was down 1.5%.

segments.name: IMFL vs non-IMFL margins
segments.commentary: IMFL EBITDA margin is about 24%+ in Q2; non-IMFL margin is about 9.5-10%.

segments.name: Luxury portfolio
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover was Rs 475 crore; management says it is well on track for 25% value growth in FY27. Virasat Indian Single Malt is priced at about Rs 3,500-4,000 a bottle.

segments.name: Vodka
segments.commentary: Vodka reached 6.3% of IMFL in Q2, up from 3.7% in 2025 and 4.5% in 2026. Flavoured vodka is about 75% of Radico's vodka; vodka is about 30% of Radico's volume.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Shipments to West Asia have recovered after the initial disruption in Feb-Mar 2026; freight costs are the main issue. Radico is now listed in 4 UK airports and in about 70 duty-free locations, with a target of 100.

guidance_outlook: FY27 P&A volume growth guidance upgraded to 30% (from prior guidance, which was revised twice this year).
EBITDA margin guidance of around 20% maintained for FY27.
Luxury portfolio value growth guidance of 25% for FY27 reiterated.
Regular category expected to grow about 1-2% from H2 onward; Maharashtra base effect expected to be largely neutralised in H2.
Management did not give FY28-29 volume numbers, but said momentum will continue and margins will keep expanding; FY28 guidance may come at year end.

segments.commentary: Housing loans grew about 19% and car loans about 71%. Retail gold loans stood at about Rs 5,400 crore, and the 'others' bucket grew about 40% YoY, mainly on gold loans.

segments.name: Agriculture gold loans
segments.commentary: Agri gold loan book is about Rs 12,200 crore, so total gold loans are about Rs 18,000 crore at an estimated 8.5-9% yield.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore MTM hit on the AFS book. Management cited a Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit against Rs 557 crore, which it said it would clarify offline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth 10-12%, credit growth 12-14% (unchanged on deposits, credit range held at 12-14%).
FY27 CASA 37-38%; RAM share raised to 62-65%; CD ratio 80-82%.
FY27 credit cost below 0.75%; global NIM 2.8-2.9%.
FY27 gross NPA below 2%, net NPA below 0.2%, slippage ratio below 1%.
FY27 recovery and upgradation target Rs 2,000-2,500 crore.
ROA of 0.87% in FY26; management expects 0.95-1% by end of FY27.
FY27 IT budget above Rs 1,000 crore, following Rs 899 crore spend in FY26.
capex_capacity: Network: 3,412 domestic branches plus 2 overseas branches (Hong Kong, Singapore) and 1 representative office in Iran; 110 branches added in FY26; 61% of domestic branches in rural and semi-urban areas.
IT spend rose from Rs 576 crore (FY24) to Rs 642 crore (FY25) and Rs 899 crore (FY26).
Completed: CBDC app on iOS and Android, Murex treasury, Kolkata data centre consolidation, API gateway, ALM TPM automation, MuleHunter integration.

Planned for FY27: omnichannel mobile banking, cash management, supply chain finance, RPA, forex and prepaid cards, document management, e-notes, identity access management, Kolkata DR, centralised forex processing, and a CASA back office.
QIP approved by the Board, but management will seek shareholder approval at the AGM first and will not launch it this quarter.
demand_pricing: Corporate pipeline of about Rs 14,000 crore, but disbursement is held back by pricing; management said it will not grow corporate credit at the cost of margins.
Demand is coming from renewables, data centres, smart metering and road projects.
AAA-rated exposure is about 33% of the book (unchanged YoY); AA exposure fell to 26% from 29%.
About 65% of the loan book is linked to the repo rate; retail and MSME make up over Rs 1.1 lakh crore of the book.
CD ratio rose to 80.21% from the 75-77% target, which led the bank to push deposit mobilisation, with a focus on retail term deposits, savings and current accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance (credit growth of 12-14%) a sign that the West Asia conflict is weighing on the bank, and is SMA 1 rising stress for MSMEs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance is conservative and has been 12-14% for three years while actual credit growth was 16% in FY24, 17.72% in FY25 and 19.44% in FY26. It attributed the rise in SMA 1 (to Rs 651 crore from Rs 260 crore) to the February 28-day effect rather than stress, and said total SMA 0-2 is 0.45% of standard advances.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall to Rs 182 crore from Rs 278 crore QoQ, and what buffers exist against ECL and the Labour Code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop reflects a Rs 260 crore PLI provision in FY25, of which only about Rs 100 crore was paid in FY26, leaving about Rs 160 crore provided. It said it holds an ECL provision of Rs 1,038 crore, a Rs 341 crore contingency provision, and a Rs 530 crore COVID provision, for about Rs 1,900 crore of total buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Given the share price and the Rs 1,900 crore buffer, will the bank raise capital this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to raise capital this quarter. It will seek AGM approval first and then launch the QIP at an opportune time when markets support it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-to-income drop driven by, and what is the outlook for ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fee income growth of 32% QoQ and 25% YoY, and tighter control of controllable costs, with recoveries from written-off accounts at about Rs 1,300 crore in FY26 against Rs 2,400-2,500 crore a year earlier. It expects ROA to reach 0.95-1% by end of FY27, from 0.87% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the West Asia war on MSMEs, and what share is covered by CGTMSE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen a major impact, with MSME slippages flat QoQ and no sharp rise in SMA. About 40% of advances are covered under CGTMSE.

qa_highlights.question: Why was treasury negative and what is the AFS reserve position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore AFS MTM hit as yields rose above 7%. Yields have since eased to 6.95-6.98%, and AFS reserves stood at negative Rs 140 crore at March 2026.

risks_watch: Corporate loan growth could stay subdued while pricing discipline holds back disbursements from the Rs 14,000 crore pipeline.
The West Asia conflict may weigh on MSMEs; watch SMA 1 and SMA 2 buckets and MSME slippages in Q1 FY27.
Bond yields and treasury MTM could swing again; FY26 AFS reserves were negative Rs 140 crore.
Employee costs could rise when the Rs 160 crore residual PLI provision is paid, and the Labour Code effect is not yet quantified.
Deposit growth may lag credit growth (11.59% vs 19.44%), which keeps CD ratio pressure on margins; watch whether bulk deposits rise.
Management did not clarify the Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit figure on the call and said it would respond offline.
532505|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on headline delivery, with management repeatedly stressing that FY26 results beat guidance. Defensive on the FY27 guidance and SMA questions, where it attributed changes to the February day-count effect and to the bank's conservative pricing, not to stress.
key_quotes: So, there is no such thing that because of this temporary crisis, we have shifted our guidance downwards.
We do not want credit growth in the Corporate segment at the cost of margins.
February impacts every financial year. SMA 2 is 60 days, but February has 28 days, while January and March have 31 days.
So, all three put together today, we are holding around Rs.1,900 crore of additional provision as a buffer towards our ECL framework.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network stands at 3,412 domestic branches after 110 added in FY26, with no further branch additions guided; the FY27 spend is on IT and back-office, not new physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Credit growth guidance of 12-14% and deposit growth of 10-12% imply continued expansion from a 19.44% advance growth base in FY26, backed by RAM growth of 24%+ and a Rs 14,000 crore corporate pipeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex discussion is limited to IT (FY27 budget above Rs 1,000 crore vs Rs 899 crore in FY26) and no utilisation figure or new plant was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit grew 19.44% in FY26 against 12-14% FY27 guidance, and management called the guide conservative, but corporate disbursements are held back by pricing on a Rs 14,000 crore pipeline.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit growth guidance of 12-14% sits well below the 19.44% delivered in FY26, and the Rs 160 crore residual PLI payment and unquantified Labour Code effect could pressure employee costs; the risk is more that guidance is conservative than that it is cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management has a dated FY27 plan for omnichannel mobile banking, cash management, supply chain finance, forex and prepaid cards, and e-notes, following completed CBDC app and Murex treasury projects.

rows.label: Corporate loan pricing discipline
rows.why: Management will not grow corporate credit at the cost of margins, so the Rs 14,000 crore pipeline converts only if pricing clears, which caps credit growth near the 12-14% guide.

rows.label: Asset quality and recovery target
rows.why: Gross NPA is at 2.17% against a sub-2% FY27 target, and the recovery and upgradation target is Rs 2,000-2,500 crore against about Rs 1,300 crore recovered from written-off accounts in FY26.

rows.label: QIP after AGM approval
rows.why: The Board has approved a QIP, but the launch needs AGM approval and waits for market conditions; there is no plan to raise this quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, ROA path and recoveries, but defensive on the FY27 guidance and the SMA 1 rise to Rs 651 crore from Rs 260 crore, and it left the Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit figure to be clarified offline.

532505|2026-06.headline: UCO Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 8% YoY to Rs 656 crore despite a Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; operating profit up 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore.
532505|2026-06.overview: UCO Bank reported Q1 FY27 with advances up 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore and deposits up 11.28% to Rs 3,32,315 crore. Operating profit rose 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore, helped by Rs 1,018 crore of technical write-off recoveries, of which about Rs 800 crore is from a few accounts management does not expect to recur. Net profit was held to Rs 656 crore by total tax of Rs 1,919 crore, including a one-time Rs 1,237 crore DTA remeasurement on the shift to the new tax regime. Management said most asset-quality and margin metrics were within guidance, and that it would review credit growth guidance only after Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,919 crore (regular ~Rs 625 crore plus one-time DTA Rs 1,237 crore)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -55 bps YoY; NNPA -20 bps YoY
Was 54.06% last year and 52.66% in March; management expects normalised ~50%

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 27.32% YoY. Home loans grew about 20% and vehicle loans about 65% YoY off a low base; management expects roughly 30% vehicle loan growth and 20-25% home loan growth.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 30% YoY; gold loans are cited as a growth driver.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 18.79% YoY; management expects 19-20% growth to continue. ECLGS sanctions stand at Rs 2,150 crore with Rs 1,700 crore disbursed.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 25.27% YoY and make up 64.5% of the book, within the 62-65% guidance; management aims to hold around 65%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 17%, driven by working-capital limit drawdowns. The bank holds no IBPC exposure and is curtailing low-yield PSU and government lending.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth guidance kept at 12-14%, though management says it aims to exceed this; review after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.
NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%, with management aiming to stay slightly above 2.9%; yield on advances expected to hold.
Cost-to-income expected at or around 50% or below for FY27, despite Q1's 37.49%.
ROA of 0.68% annualised in Q1; management sees it near 1% by year-end as the DTA charge is a one-time item.
Credit cost to stay below the 0.75% guidance; deposit repricing largely complete, so cost of funds expected to stay stable.
Expected Credit Loss (ECL): about 60% of the estimated transition requirement already provided as buffer; remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before the ECL regime starts.
capex_capacity: Around 400 branches in West Bengal under five zonal offices; pan-India network of 3,421 branches.
GIFT City branch to open in the next month; all approvals in place and IT implementation in progress.
Omni-channel platform and corporate cash management service said to launch 'very soon'.
GST smart product to rise from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 1 crore ticket size; pre-qualified personal loan journey to be extended to the call centre.
Digital balance sheet of about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June, up from Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 31 STP journeys live; about 70% of fixed deposits now booked digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail loan rates held steady, as they are linked to the repo rate; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026 from 8.75%.
Corporate pricing held steady; management sees demand shifting to loans as bond yields are limited.
Yield on advances was stable, moving only about 3 bps QoQ.
Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management did not quantify the split and sees it as market expansion.
Management reports no stress in any sector; corporate pipelines in infrastructure, renewable energy, transmission, steel and cement.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give full-year guidance on cost of funds, cost of deposits, cost-to-income, RAM and corporate advances, ROE and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds fell to 4.36% as deposit repricing completed; expected to stay stable. NIM 3.05% vs 2.8-2.9% guidance, aim to stay above 2.9%; yield on advances moved about 3 bps. Cost-to-income 37.49% in Q1 but flattered by about Rs 800 crore from few TWO accounts; FY27 target around or below 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank shifting away from IBPC and low-yield government lending, and where is the rebalancing?
qa_highlights.answer: No IBPC exposure now. Growth comes from RAM (above 25%), with retail 27.3%, agri 30%, MSME 19%. Corporate grew about 17%; PSU and government lending being curtailed but is already very limited.

qa_highlights.question: What upside does UCO get from West Bengal's investment climate, given its Kolkata head office?
qa_highlights.answer: About 400 branches in West Bengal across five zonal offices; opportunities seen in steel, railway-related and infrastructure projects. Pan-India network of 3,421 branches.

qa_highlights.question: What would ROA have been under the old tax regime, and what are NIM, ROA and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No figure given; the shift to the new regime is statutory. Management said ROA could have been above 1% excluding the Rs 1,237 crore charge, a rough estimate. ROA of 0.68% now, seen near 1% by year-end; NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Where is competition coming from (PSU, private, NBFC)?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management would not quantify the split and views the market as expanding. Digital balance sheet about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June vs Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 70% of FDs booked digitally.

qa_highlights.question: Should the 12-14% credit growth guidance be raised given 21% actual growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance kept at 12-14% for now; the bank aims to grow above industry and will review only after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS sanction and disbursement, and is any MSME stress visible?
qa_highlights.answer: ECLGS sanctions about Rs 2,150 crore, of which Rs 1,700 crore disbursed, under 50% of eligible customers' loans. SMA-1 book (Rs 1 crore and above) fell to Rs 1,009 crore (0.36%) from Rs 1,125 crore (0.43%) in March; slippage 0.63%.

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provision is already held versus the requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Assessment done on the 1 April transition date; about 60% of the requirement already provided as buffer over and above mandatory provisions. Remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before ECL starts.

qa_highlights.question: Retail loan pricing trends and corporate pricing; was there JP Associates interest recovery in TWO income?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail rates held as they are repo-linked; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026. Corporate pricing held, with demand shifting to loans as bond yields limited. No interest recovery from JP Associates in interest income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ, why did fee income from loan processing fall, and what drove other commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits rose slightly due to reclassification of deposits and borrowings; overall cost of funds still lower. Advance-related fees fell as renewal charges are now recognised on actual basis; other commission rose on PSLC sale of about Rs 2,000 crore earning Rs 55 crore.

risks_watch: Q1 profit is flattered by about Rs 800 crore of TWO recoveries from a few accounts that management does not expect to recur; cost-to-income of 37.49% will normalise upward.
Credit growth running about 21% against 12-14% guidance; guidance review only after Q2 FY27, so the gap may widen or force a revision.
ECL transition: remaining 40% of the requirement to be provided over 4-5 quarters, a future provisioning drag.
Deposit cost rose QoQ due to reclassification; watch whether cost of funds stays at 4.36% after deposit repricing.
Retail vehicle loan growth of about 65% off a low base; management expects about 30% going forward. Concentration in RAM at 64.5% against a 62-65% band.
Corporate book growth driven by working-capital limit drawdowns; sustainability of demand and yield on the corporate book to watch.
ECLGS and MSME stress: management sees none, but the ECLGS 5.0 disbursement pace and SMA-1 trend need monitoring.
key_quotes: So, our cost of funds has come down to 4.36%.
We will review the guidance after the 2 nd Quarter numbers, because in the midterm, we can review.
As of now, we have not seen any risk from any sector.
So we can't quantify as to how much competition I am getting from the private or from the public sector.
532505|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and profitability, while cautious on forward guidance: management kept the 12-14% credit growth and 2.8-2.9% NIM guidance and deferred any revision to after Q2. It was evasive on the ROA under the old tax regime and on the split of competition between private and public sector banks.

rows.why: NIM at 3.05% is above the 2.8-2.9% guidance and management aims to stay above 2.9%, but cost-to-income is flattered by about Rs 800 crore of TWO recoveries (37.49% in Q1) and is guided to around or below 50% for FY27, so reported margin gains are likely to reverse at the cost line.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore against 12-14% guidance, backed by a Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline, retail up 27.32%, agri up 30% and MSME up 18.79%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the bank's CD ratio of 82% and 37.49% cost-to-income suggest no pressing capacity need, and management mentioned no capex plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit growth of 21.18% is well above 12-14% guidance and management aims to exceed it, but it will only review guidance after Q2 FY27, and NIM at 3.05% is above the 2.8-2.9% range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cost-to-income is set to normalise from 37.49% to around 50% once the about Rs 800 crore TWO recoveries stop recurring, and about 40% of the ECL transition requirement still has to be built over 4-5 quarters.

rows.why: Digital balance sheet rose to about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June from Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March (+40%), with 31 STP journeys live and about 70% of FDs booked digitally.

rows.why: About 60% of the ECL transition requirement is already provided; the remaining 40% must be built over the next 4-5 quarters before the ECL regime starts, which is a future provisioning drag.

rows.why: ROA is 0.68% annualised after the Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; management sees it near 1% by year-end and said it could have been above 1% excluding the charge.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth (21% advances), asset quality (GNPA 2.08%, credit cost 0.39%) and profitability, but held the 12-14% credit growth and 2.8-2.9% NIM guidance and deferred revisions to after Q2; it was evasive on ROA under the old tax regime and on the private versus PSU competition

532505|2026-09.headline: UCO Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 26.77% YoY to Rs 786 crore; advances grew 24.70%, well above the 12-14% guidance.
532505|2026-09.overview: UCO Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 786 crore, up 26.77% YoY from Rs 620 crore, with operating profit of Rs 1,872 crore (up 16.04%). Global advances grew 24.70% to Rs 2,87,690 crore, while deposits grew 14.36% to Rs 3,49,590 crore and CASA ratio slipped to 36.77%. Gross NPA fell 60 bps YoY to 1.96% and net NPA to 0.18%, both within guidance. Management said the quarter's slippage rise was mainly agriculture crop-loan marking done half-yearly in September, and that the June quarter had a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery that did not recur.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -60 bps YoY; NNPA -25 bps YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 30.23% YoY; housing loan growth above 20% YoY with average home-loan ticket up from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 29.59% YoY; agri slippages rose to Rs 205 crore in Q2 from Rs 73 crore in Q1, but were below Rs 238 crore a year ago.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 20.32% YoY; management sees scope for more growth here.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; sanctioned but undisbursed corporate pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore.

segments.name: RAM portfolio
segments.commentary: RAM portfolio is Rs 1,68,736 crore, up 26.92% YoY, and its share of advances has crossed 65% against the 62-65% guidance.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Hong Kong and Singapore branches are operating; GIFT City IBU opened in Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guidance of 12-14% for FY27 was kept; management said it aims to grow above guidance but will not revise it mid-year.
Deposit growth guidance of 10-12% was exceeded (actual 14%+).
GNPA guidance is below 2% by 31 March 2027; already at 1.96%.
Net NPA guidance is below 0.25% for the year; already at 0.18%.
Global NIM guidance of 2.80-2.90% was exceeded (3.00%); management expects to sustain NIM above guidance with repo pass-through.
Credit cost guidance is below 0.75% for FY27; Q2 is 0.65%.
Cost-to-income expected to be around 50% for the full year and possibly below 50% next year.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027 estimated at about Rs 3,200 crore+ requirement; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 3,439 after adding 27 branches in the quarter; business per branch Rs 185 crore vs Rs 161 crore a year ago.
Business per employee Rs 30 crore vs Rs 25 crore a year ago.
GIFT City IBU opened in Q2; three international branches (Hong Kong, Singapore, GIFT City).
Digital business balance sheet under Project Parivartan above Rs 48,000 crore as of 30 September 2026.
Seven processes automated via RPA; digital marketing solution onboarded; customer 360-degree portal rolled out in branches.
Recruitment of specialist officers (data analysts, CAs, trade finance officers) in FY27; further recruitment of professional officers and customer service associates planned.
demand_pricing: Advances growth came from all segments; RAM share has crossed 65%, and management expects it to hold around 65% with corporate growth also continuing.
Corporate sanctioned pipeline of about Rs 10,000 crore is undisbursed; disbursement depends on corporates' acceptance of lending rates and capex plans.
About 66% of advances are linked to external benchmark (repo/EBLR); a 25 bps repo hike was passed on immediately to these loans.
Deposit rates unchanged for now; management said no immediate need to raise term deposit rates, with any hike applying only to new deposits and renewals.
Gold loan yield is about 9% (slightly below) and unchanged QoQ.
Housing loan growth above 20% YoY from both volume and ticket size; second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are small.
Domestic yield on advances 8.11%; global yield 7.79%; cost of funds 4.44%, up slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Recoveries from written-off accounts fell to Rs 301 crore from Rs 1,018 crore; is this a normalised rate, and what is the treasury outlook given rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the June quarter included a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery from one large account; excluding it, June recovery was about Rs 233 crore, so Rs 301 crore is the normalised run-rate. On treasury, management said yield hardening pressures profitability, but ~66% of advances are repo/EBLR-linked, so NII gains should offset treasury losses; FVTPL book is small.

qa_highlights.question: Slippages rose from Rs 428 crore to Rs 538 crore and SMA-1 rose from Rs 228 crore to Rs 437 crore; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were Rs 549 crore in the quarter per management; the rise is mainly half-yearly crop-loan agriculture marking in September. SMA-1 and SMA-2 (Rs 1 crore and above) stood at 0.42% vs 0.77% a year ago, with a QoQ uptick described as manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates be raised, and with what lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate need to raise deposit rates; current term deposit rates maintained. Any hike would apply only to new deposits and renewals, decided later based on deposit requirement.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change in corporate stance, and will the bank raise its credit growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; RAM share crossed 65% (guidance 62-65%) and is expected to hold around 65%. Corporate sanctioned but undisbursed pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore, dependent on lending rates and capex. Guidance of 12-14% kept; management aims to exceed it but will not revise mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition estimate for 1 April 2027 and has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition requirement estimated at about Rs 2,500 crore in one answer and Rs 3,200 crore-plus in another; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions, including COVID provisions of Rs 530 crore, extra provisions of Rs 341 crore and about Rs 1,600 crore ECL-specific. Estimate not materially changed from three months earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan yield and how is it trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan yield is around 9%, slightly below; no change QoQ as no rate changes were made. Any EBLR-linked gold loans will reprice with the repo hike.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating expenses rise by about Rs 160 crore, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is normal, reflecting IT investment, physical infrastructure and network expansion, plus a lag in opex growth in earlier quarters; expected to stay in a similar range, depending on transaction volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income outlook for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost was 0.65% vs guidance below 0.75%, with ECL provisioning of Rs 570 crore in the quarter and accelerated NPA provisioning to bring NNPA to 0.18%. Cost-to-income was 50.39% (about 45% excluding the June one-off effect); expected around 50% for FY27 and possibly below 50% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Second-hand car loan growth and yield, and housing ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are a small share of car loans; management will work out numbers. Average home-loan ticket rose from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh, with growth from both volume and ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Is NII growth enough to offset treasury stress, and what NIM is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said repo-linked NII growth (about 66% of advances) would more than offset treasury stress, and that FVTPL exposure is small. Global NIM was 3.00% and domestic 3.19%, against guidance of 2.80-2.90%; management expects to sustain NIM above guidance.

risks_watch: Treasury losses from hardening yields; FVTPL book is small but MTM impact depends on the yield path and any further RBI repo action.
Asset quality: quarterly slippage of Rs 549 crore (0.85%), with agri slippage Rs 205 crore and SMA-1/2 up QoQ to Rs 437 crore; watch whether the September agri marking reverses or persists in March.
Recovery from written-off accounts normalising at about Rs 300 crore per quarter, down from the Rs 1,018 crore a year ago, as large accounts are largely resolved.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027: requirement of about Rs 2,500-3,200 crore plus, with Rs 2,500 crore already provided; any further top-up depends on profitability.
Deposit mobilisation: CASA ratio slipped to 36.77% and deposit rates are unchanged, while advances growth of 24.70% far exceeds 10-12% deposit guidance.
Corporate growth conversion: Rs 10,000 crore sanctioned corporate pipeline remains undisbursed and depends on lending rates and capex; watch the RAM-share cap near 65%.
key_quotes: So, this is the normal recovery, and this quarter we don’t have any such big recovery account, which was a one-off in the last quarter.

532509|2026-06.headline: Suprajit Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to INR1,070 crore and operational EBITDA 57% to INR129 crore, while standalone EBITDA was flat at INR60 crore.

Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM) drove the gain, with EBITDA margin rising from 5.8% to 12.6% after the global restructuring. Standalone margins were squeezed by raw material and wage inflation in ICM (margin ~15% to ~13%) and by delayed price pass-through in PLE (margin 6.7%, down 2.8pp); management calls both timing issues and expects recovery in Q2-Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance from the 25 May 2026 release.

qa_highlights.answer: Last year's gains came from large favourable currency moves on loans, debtors/creditors and forward covers, plus a Morocco subsidy not repeated. Currency has been stable since March, so the Q1 figure is much smaller.

rows.label: PFS divestment via SBI Capital
