532525|2026-03.headline: Bank of Maharashtra FY26: net profit INR7,019 crore (+27% YoY), full-year NIM 3.91%, ROA 1.86%, all guidance met; FY27 ROA guidance 1.80%.
532525|2026-03.overview: Management reported that all FY26 guidance metrics were met, several with headroom, with total business up 17% and advances up 22% YoY. Gross NPA fell 29 bps to 1.45% and net NPA to 0.13%, while operating profit rose 16% to INR10,826 crore. Management created an INR200 crore "global geopolitical uncertainties" provision in Q4 as a buffer against the West Asia crisis, and said stress is not yet visible in MSME. Non-interest income was weak (2.51% growth) due to a one-time INR290 crore MTM hit from the RRB amalgamation. FY27 guidance was issued across 18-19 parameters, with ROA lifted to 1.80%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew 32% YoY; home loans +29%, vehicle loans +56%, gold loans +53% to INR24,000 crore, of which about INR5,000 crore is co-lent with NBFCs. Retail slippages in Q4 were about INR100 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book grew 22% YoY, with RAM split 63:37 (retail/agri/MSME vs corporate). Corporate reported no slippages in Q4; INR72,000 crore sanctioned in FY26 with INR34,500 crore undisbursed.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME grew 11% YoY (about INR6,000 crore added per management); MSME NPA fell to 1.54%. Q4 MSME slippages were about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri grew 13% YoY; agri NPA was 7.72% (about INR3,100 crore). Q4 agri slippages were about INR300 crore.

segments.name: GIFT City IBU
segments.commentary: Overseas advances rose to INR6,142 crore from INR3,517 crore (2% of book). Management said the IBU turned profitable in March after covering all overheads; 650 million USD booked against a 1 billion USD 12-month aspiration.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: AFS reserve swung from +INR175 crore in Q3 to -INR362 crore at 31 March; FVTPL MTM gain of about INR40-45 crore booked.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total business growth 16-17%; advances 18%; deposits 14-15%; CASA around 50%.
RAM growth 18% with RAM corporate mix at 60:40 (+/-2%); non-interest income growth 10%; NII growth 15%.
FY27 NIM guidance 3.75%; cost to income below 40%; ROA 1.80%; ROE 20% or more.
GNPA within 2%, NNPA within 0.25%, slippage below 1%, credit cost around 1%, PCR around 98%, CRAR maintained at 18%.
Management expects FY27 tax at about 10% of PBT (OP tax rate 13-14%), with PBT-basis tax about 18-20%, after unabsorbed losses of about INR1,200-1,300 crore were used up in Q1.
Debt waiver: about INR2,000 crore expected (INR917 crore overdue + INR1,067 crore NPA eligible KCC accounts), with approval expected Q2 to Q3 FY27; agri NPA could fall to about 5.33%.
capex_capacity: Project 321: 321 new branches in the first 3-year phase, 183 functional to date; Board has approved 1,000 branches over 5 years.
GIFT City IBU: first business booked September 2025; retail products planned for H2 FY27.
PLI for Scale 4 and above not yet released; 100% provision made, release pending discussions.
demand_pricing: Management expects West Asia crisis impact to show from Q2 FY27 rather than Q1, with Brent above USD115 cited as a risk; no MSME stress seen as of March.
Q4 SMA-1 was INR241 crore and SMA-2 INR56 crore as of 31 March (per analyst).
Management said it would price risk more carefully where risk rises, but gave no specific pricing action.
Pool/assignment book of about INR14,000 crore is largely lent to AA/AAA NBFCs; security cover is low as it is pool-based.
Gold co-lending slowed after RBI's CLM1 guidelines from 1 January 2026; fresh underwriting resumed in early March, with 9 NBFC co-lending partners signed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the West Asia war affect corporate and MSME accounts from April onward, and what stress is visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no stress was visible in March and MSME NPA fell to 1.54%, but impact is expected from Q2 FY27 and depends on how long the crisis lasts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the special provision fall to INR1,010 crore from INR1,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the COVID buffer was released, and a new INR200 crore global geopolitical uncertainties provision was built in Q4, with no regulatory prescription behind it.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time non-interest income drag?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time INR290 crore MTM provision was taken on investments in the RRB (Vidharbha Konkan Gramin Bank) that was amalgamated into a single Maharashtra RRB, with the bank as sponsor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net worth fall QoQ and gold loans drop about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth fell due to AFS reserve movement and dividends (interim 10% plus final 12%, about INR1,692 crore total). Gold loans dropped because fresh underwriting paused during the shift from CLM2 to CLM1 co-lending; underwriting resumed in early March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank is on the normal tax rate from Q2 FY26, with OP tax at 13-14%. FY27 PBT-basis tax is expected around 18-20%, and the call gave a 10% figure for the tax on PBT in the same answer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split of Q4 slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail about INR100 crore, agri about INR300 crore, MSME about INR400 crore, and corporate nil.

risks_watch: West Asia / crude-driven stress in MSME and corporate books from Q2 FY27; a 1.2% to 2% geopolitical provision top-up is open.
Timing and size of the state KCC debt waiver (about INR2,000 crore); the scheme is not yet approved.
Tax-rate normalisation to about 25% creates an earnings headwind; management guided FY27 PBT-basis tax at 18-20%, but the figures given on the call are inconsistent.
Non-interest income growth (2.51% in FY26) versus 10% target; a fee-income push is planned for FY27.
Gold co-lending volume recovery after CLM1 transition; the book fell about 17% QoQ.
Pending PLI payout for Scale 4 and above, and the NCLT recovery pipeline (about INR7,500 crore in NCLT).
532525|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance, with management calling the targets "sacrosanct". Cautious and somewhat evasive on the West Asia impact, saying the full effect cannot yet be gauged and that the crisis is not over.
key_quotes: we have been able to meet all the guidance and at some of the places with a decent margin above the guidance that was shared in the beginning of the year.
These are sacrosanct numbers for us. We will be achieving itself.
So we can only hope that the crisis resolves and what damage must have happened, the impact, how fast it can be replaced is also needs to be seen.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 NIM was 3.91% against FY27 NIM guidance of 3.75%, so management is guiding a ~16 bps compression, and credit cost is guided around 1% against a much lower FY26 run-rate.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: over 5 years, with 183 of 321 Project 321 branches already f
rows.why: Board approved 1,000 branches over 5 years and 321 in the first 3-year phase, with 183 functional to date (57%), so branch rollout continues through the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 guidance is advances +18%, deposits +14-15%, total business +16-17%, against FY26 advances +22% and total business +17%, backed by 9 NBFC co-lending partners and gold co-lending restarting.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; utilisation is not disclosed for a bank, and branch expansion is already approved under Project 321.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 delivered ROA 1.86% against 1.75% guidance and NIM 3.91% against 3.75%, but FY27 guidance was set at roughly the same bar, with ROA raised only 5 bps to 1.80%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects the West Asia crisis to hit from Q2 FY27 with Brent above USD115 cited as a risk, a geopolitical provision top-up of 1.2-2% is open, and tax normalises to about 18-20% on PBT.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: GIFT City IBU plans retail products for H2 FY27 after turning profitable in March with USD650 million booked against a USD1 billion 12-month aspiration.

rows.label: Risk-based repricing if stress rises
rows.why: Management said it would price risk more carefully where risk rises but gave no specific action, with Q4 slippages of about INR800 crore across retail, agri and MSME (corporate nil).

rows.label: State KCC debt waiver of about INR2,000 crore
rows.why: The waiver covers INR917 crore overdue plus INR1,067 crore NPA eligible KCC accounts, with approval expected Q2-Q3 FY27, and agri NPA could fall to about 5.33% from 7.72%.

rows.label: PLI payout for Scale 4 and above
rows.why: 100% provision is already made, but release is pending discussions, so any release would be an upside to other income with no date given.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance (targets called sacrosanct) but cautious and somewhat evasive on West Asia impact, which it said cannot yet be gauged; analysts pressed on tax-rate inconsistency, the 10% vs 18-20% PBT tax figures, and the gold book's 17% QoQ drop.

532525|2026-06.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q1 FY27: net profit up 27% YoY to INR2,020 crore, advances up 27%, NIM 3.85%, all guidance parameters beaten.
532525|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026) with total business up 19% YoY, advances up 27% and deposits up 13%, against guidance of 16-17%, 18% and 14% respectively. Operating profit rose 21% YoY to INR3,117 crore and net profit rose 27% to INR2,020 crore. Asset quality held: gross NPA flat QoQ at 1.45%, net NPA 0.13%, credit cost 0.99%. Management kept its FY27 guidance unchanged despite the faster growth, and flagged the NIM (3.85%, down 10 bps YoY) and the rising cost of deposits QoQ as the points to watch.

financial_highlights.value: INR1,04,000 crore added in past year

financial_highlights.change: Guidance 14%; no CDs raised in Q1
vs INR33 crore in March quarter; includes one-time SR of INR104 crore

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 25% YoY; retail gross NPA 0.34% per management, with home loan sanctions in the past 12 months 80% from CIBIL 750+ borrowers.

segments.name: Agri
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 30% YoY; agri gross NPA 7.58%, down from about 9% a couple of quarters back.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 23% YoY; MSME gross NPA 1.60%, and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 30% YoY, up from 17-18% in the prior four quarters; RAM:corporate mix at 63:37.

segments.name: IBU (GIFT City)
segments.commentary: IBU book about INR8,200 crore, contributing about 3 points of the 27% advances growth; sanctions of $965 million; global yield 8.57% vs domestic 8.66%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth guidance kept at 18%, despite Q1 growth of 27%; management said it would not revisit the number.
NIM guidance of 3.75% maintained; management said no further rate cuts are now expected and a rate hike may come.
Cost-to-income guided below 40%; Q1 running at about 36-38%.
Credit cost guided below 1%; Q1 at 0.99%.
Gross NPA guided below 2% and net NPA below 0.25%; Q1 at 1.45% and 0.13%.
Equity raise of INR5,000 crore planned this FY, with Board, shareholder and RBI approvals in place; awaiting government approval.
Tax rate guided at 12-13% on operating-profit basis and 16-17% on PBT basis.
Debt waiver scheme (under formulation): eligible portfolio about INR3,500 crore; expected to be settled within FY27; maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions.
ECL: about INR125 crore per quarter of provisioning needed through March 2031, to be charged against net worth per RBI's final guidelines rather than P&L.
capex_capacity: Opening about 200 new branches a year under a 5-year expansion plan; new branches are staffed from day one.
Staff strength about INR17,500 crore (figure as stated) vs about INR13,000 crore two years ago; recruitment to continue.
Mobile banking app active registered users up from 2.75 lakh (old version) to over 14 lakh.
Around 40% of branches are in rural areas.
LCR average 118% vs terminal LCR 114%; management targets a 115-120% band.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth of 13% with no CDs raised in Q1; PSB average deposit growth 11% and private banks 14%, per management.
Domestic CD ratio 86%; 81.99% after including about INR19,000 crore of refinance (blended cost 6-6.5%).
Repo-linked share of loan book 53%, MCLR-linked 44%; MCLR was raised in the last two ALCO reviews and will reset gradually over the next year.
5-year FCNR deposit offered at 6.60%, positioned against the best PSB offers.
ECLGS: eligible portfolio INR6,700 crore, sanctions INR4,500 crore (65%), disbursed INR3,560 crore (82% of sanctions); MSME INR2,700 crore, corporate INR400 crore.
Retail term deposit growth 16% vs total deposits 13%; management attributes the QoQ rise in deposit cost to special retail TD schemes.
Gold loans about INR13,000 crore, up 75% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII (14.5%) lag advances growth (27%), and would management revisit the 18% loan growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept NII guidance of 15% and NIM of 3.75%, citing a branch-level profitability dashboard and tighter pricing. It said it would keep the 18% advances guidance, with IBU contributing 3 points of the 27% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did current account balances fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it not a major concern: the decline is about 2,500-3,000 bps of the current account book, and CASA still grew 9% YoY, adding INR14,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Agri provisions and debt waiver impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Eligible portfolio INR3,500 crore; government receivable INR2,750 crore; maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions. Settlement expected within FY27, plus INR50,000 per farmer incentive into SB accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax rate is about 12-13% on an operating-profit basis and 16-17% on a PBT basis, aided by rural advances (about 40% of branches rural), bad-debt write-off benefits and DTA.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of 8-9% vs balance sheet growth above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost growth is driven by staffing new branches from day one; cost-to-income is 36-38% and guided below 40%. Branches opened three or more years ago have all turned profitable, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did treasury profit jump to INR266 crore and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury included a one-time SR of INR104 crore, with part of the payment possibly coming in later quarters; no treasury profit targets are set.

qa_highlights.question: SMA-2 jump from INR56 crore to INR208 crore; is MSME stress rising?
qa_highlights.answer: A single government entity account of INR87 crore moved into SMA-2 and is expected to regularise. SMA-1+2 stands at 1.34%, down 5 bps YoY.

risks_watch: Cost of deposits rose 5 bps QoQ to 4.38% and retail term deposits are growing faster than total deposits; watch the QoQ trend.
Thin CASA growth in Q1 (current account balances fell sharply QoQ) and reliance on refinance (about INR19,000 crore) and possible CDs as deposit growth lags loan growth.
Agri gross NPA at 7.58% and the debt-waiver haircut timing; the Rs 87 crore government account in SMA-2 needs to regularise.
Agri and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ (MSME 1.60%); watch for stress from geopolitical conditions (West Asia).
NIM pressure from MCLR resets, with the yield on advances down 71 bps YoY to 8.57% globally; the rate-hike benefit depends on repo-linked share at 53%.
Equity raise of INR5,000 crore pending government approval; treasury gains include a one-time item of INR104 crore.
ECL provisioning of about INR125 crore per quarter through March 2031 against net worth.
532525|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and asset quality, with repeated emphasis on keeping guidance unchanged. Management was evasive on the NII-versus-loan-growth gap and the cost-of-deposit trajectory, answering both with qualitative points rather than numbers.
key_quotes: We are committed to the guidance numbers that we have shared.
Gross NPA is maintained at the March level 1.45% against our guidance of maintaining it below 2%.
So refinance, again, why we decided not to go for high-cost bulk deposits, the blended cost that we have experienced while we go for refinance is in the range of 6% to 6.5%.
The mantra is very clear. It has to be a profitable growth and no compromise on the quality.

rows.why: Advances grew 27% YoY (INR65,000 crore added) against FY27 guidance of 18%, and deposits grew 13% vs 14% guidance; IBU contributes about 3 points of growth and gold loans are up 75% YoY to about INR13,000 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex utilisation figure disclosed; the INR5,000 crore equity raise (Board, shareholder and RBI approvals in place, awaiting government nod) funds growth but is not a capex plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management kept the 18% advances guidance despite Q1 growth of 27% and said it will not revisit the number; NII guidance kept at 15% after NII grew only 14.5%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch discussed; only a 5-year FCNR deposit at 6.60% was mentioned as an existing offer.

rows.label: Equity raise of INR5,000 crore this FY
rows.why: Board, shareholder and RBI approvals are in place and only government approval is pending, against advances growing 27% and CRAR at 18.64%.

rows.label: Debt waiver scheme settlement
rows.why: Eligible portfolio about INR3,500 crore with maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions, so the P&L hit is largely absorbed.

rows.label: ECL provisioning charged to net worth
rows.why: About INR125 crore per quarter of provisioning is charged against net worth per RBI's final guidelines rather than the P&L.

tone.note: Management was confident on loan growth, asset quality and keeping guidance unchanged, but evasive on the NII-versus-loan-growth gap and the cost-of-deposit trajectory; analysts pressed on those points.

532525|2026-09.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q2 FY27: business up 25% YoY, advances up 30%, ROE 26.98%, GNPA down 47 bps to 1.25%.
532525|2026-09.overview: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics were met in Q2, with business crossing INR7 lakh crore and advances growing 30% YoY (23% ex-IBU). Operating profit rose 31% and net profit 41% YoY, lifting ROE 440 bps to 26.98% and NIM 12 bps to 3.97%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.25% and NNPA at 0.12%, helped by write-off recoveries and lower NPA provisions, while INR500 crore of ECL provisions was booked in the standard asset line. Cost of deposits fell 4 bps YoY to 4.38%, though management acknowledged a QoQ rise tied to FCNR(B) and OFCB raises of about $1.65 billion.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of deposits / cost of funds

segments.name: Advances / large credit
segments.commentary: Large credit up 38% YoY to INR36,000 crore, of which INR18,000 crore from GIFT City IBU and INR18,000 crore domestic (19% growth). Domestic credit ex-IBU grew 23%, with RAM, retail, agri and MSME each above 20%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 22% YoY, or 19% ex-FCNR(B); CASA up 12% YoY with INR19,000 crore CASA added over the last FY.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book INR44,000 crore, up 34% YoY (about INR11,000 crore). Agri gold loans INR18,600 crore vs INR6,500 crore in Sep-25; agri stress down 35 bps to 3.51%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loan outstanding INR33,000 crore; MSME gold loan about INR2,000 crore. Retail gold declined QoQ as loans were reclassified to agri/MSME under RBI norms.

guidance_outlook: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics across growth, profitability, asset quality and capital were met in H1.
Domestic credit guidance is 18%; management sees no challenge sustaining above 18% with INR23,000 crore pipeline and INR10,000 crore expected to be disbursed by March 2027.
Recovery target from written-off accounts of INR1,300-1,500 crore annually for the next 4-5 years; FY27 recovery so far INR1,023 crore.
ECL: total assessed requirement INR2,500 crore over 4 years; INR750 crore already provided (INR250 crore earlier plus INR500 crore in Q2), which management says covers more than 1 year.
Maharashtra debt-waiver government receivable (about INR2,700 crore of eligible INR3,500 crore): about INR1,200 crore received to 30 Sep; SLBC timeline for balance is 31 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: about 200 branches planned annually; 77 branches made functional in H1 FY27.
Employee strength raised to 17,500 from about 13,000 two years earlier, driven by branch expansion and specialist hiring (treasury, IBU, IT).
IT budget: INR900 crore in FY25 and INR985 crore in FY26, with a large share on cyber security.
Pipeline sector mix: infra power about 18%, roads/HAM about 12%, renewables about 10%, metals and others about 10%; data centres cited as a niche growth area.
demand_pricing: Credit growth ex-IBU of 23% YoY; IBU book INR18,500 crore funded partly by about $560 million of FCNR(B) leverage. The FCNR(B) special window has closed.
Repricing: management raised rates on several MCLR-linked state PSU facilities (several thousand crore, about 25 bps on some) in Q1, contributing to NIM gains.
Global yield on advances 8.86%, domestic 9.02%; IBU yield not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan pricing tiers: agri lowest, MSME about 50 bps higher, non-priority retail highest.
EBLR-linked loans are 47% of the loan book.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning: standard/restructured provisions rose to INR603 crore from INR76 crore; what is the ECL preparedness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPA provisions fell from INR580 crore a year ago to INR120 crore this quarter, helped by recoveries. Standard-asset provisions rose to INR603 crore including INR500 crore of ECL; total ECL assessed at INR2,500 crore over 4 years, with INR750 crore already provided.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth sustain after the FCNR window closes, and will write-off recoveries continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IBU leverage was about $560 million from FCNR(B) and the window is closed; domestic growth is 23% and the INR23,000 crore pipeline supports growth above the 18% guidance. Write-off recovery target is INR1,300-1,500 crore a year for 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FCNR(B) is fixed at 6.51%, OFCB at 6.11%, and 1-year CDs at about 7.75-7.9%. About $1.65 billion was raised via FCNR(B) and OFCB against a $1.5 billion plan, with 5-year fixed-cost borrowings and a 3x oversubscribed MTN issue; YoY cost of deposits fell 4 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 30 bps QoQ rise in yield on advances despite IBU mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to repricing of MCLR-linked state PSU accounts (about 25 bps on several thousand crore), a one-off write-off recovery impact of about 2-3 bps on NIM, and a 3-4 bps ITR refund. Only INR30 crore of the INR125 crore recovery has gone to interest income so far.

qa_highlights.question: Drought exposure and restructuring under SLBC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no visible agri stress; special SLBC restructuring applies at 33-50% crop loss (1-year moratorium, up to 3-year tenor) and above 50% loss (5-year tenor including 1-year moratorium). Farmer applications open till February 2027; past experience suggests 10-15% take-up, with about 5% provisioning on the restructured amount.

qa_highlights.question: Agri gold and retail gold trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri gold loans rose to INR18,600 crore from INR6,500 crore YoY. Retail gold declined QoQ because loans were reclassified to MSME/agri under RBI norms; total gold outstanding INR33,000 crore and MSME gold about INR2,000 crore.

risks_watch: Drought and El Nino: Maharashtra drought could trigger SLBC restructuring; management estimates 10-15% take-up and says no visible stress yet.
ECL transition: INR2,500 crore total assessed; management said the number may fall; surplus provisions of INR1,600-1,800 crore (COVID, global uncertainties INR200 crore) can be used.
Cost of deposits: QoQ increase from high-cost FCNR(B)/OFCB/CD raises; FY28 impact on margin depends on deployment.
Maharashtra debt-waiver balance of about INR1,500 crore receivable; management does not count on it and timing depends on state process (deadline 31 March 2027).
Pace of IBU growth after the FCNR(B) window closed; IBU yield not disclosed.
Cyber and DPDP compliance; management deferred detailed answer.

So I don't see a challenge at all to maintain a pace above our guidance of 18% in credit in future also.

532527|2026-03.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 1,216.78 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.1%, and management guides to further improvement in FY27.
532527|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 1,216.78 crore, up 28% YoY and 11% QoQ, with EBITDA excluding other income of Rs 208.19 crore (up 111% YoY, 27% QoQ) and margin of 17.1%. Profit before tax was Rs 64.33 crore, held back by about Rs 10.4 crore of consolidation effects (Rs 5.9 crore subsidiary profit elimination and Rs 4.5 crore Mexico subsidiary loss). FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 4,238 crore (up 5%) and EBITDA Rs 642.70 crore (up 15%), while PBT fell 24% to Rs 112.58 crore versus Rs 148.79 crore (excluding exceptional items) in FY25. Q4 orders won totalled Rs 594 crore over four years, split 56% automotive and 44% non-automotive.

segments.commentary: Rail wheel JV expected to start production by Q1 FY27, with 230,000-wheel capacity and a railway offtake guarantee of about 40,000 wheels in FY27 for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore.

Domestic auto demand was strong after the September GST rate cut, with M&HCV, tractors and PVs reporting double-digit wholesale growth in Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: The figure covers forgings and castings together. Management expects 85-90% casting utilisation over the year, with margins of about 15-16% and Rs 400-500 crore of additional revenue. Management declined to put a figure on the incremental revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wheelset JV's contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Production starts by Q1 FY27 and about 40,000 wheels are expected in FY27 under the railway offtake guarantee, for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore. Pricing is still being reset for two years of inflation.

532527|2026-06.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 1,217 crore (+19.8% YoY), PAT Rs 46.9 crore (~4x YoY), EBITDA margin 17.96%.

EBITDA margin rose to 17.96% from 17.11% in Q4, while management said energy and shipping costs were not fully passed on. Net debt fell about Rs 100 crore QoQ to around Rs 1,900 crore, and management reiterated a Rs 500 crore leverage reduction target for FY27. Management guided to strong export growth, a wheels JV and rail trial ramp-up, and a multi-year non-ferrous (aluminium, titanium, Inconel) push.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Won Rs 15 crore of Metro orders from Indian Railways. Rail wheel JV (RKTR) trial production has started; first 300 sample wheels to be submitted in August.

Exports expected at about 35% of consolidated revenue for FY27 and growth of 'almost 20% plus' in exports; management called it possibly the highest export revenue ever.

FY27 capex guidance around Rs 350 crore, plus Rs 20-30 crore further investment into the rail wheel JV.

capex_capacity: Majority of strategic capex is complete; focus shifted to utilisation and asset turn. Management cited asset turn of 2.5x on ~Rs 3,700 crore net block implying ~Rs 9,000 crore sales at 100% utilisation, though it said 75-80% is the practical ceiling.
Ring rolling capacity at 127% utilisation; management said no plans to add ring rolling capacity and expects peak utilisation for two to three years.

Casting plant capitalised in Q4 FY26; integration substantially complete and capacity ramp-up expected over the next three quarters.
Aluminium forging capability in place; Inconel/titanium capex limited to about Rs 10-20 crore for heating arrangements.
Wheel JV: 80,000 confirmed Railway wheel order plus about 25,000 wheels from JV partners (~1,10,000 total), covering production until end FY28. Major new capex to be announced only by end FY28.
demand_pricing: Management described the order book as strong, with healthy domestic demand, and expects the next half (after monsoon, around September) to be exciting domestically.
Export growth driven by Europe and North America, with new orders from existing and new customers; customer names not disclosed.
Steel is passed through with a one-quarter lag; gas, energy and shipping costs are not fully passed on. No hedging available for steel.
Currency is passed through every quarter on all contracts, per management, so rupee depreciation (1-1.5% in quarter) gives no net benefit.

Domestic realisation rose QoQ on better mix, higher utilisation and product choice. Casting realisations declined QoQ due to one-off components run during capacity ramp-up; management expects recovery.
Management said it would not guide on profitability or a full-year margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin rise only 85 bps QoQ when gross margin rose ~535 bps? Is it only price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied it was only price, citing product mix. It said energy and shipping costs have not been passed on, which limited EBITDA margin gains; improvement should follow once costs stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Are there target ROCEs for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 ROCE of 12-15% and FY28 target of 20%, with ROCE returning to historical levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 278 crore auto order be domestic or export?
qa_highlights.answer: Entirely domestic: ~82% passenger vehicle and ~18% two-wheeler; the two-wheeler business is crankshafts from the Gurugram machining facility. Management says the PV order is EV, which is domestic-brand supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV vs ICE mix in passenger vehicles and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: PV order book is about 50:50 ICE and EV. Export sales have so far been more EV-led, with bulk ICE supply starting.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt fall to Rs 1,000 crore in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No target given; management said it is not aiming for a zero-debt company but will keep leverage under check while growing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the Rs 8,000 crore turnover target?
qa_highlights.answer: Target moved to FY29 (one year later), implying 22-25% CAGR from last year's turnover of about Rs 4,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 margin improving given market conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: No improvement in market conditions yet. Management said energy and shipping costs will not moderate unless geopolitical issues are resolved.

532528|2026-06.headline: Datamatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore, with EBITDA margin up 343 bps to 19.7%.
532528|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 101.1 crore at a 19.7% margin, with the margin gain attributed to cost discipline and operational excellence. Digital Operations drove growth (revenue up 16.1%, EBIT margin 19.3%), while Digital Technologies grew 6.1% at an 8.9% EBIT margin and Digital Experiences declined 5.3%. Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance, citing softness from geopolitical uncertainty, and said about 60% of FY27 deals won were AI-led or AI-driven. The TNQTech integration into Lumina Datamatics was completed in the quarter, and a INR 200 crore TNQTech payout was made in Q1.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 64 crore, down 5.3% YoY; EBIT margin 11.7%. Management said several good-sized deals were signed this year and the practice is seeing an upswing.

532531|2026-03.headline: Strides FY26 revenue rose 6.4% to INR48,587 mn and EBITDA 15% to INR925 crore at 19% margin; Q4 US revenue weak at $70 mn as flu season failed to materialise.
532531|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 6.4% YoY to INR48,587 mn, held back by a weak second-half US flu season and donor-funding pressure in access markets; management says underlying growth was about 10% excluding access markets. Ex-US revenue grew 21% and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, while EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 19% for the year. Q4 EBITDA rose 10% YoY to INR240 crore (18.1% margin), with about INR20 crore of logistics and air-freight cost pressure. Operational PAT crossed INR500 crore for the first time at INR518 crore, and the Board recommended a dividend of INR5 per share.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue $284 mn and Q4 $70 mn, hit by a weak second-half flu season; 6 launches in the year, 9 products exited, and some molecules faced higher competition, with leading positions in 37 of 70 products. Controlled substances from the Chestnut Ridge ANDA acquisition are in their first full year, with 4 products launched and quota allocations below expectations.

segments.name: Ex-US (total)
segments.commentary: Grew 21% in FY26 and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, with a 3-year CAGR of about 19%. Quarterly ex-US revenue rose from about $40 mn in Q1 FY24 to about $70 mn in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Other regulated markets (ORM)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue rose from about $31 mn in Q1 FY24 to a $52 mn exit run rate in Q4 FY26, with traction in Europe, UK, Australia and the Nordics.

segments.name: Africa / growth markets
segments.commentary: Focus is shifting toward branded business, with Francophone Africa growing faster than the underlying market. The Sandoz product acquisition (announced Feb 2026) is expected to contribute from H2 FY27 and to lift the branded portfolio more than 1.5x.

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration: EBITDA margin upwards of 20% and gross margin in the 58%-60% range; Q&A reiterated a 18%-20% margin range for the near term.
US aspiration of $375-400 mn by FY28, described as a full-year FY28 target rather than an exit run rate; management said about 8 quarters remain.
Sequential growth expected from Q4 to Q1 FY27; Q4 sequential growth stated at 11% (14% excluding institutional business).
US growth expected to pick up from H2 FY27; FY26 seasonality was roughly 50:50 H1:H2 versus the usual 45:55.

Sandoz portfolio expected to contribute from H2 FY27; R&D spend to be $20-25 mn a year over the next 2 years; tangible and intangible investment run rate about INR300 crore; nasal sprays, patches and films expected to contribute mainly from FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: FY26 total investment INR418 crore: INR236 crore tangible (including nasal spray capacity, ex-US capacity and a UK office) and INR182 crore intangible (global product rights and SAP HANA ERP upgrade).
Tangible capex is nearly complete beyond maintenance; a run rate of about INR300 crore across tangible and intangible is expected, including possible acquisitions of global rights.
Capacity sufficient for the next 2 years; no major additional capacity needed in the next 1-2 years apart from growth capex.
Chestnut Ridge facility (acquired from Endo) is capable of manufacturing nasal sprays and controlled substances; second nasal spray filed in May 2026, with commercialisation about 12 months away.
Patches and thin films: filing expected in 12-18 months.
demand_pricing: US flu-season demand did not recover in H2 as it had in prior years, and wholesaler discipline also contributed.
Marginal US pricing pressure, offset by COGS improvements; gross margin held in the 58%-60% range for 8 quarters.
Intense competition in a few molecules led to market-share rationalisation; management prioritises profitability over volume.
Q4 logistics and air-freight costs of about INR20 crore hurt margins; price increases are being negotiated with customers.
Access markets are facing donor-funding challenges, which management describes as tactical.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening in the US, including discontinuations and delayed launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the missing flu season, controlled-substance quota timing, and a policy of not launching until market conditions are attractive. It said 150 products are in the portfolio and launches will continue through FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are controlled substances and nasal sprays structurally higher-margin, and how big is the controlled substances opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said controlled substances are an in-US-for-US strategy and margins will be similar to the current profile, not dramatically different. It declined to give revenue potential, saying the company needs more DEA quota first, and the company has gone back to the DEA for additional quota.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 SG&A and freight spike persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A will stay around the current range, with Q4 freight costs elevated. It said a discount factor should be applied to Q4 when modelling.

qa_highlights.question: What are the nasal spray and new modality timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: One or two nasal products could launch earlier, but bulk revenue is expected in FY28-FY29. Patches and thin films filings are expected in 12-18 months, with about 5-6 additional third-party nasal programmes added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sandoz deal's impact and the R&D outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The Sandoz deal is expected to close in H2 FY27 (October-March). R&D spend is expected to be $20-25 mn over the next 2 years.

risks_watch: US growth depends on a recovery in H2 FY27 and on the controlled-substance quota outcome from the DEA; no timeline was given.
Gross margin needs to stay in the 58%-60% range amid logistics, fuel, raw material and FX cost pressure.

Competition in several US molecules and a 2-year wait before new nasal spray and modality revenue.
Access markets exposed to donor-funding challenges; Sandoz integration timing.

Ex-US revenue grew 17% YoY but fell sequentially from $70m in Q4 FY26 to $63m on supply-chain shipment delays that management calls timing, not demand. US revenue was flat at ₹6,282m ($68m) amid competition in newer launches, and management guided that H2 FY27 will be stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify revenue lost to freight-related supply delays in US?

qa_highlights.question: Net debt-free path?

qa_highlights.question: Weighted cost of debt and debt mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted cost of debt is about 7.6%, with major debt in India and the US; interest cost has fallen for 7-8 consecutive quarters. Management said CARE rating covers only a subset of loans.

qa_highlights.question: Controlled substance quota status?
qa_highlights.answer: Quota allocations happen twice a year based on past sales; controlled substances are about 5% of revenue; June cycle did not yield success, with a response expected in the next month.

qa_highlights.question: Product launches in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10 launches planned from now to 31 March 2027, with bulk of launches in H2 and profitability thresholds applied.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend of INR2.5-3.0 billion per year combining maintenance, R&D and hard capex; no greenfield plans under consideration.

532531|2026-09.headline: Strides Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record ₹14,297 million (+17% YoY), with Ex-US overtaking US, but FY28 US $375m aspiration slips beyond FY28.

Ex-US revenue reached ₹6,963 million (+31% YoY) and exceeded US revenue for the first time, reaching 102% of US revenue in the quarter. US revenue of ₹6,855 million (+9% YoY) recovered sequentially, but management pushed the ~$375 million US revenue aspiration beyond FY28 while keeping the overall FY28 growth ambition intact. Working capital rose ₹307 million in H1 as inventory was built, lifting net debt to EBITDA to 1.72x.

532538|2026-03.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA/ton of INR1,253 (ex-West Asia ~INR1,240), 200 MTPA capacity crossed, dividend INR240/share proposed.
532538|2026-03.overview: UltraTech crossed 200 million tonnes of Indian cement capacity a year ahead of target and completed 100% brand migration for India Cements and Kesoram at end-March 2026. Q4 consolidated volumes were above 44 million tonnes (brand volume up 19% YoY), grey cement prices rose about 2.5% across most geographies, and consolidated EBITDA per tonne was INR1,253 versus INR1,225 in Q4 FY25 (ex-acquired assets INR1,296). West Asia conflict is a headwind on fuel, packing bags (about INR90 crore extra bag cost in March), freight and forex mark-to-market (about INR120-130 crore). Management guided 7-8% sustainable volume growth, double-digit volume growth for FY27, and a Board-proposed dividend of INR240 per share for FY26.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum; management targets double-digit volume growth for FY27. Industry growth estimated at 6-7% for Q4 and about 6.5% for FY27.
Capacity: 200 Mtpa crossed; committed further 37 Mt taking capacity above 242.5 Mtpa in phases by FY28; plans beyond 240 Mtpa being developed.
Capex of about INR8,000-10,000 crore every year for the foreseeable future, funded from balance sheet; leverage to stay below 1x net debt/EBITDA after growth capex.

Clinker factor (cement-to-clinker ratio) target of about 1.54x by FY28, from 1.48x; 85% green power target by FY30 (43% today).

Green energy: 1.8 GW platform; 43% of power from green sources; no thermal capacity to be added, per management, with more WHRS and renewable tie-ups.
Lead distance reduced to 367 km; bulk terminal network expanding including new Lucknow facility.

demand_pricing: Grey cement prices up about 2.5% in most geographies in Q4 on improved trade mix and premiumisation; cement price hike taken in April 2026 and management expects it to stay.
Trade mix about 65-67%, not diluted; infrastructure share was weaker in Q4 due to end of high-speed rail work in Gujarat.
Bag costs rose from INR9 to about INR15 per bag in March, now about INR13-14; management says price increases already offset about INR6/bag increase.
Fuel: average fuel cost about INR1.77/kcal, may rise to about INR1.8 in June quarter; long-term fuel contracts seen as favourable going forward.
Management sees no supply shortage of bags or pet coke; dispatches unaffected. Demand seen steady; slowdown noted in last 15 days of March around West Bengal and Tamil Nadu elections.
Management attributed cement's relatively muted price hikes versus steel, PVC and agri inputs to industry fragmentation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is possible if the company and cement market perform well; the Board decides. Capex plan is INR8,000-10,000 crore a year funded from balance sheet with rising operating cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: How much of realisation gain is from brand transition?

qa_highlights.question: Cost impact of West Asia conflict and June-quarter outlook?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR200/t of India Cements EBITDA sits in UltraTech books; INR800/t in India Cements books; further efficiency of about INR200/t still to come, with price increases and operating leverage taking it beyond INR1,000/t.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to industry fragmentation; said price increases typically come in Q1 of the fiscal and that prices will be raised as costs rise.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for merging India Cements and status of legal cases, and RCB ring-fencing?

Whether cement price hikes taken in April 2026 stick given industry-wide cost pressure and monsoon seasonality.
Pace of India Cements EBITDA gains toward INR1,000/t and pending legal cases before further integration/merger of India Cements.
Cable and wire business launch timing (targeted early Q3 FY27) and dividend sustainability beyond FY26.

key_quotes: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India, a first for any company in a single country outside of China.
We said we would do these things, we have done them and we enter fiscal '27 in a stronger strategic position than at any point in our history.

532538|2026-06.headline: UltraTech Q1 FY27 domestic grey volumes rose 13.1% with EBITDA of INR5,146 crore and PAT up 17.2% to INR2,604 crore despite a fuel and packing cost shock.

India Cements turnaround continued, with EBITDA per ton reaching INR603 from INR509 in the prior quarter, and cables and wires remains on schedule for Q3 FY27 launch. Management guided to a INR130-140 per ton cost increase in Q2 FY27 and reaffirmed double-digit volume growth for FY27.

532538|2026-09.headline: UltraTech Q2 FY27: volumes up 13.8% with 71% utilisation; trade prices exited September ~3% above Q1 average and are about 5% above Q2 average.
532538|2026-09.overview: Management described a quarter where a weak monsoon kept construction active, while a West Asia conflict pushed fuel costs higher. Q2 trade prices averaged roughly 1-1.5% below Q1 on a soft August, but rose sharply in late September and October. Volume growth of 13.8% ran ahead of an industry estimate of about 10%, and net profit rose 21% YoY. Fuel cost per bag rose to INR 51.5 from INR 45, and the company expects the price increases to flow mainly into Q3 earnings.

financial_highlights.change: absolute fixed costs up 4% vs volume +13.8%

segments.name: Cement - regions
segments.commentary: North grew over 20% and South 15-20%; East ~5%, West ~10%, Central ~10%. Utilisation was above 70% in North and South, about 70% in West, and about 60% in Central and East.

segments.name: Wires and Cables (Ultravolt)
segments.commentary: Launched 3 September 2026 with INR 1,800 crores planned capex, of which INR 1,100 crores is spent or committed. Production of house wire, panel wire and multicore cable has started; power and control cable lines are due in H2. Management says it is too early to judge revenue or margins; it is a division, not a subsidiary.

guidance_outlook: Trade prices exited September at least ~3% above Q1 average; October prices are about 5% above Q2 average, with management expecting more increases in the next couple of months.
Full benefit of price increases expected in Q3 earnings rather than immediately, given festive-season slowdown.
FY27 capex guidance held at about INR 10,000 crores (plus or minus), with a fuller view after Q3.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1x by end-March 2027.

Business-as-usual delivery of the INR 1,400/tonne EBITDA exit-March-2028 target, with cost pressures expected to be covered by price increases.
Expects industry volume growth of about 8% in H1 FY27 and very strong momentum to March 2029.
Ultravolt: a mature business expected in FY28; April-June 2027 quarter is flagged as one worth discussing.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 4.6 Mtpa in September, taking domestic cement capacity to 204.7 Mtpa, including the 3.6 Mt greenfield plant at Petnikota (Andhra Pradesh) and 1 Mt of debottlenecking at 3 units.
On track for 240 Mtpa as planned; next phase of organic growth to be announced, with North capacity expansion plans to come before end-FY27.
Added 116 MW renewable power and 10 MW waste heat recovery; 47% of power from non-fossil sources; 2 GW green power for captive use.
Thermal substitution rate about 7.2% after AFR systems commissioned at 2 plants.
Ultravolt plant at Jhagadia (Gujarat); 1 main warehouse, 5 regional distribution centres and about 16 branch warehouses.
India Cement kiln shutdowns planned for upgrades (WHRS, preheater height) with benefits expected from Jan-Mar 2028 quarter.

UBS network above 25% of trade sales, with about 6,500 stores targeting 10,000 by FY28-29.
Ultravolt pricing is at market parity; the company says differentiation comes from premium Class 5 HR/FR products.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ultravolt's capex go beyond INR 1,800 crores?

qa_highlights.question: Will the industry return to pricing power?

qa_highlights.question: Will the EBITDA per tonne target of INR 1,400 hold?

Business as usual is what my expectation is to deliver that INR1,400.
I won't pretend that second half will be free of cost pressures.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: Capacity now 204.7 Mtpa after 4.6 Mtpa commissioned in Sept 2026 and utilisation is 71% (vs 66% LY), with management reaffirming the 240 Mtpa target and North expansion plans before end-FY27; timing of the next phase is not yet dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes grew 13.8% YoY against an industry of about 10%, the 4.6 Mtpa commissioned in September lifts capacity to 204.7 Mtpa, and the industry is sold out with management expecting about 8% industry growth in H1 FY27 and strong momentum to March 2029.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 71% is below the 80% threshold, but the industry is sold out and management has said North expansion plans will come before end-FY27 on the way to 240 Mtpa; FY27 capex is held at about INR 10,000 crore, with a fuller view after Q3.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Trade prices exited September about 3% above the Q1 average and October is about 5% above the Q2 average, with more increases expected in the next couple of months, and the full benefit is expected in Q3 earnings.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel cost per bag rose to INR 51.5 from INR 45 (~13% QoQ), the kcal cost may rise from INR 2.1 to INR 2.2, and management said H2 will not be free of cost pressure, though price increases of about 5% above the Q2 average are expected to cover it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: H2 FY27 (power and control cable lines)
rows.why: Ultravolt launched on 3 September 2026 with house wire, panel wire and multicore cable production started, and power and control cable lines are due in H2 FY27 on INR 1,800 crore planned capex (INR 1,100 crore spent or committed).

rows.label: Ultravolt ramp-up and revenue target
rows.why: Ultravolt is a mature business expected in FY28, with revenue target possibly INR 16,000-18,000 crore against the earlier INR 10,000 crore, but revenue and margins are not yet disclosed and pricing is at market parity.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1x by March 2027
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March 2026 after capex and dividend, and management has committed to below 1x by March 2027.

rows.label: Price increases of 7-10 per bag in late September

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and the South region and reaffirmed the INR 1,400/tonne and sub-1x leverage targets, but was evasive on forward cost curves, fuel contract terms and Ultravolt numbers, which were deferred; analysts pushed on H2 cost inflation and fuel costs.

532539|2026-03.headline: Uno Minda Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 5,336 crore with EBITDA margin of 11.3%, but commodity and labour cost pressure is expected to weigh on coming quarters.
532539|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was INR 5,336 crore (+18% YoY) and EBITDA was INR 603 crore (+14%) at an 11.3% margin, both company records. PAT attributable to shareholders rose 22% to INR 326 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR 19,589 crore (+17%), normalised EBITDA INR 2,182 crore (+16%) at 11.1%, and normalised PAT INR 1,166 crore (+24%). Management flagged that aluminium and labour cost spikes (Haryana labour rates up about 35%) are expected to hit coming quarters sizably, and is negotiating faster price pass-through with customers.

segments.name: Switch systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,343 crore (+17%, 25% of consol), a record quarter; 2-wheeler switches grew over 26% and 2-wheeler switch exports were INR 86 crore. FY26 revenue INR 4,871 crore (+16%).

segments.name: Lighting systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,154 crore (+13%, about 22% of consol); FY26 INR 4,402 crore (+14%). Management says 4-wheeler lighting is now in consolidation after a threefold expansion over five years.

segments.name: Casting (alloy wheels and die casting)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 982 crore (+14%, about 18% of consol): 4-wheeler alloy wheels INR 535 crore, 2-wheeler alloy wheels INR 259 crore, die casting INR 188 crore. FY26 INR 3,694 crore (+15%). Aluminium pass-through contributed about 4-5% of growth.

segments.name: Seating systems
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 381 crore (about 7% of consol); FY26 INR 1,416 crore (+23%). Q4 exports INR 54 crore.

segments.name: Green mobility (new reporting segment)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 423 crore (+25%, 8% of consol): alternate fuels INR 186 crore, 2W/3W EV systems INR 147 crore, 4W EV INR 46 crore, EV controllers INR 44 crore. FY26 INR 1,405 crore (+7% on restated INR 1,313 crore).

segments.name: Others (incl. acoustics, sensors/ADAS, blow moulding, aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,053 crore (+25%, about 20% of consol): sensors and ADAS INR 205 crore, acoustics INR 225 crore, blow moulding INR 118 crore, non-EV controllers INR 86 crore. FY26 INR 3,801 crore (+26%). Acoustics was moved into this category.

segments.name: Aftermarket and international
segments.commentary: Q4 aftermarket revenue INR 340 crore (about 7% of consol) plus INR 232 crore to OEM spare parts division. International business was about 10% of Q4 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated capex planned at about INR 1,750 crore: about INR 650 crore sustaining and about INR 1,100 crore growth, plus land; more land may be needed at CSN, Hosur and Gujarat.
Annual EBITDA margin guided at about 11% plus or minus 50 bps, including known start-up costs of new plants.
Automotive industry expected to sustain growth momentum in FY27; 7 of 11 ongoing projects to commence production or ramp up in FY27.
Sunroof manufacturing commissioning expected by end FY27; EV powertrain Khed Phase 1 expected in H2 FY27.
Physical exports from India (ex overseas plants) of about INR 600 crore in FY26 expected to cross INR 1,500 crore in the next few years.
Labour cost impact of about a couple of hundred crore for Haryana and Gujarat alone, with other states yet to announce floor wages; mitigation via customer pass-through being negotiated.
Expected sizeable commodity-driven margin impact in coming quarters; management seeks shorter pass-through cycles (monthly or quarterly instead of half-yearly).
capex_capacity: Khed City (Pune) EV powertrain facility to begin operations in H2 FY27; Phase 1 of the Kharkhoda/Farrukhnagar-linked programmes also in progress.

New greenfield EV powertrain plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar under UMAIPL: total investment about INR 550 crore, EDU with Inovance Automotive technology partner, DHT through a customer partnership, commissioning by Q2 FY28.
CSN casting plant of about INR 300 crore to serve EDU and DST; combined EV powertrain capex about INR 1,200 crore, revenue potential more than 2x (INR 2,500 crore+, peak up to about INR 3,000 crore).
4-wheeler switch shifting from Manesar to Farrukhnagar expected to complete over the next 6 months; 2-wheeler lighting's three plants being merged into one at Kharkhoda.
Capacity post expansion: about 9.5 million 2-wheeler alloy wheels per year and about 7 million 4-wheeler alloy wheels, based on announced projects.
Commissioned in Q4: 4-wheeler lighting plants at Khed City and Indonesia, 2-wheeler alloy wheel expansion at Supa, 4-wheeler alloy wheel Phase 1 at Kharkhoda, and Bawal expansion.
Sunroof order book potential exceeds INR 350 crore after a new INR 85 crore annual peak order; facility commissioning by end FY27.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 PV production a record 5.5 million units (+9%); 2W production a record 26.6 million (+12%); CV production 1.17 million (+13%); 3W Q4 production +32%. Management cited EV penetration of 4.2% in PV and 6.5% in e-2W.

Q4 alloy wheel penetration moderated: 4-wheeler customers shifted mix to entry-level models with lower alloy adoption; in 2W, some programmes switched to steel wheels. Current penetration is about 70% in 2W and about 40% in 4W (as stated).

Pass-through: 3- or 6-month cycles set by customer policy, not by commodity; 1-2 customers operate annually. Management says commodity spikes of 30-40% are not normal and is seeking monthly or quarterly adjustments.

Gross margin compressed by about 1% YoY in Q4, attributed to newer lower-margin businesses and commodity impacts; the trading business (EV-related, about INR 40-45 crore) is too small to be significant.

New wins: 2W lighting order with annual peak value about INR 450 crore (SOP H2 FY28, about 25% of current 2W lighting revenue); 2W silver-box display order about INR 200 crore (production from Q4 FY27); CV seating export orders about INR 390 crore from 3 customers in Europe and North America (supplies from FY28); IVI order about INR 600 crore (SOP Q3 FY29, via Denso JV, outside consolidated revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Why set up a second 4W EV powertrain plant (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) while Khed is still under construction, and how will the multiple plants (about 9 starting FY27, ~INR 1,800 crore capex) be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited firm customer partnerships for DST and EDU and a customer push to be closer to them; Khed capacity was earmarked for existing businesses. It said one plant commissions this year and the second after about a year. Execution is handled by separate business teams, so no team overlaps across plants. Revenue guidance for the new plant was not given.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 debit/credit note quantum affecting margin, and how much aluminium pass-through and commodity impact was there?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantum of the Q4 debit/credit note adjustments was not shared because it differs by business. Some customer price settlement income was booked in Q4. Aluminium pass-through contributed about 4-5% of casting growth. Commodity impact is expected to be sizable in coming quarters; Haryana labour rates are up about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the new 4W EV plant revenue potential and how much of the 1.85 lakh capacity is booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Booked share was not disclosed; the 1.85 lakh figure is eventual capacity and will be built as business is won. Khed (INR 400 crore+) and the new plant (INR 550 crore) plus about INR 300 crore CSN casting total about INR 1,200 crore capex, with revenue above 2x, at least INR 2,500 crore and up to about INR 3,000 crore at peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin impact from the labour and commodity pressures, and how does pass-through work?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour impact is about a couple of hundred crore for Haryana and Gujarat alone, with other states yet to announce floor wages. Pass-through cycles are set by each customer (3 or 6 months, with 1-2 customers annual), not by commodity. Management is seeking monthly or quarterly adjustments. The 11% plus/minus 50 bps guidance includes known start-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the alloy wheel penetration levels and the 2W alloy wheel and 4W alloy wheel capacity post expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Current alloy wheel penetration is about 70% in 2W and about 40% in 4W. Capacity post expansion is about 9.5 million 2W alloy wheels per year and about 7 million 4W alloy wheels, based on announced projects.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down about 1%, and how large is the trading drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin fell about 1% YoY. Management attributed this to newer lower-margin businesses and commodity impact. The EV-related trading business is about INR 40-45 crore and too small to matter. Exports from India were about INR 600 crore in FY26 and are expected to cross INR 1,500 crore in the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the Denso JV infotainment (IVI) order and how does it reflect in consolidated numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: The IVI order has annual peak value of about INR 600 crore, with SOP in Q3 FY29 and about 70% of current JV revenue of INR 846 crore. It sits in the Denso JV and is excluded from consolidated revenue, appearing only as share of JV profit. No further new business timing was committed.

risks_watch: Commodity (aluminium) and labour cost spikes (Haryana up about 35%; labour impact about INR 200 crore for Haryana and Gujarat) hit coming quarters, and pass-through cycles of 3-6 months (1-2 customers annual) lag the cost increase.

Start-up costs and execution load as about 7 of 11 projects commence or ramp in FY27, including Khed EV powertrain (H2 FY27), sunroof (end FY27) and CSN/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plants; the 11% plus/minus 50 bps EBITDA guidance must absorb these.
Alloy wheel penetration softening (4W mix shift to entry models, 2W programmes switching to steel wheels) could weigh on casting growth.
Capex of about INR 1,750 crore in FY27 and possible additional land at CSN, Hosur and Gujarat; net debt rose to INR 2,179 crore, partly from the INR 200-odd crore FRIWO-linked acquisition.
Q4 debit/credit note adjustments were not quantified, so the underlying Q4 margin base is harder to assess; monitor Q1 FY27 margin and the pass-through reset to monthly or quarterly.
Revenue visibility on the new 4W EV plant is not disclosed; booked share of the 1.85 lakh capacity and revenue timing remain open.
key_quotes: So some of the customers have been positive with some of the customer discussions have been happening, and we still have like 1, 1.5 month for this quarter.
Normally, you expect labor price to be 5%, 7%, 8%, 10% kind of a thing. But 35%, obviously, is not something which can be absorbed easily.
And we expect to complete the transition of Manesar plant to Farrukhnagar over the next 6 months.
But we do expect to absorb all this in our current profitability.

532539|2026-06.headline: Uno Minda Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 5,557 crores; EBITDA margin 10.3%, with FY27 guidance of 11% ±50 bps held.
532539|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations hit a record INR 5,557 crores, up 26% YoY against INR 4,420 crores excluding prior-period income. EBITDA excluding prior-year exceptional income grew 21% to INR 572 crores, but margin was 10.3% as commodity and gas inflation, a ~40 bps mathematical pass-through dilution and minimum wage hikes weighed on it. Management kept the annual EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps, biased to the upper end. PAT attributable to shareholders rose 24% to INR 296 crores, and the company added seating, sunroof and lighting orders while the Inovance JV awaits China approval.

segments.name: Switching systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,335 crores, +20% YoY, 24% of consolidated turnover. 4-wheeler switches under Uno Mindarika grew 24% to INR 525 crores; Manesar to Farrukhnagar shift on track for H2 FY27.

segments.name: Lighting systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,153 crores, +14% YoY, ~21% of revenue. New domestic 4-wheeler lighting nomination from a global OEM; INR 450 crores annual peak value order in 2W lighting; Indonesia 4W lighting plant secured a second customer with SOP in Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Casting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,090 crores, +32% YoY, ~20% of revenue and the fastest-growing vertical. 2W alloy wheel INR 284 crores, 4W alloy wheel INR 56 crores, aluminium die casting INR 248 crores (+66%).

segments.name: Seating systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 408 crores, +28% YoY, ~7% of revenue. Exports INR 72 crores; INR 390 crores annual peak export orders from 3 new customers; INR 320 crores greenfield 4W seating plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, operations by Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 542 crores, +78% YoY, ~10% of revenue. Alternate fuels INR 184 crores, Uno Minda EV Systems INR 186 crores, Uno Minda Automation INR 123 crores, EV controller business INR 37 crores. Like-for-like EV EV Systems plus controller revenue INR 218 crores, +24%.

segments.name: Other (reconfigured)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,029 crores, +21% YoY, ~19% of revenue. Sensors and ADAS INR 250 crores, acoustics INR 225 crores, blow moulding INR 125 crores, non-EV controllers INR 80 crores; sunroof order book crossed INR 500 crores.

segments.name: Aftermarket and SPD
segments.commentary: Aftermarket revenue INR 336 crores (~6%); OEM spare parts division INR 254 crores; combined INR 590 crores, ~11% of consolidated revenue.

guidance_outlook: Annual EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps, with a bias towards the higher end, reaffirmed despite Q1 headwinds.

FY27 capex stays at about INR 1,750 crores. Total announced project capex is about INR 3,800 crores, of which about INR 1,400 crores is spent; the remaining ~INR 2,000 crores to be spent over 18-24 months.
Gross margin may stay under pressure from commodity pass-through dilution (~40 bps) and lower-margin electronics business, but EBITDA margin should offset this.
Management expects healthy automotive growth through the rest of FY27 and aims to keep outperforming industry volumes.
Export targets: double and triple export value in absolute terms, with export growth needing to outpace domestic growth to raise its share.
Inovance JV: no holdup on plant construction or supplies as of now; more clarity expected in about one quarter.
capex_capacity: Kharkhoda 4W alloy wheel: new 60,000-unit line to be fully ramped up from Q2 FY27; a further 30,000-unit line to commission in H2 FY27.
Bawal 2W alloy wheel: 4 of 6 lines expected live in H2 FY27, adding about 1 million units annual capacity and entering HPDC alloy wheels.
Sunroof plant commissioning by end FY27; ramp in FY27 with full sales from FY28-FY29. Order book above INR 500 crores.
4W seating greenfield plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (INR 320 crores): commencement by Q2 FY28; capex of INR 3.2 billion can generate more than 2x its investment in revenue.
Lighting: consolidation of North India 2W lighting plants into Kharkhoda from H2 FY27; Indonesia lighting plant transition to new facility by end FY27.
Inovance JV plants: Khed City plant construction on schedule; CSN plant to start construction in the next couple of months.
demand_pricing: Indian automotive production in Q1 FY27 was a record 96.9 lakh units (+22% YoY); PV production 14.5 lakh (+17%); 2W 72.5 lakh (+23%); CV 2.9 lakh (+15%).
EV penetration in PV reached 6.8% (84,000 units, +54%); electric 2W registrations crossed 5 lakh in a quarter; electric 3W penetration above 60%.
Customers are passing through commodity costs, with some OEMs moving to monthly price adjustments on one or two commodities and some announcing price hikes.
Seating kit value estimated at INR 30,000-40,000 per car; management says it could become one of the group's largest kit-value products.
Competition in Indian seating is intense; the Tachi-S partnership is cited as a technology edge.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete in 4W seating (segments, market size) and how will H2 growth hold up against a high base, including Inovance SOPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has one 4W seating nomination with more models in talks and will not name vehicles before launch; kit value is INR 30,000-40,000 per car. As of now there is no holdup to Inovance products or plant work, and the H2 growth is supported by Kharkhoda phase 2, 2W alloy wheels and the Mindarika move.

qa_highlights.question: Is green mobility near group profitability, and what is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Some green mobility businesses already earn above group profitability while newer ones are below it; new businesses are expected to reach target profitability in their third full year of production. FY27 capex remains about INR 1,750 crores; FY28 guidance will be given with the annual outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How fast will margins recover toward 11%, and can wage and commodity costs be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: The ~40 bps commodity dilution persists for the rest of FY27 if prices stay high. Management expects to absorb much of the wage increase through automation and productivity and to recover commodities on a quarterly or half-yearly basis, with some customers moving to monthly indexation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall QoQ in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Casting uses the WDV method, so new capacity starts from a lower base and Q1 depreciation tends to be lower than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential of the 4W seating capex and the timing of export and sunroof ramps?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 3.2 billion seating capex can generate more than 2x revenue. Export orders run on a 2-year cycle, with impact from end FY28 and full run-rate in FY29; the sunroof ramp starts around March-April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the China Inovance JV and is e-axle import at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Press Note 3 approval is in hand, but China approval is pending after recent regulatory tightening; Inovance is seeking clarification. There is no current restriction on e-axle imports, and more clarity is expected in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export growth outlook and the gross margin trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose to INR 228 crores from INR 141 crores, and new business of about INR 400 crores is in the pipeline. Gross margin is diluted by commodity pass-through (~0.4%) and lower-margin electronics, but EBITDA margin is expected to hold given better asset turns.

risks_watch: Inovance JV: China approval pending after tighter technology-partnership rules; possible delay to JV-linked e-drive and EV product launches.
Commodity and gas inflation could persist through FY27, keeping margins under the 11% target until pass-throughs catch up.
JV and associate profit was flat at INR 48 crores, and management expects recovery from Q2 as commodity prices are passed through.
Execution on the INR 2,000 crore capex balance over the next 18-24 months, plus ramp-up of new plants (Bawal, Kharkhoda, sunroof, Sambhajinagar seating).
Green mobility traction-motor volumes are small (2 OEMs), so the segment's profitability path is still unproven.

532540|2026-03.headline: TCS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 1.2% QoQ in constant currency, third straight sequential gain, with $12B TCV and 25.3% operating margin.
532540|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹70,698 crore (up 5.4% QoQ in INR, $7.621B up 1.5% QoQ, 1.2% QoQ in constant currency), the third consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Q4 TCV was $12B including three mega deals, and client additions were seen across all revenue bands after about two years. Full-year FY26 revenue declined 2.4% in constant currency to $30.017B, while operating margin reached 25%, a four-year high. Management said the restructuring programme is complete, and the company announced annual increments effective April 1 with top performers getting double-digit increases.

financial_highlights.change: +5.4% QoQ INR; +1.5% QoQ USD; +1.2% QoQ CC

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew 1.4% QoQ in constant currency in Q4.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Grew 2.4% QoQ in constant currency in Q4.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 1.0% QoQ in constant currency in Q4.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Management said the vertical continued to grow in Q4; clients remained cautious amid rate and inflation uncertainty.

segments.name: Consumer Business Group (CBG)
segments.commentary: Saw good growth and a record TCV, with 2 mega deals (Marks & Spencer renewal and expansion, and a US healthcare and pharmacy retailer). Retail globally and TTH UK/EMEA led; CPG and TTH North America declined.

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare
segments.commentary: Marginal growth in Q4.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Good growth despite tariff volatility and EV demand recalibration; customers prioritising cost optimisation.

segments.name: Technology and Software
segments.commentary: Reasonable growth in Q4.

segments.name: Communications, Media and Information (CMI)
segments.commentary: Modest decline in Q4; signed first CMI mega deal, a five-year UK telecom consumer-business contract.

segments.name: Energy, Resources and Utilities (ERU)
segments.commentary: Robust growth overall; Energy and Resources performed well, while Utilities is under stress.

guidance_outlook: No specific revenue or earnings guidance given; management said it is positive on FY27 and on international growth, without quantifying it.
Management expects a regular Q1 and Q2 with a stronger first half, which is the planning assumption.
Wage increments effective April 1 are expected to cost 150-200 bps of margin, similar to the past cycle.
Management expects SG&A to rise both in absolute terms and as a percentage of revenue due to Build-Partner-Acquire investments.
Margins are to be kept within a tighter range, with a longer-term aim of moving toward 26%; rupee depreciation helps but is not guaranteed.
Management expects AI revenue to be net accretive to growth in FY27, aiming to arrest the degrowth in traditional services first.
Combined one-off charges for FY26 were ₹1,300 crore; no one-offs were called out in Q4.
capex_capacity: HyperVault: building toward 1 GW of AI data-centre capacity; anchor workloads seen at 100-200 MW per customer.
OpenAI partnership to build 100 MW capacity with an option to scale to 1 GW.
AMD collaboration on Helios rack-scale AI architecture for high-density AI capacity in India.
Partner ecosystem includes Tata Power, Tata Projects, Tata Communications, GE, Honeywell, ABB and Siemens for EPC, power, cooling and controls.
Land parcel finalisation and customer commitments achieved in Q4; no capex amount disclosed.
demand_pricing: Q4 TCV of $12B included three mega deals: Marks & Spencer, a leading UK telecom operator, and a US healthcare and pharmacy retailer.
FY26 TCV of $40.7B with 5 mega deals; Q4 deal mix was about 50-55% renewals and 40-45% new programmes.
Client additions: 66 accounts above $100M (+4 QoQ), 139 in the $50M+ band (+3), 1,397 in the $1M+ band (+14); every revenue band added clients after about two years.
Pricing: realisations improved, contributing about 40 bps to Q4 margin; management said TCS does not lose deals on pricing.
Clients are shifting from experimentation to industrialised AI, with vendor consolidation and cost optimisation a major theme.
Geopolitical impact so far is limited to the Middle East and travel and transportation; no broad client caution reported outside BFSI-specific caution.
Management said AI deals are 12-16 week rapid builds, and that agentic AI in business process services is gaining traction.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 international growth return to the 3-4% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan declined to give a number but said the company is quite positive on FY27 and on international growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is elevated SG&A the new normal, or will it return below 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Seksaria said investments in partnerships, recruitment, training and new businesses will keep SG&A elevated, both in absolute terms and as a share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are restructuring costs still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs were called out in Q4; the combined FY26 one-off was ₹1,300 crore. Krithivasan said the restructuring programme is complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected margin impact of wage hikes next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Seksaria said the impact should be similar to the past annual increment cycle, which was 150-200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth being sacrificed for margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan said margin is not hurting growth; the margin allows competitive pricing and funds investments such as acquisitions and HyperVault.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI revenue be net accretive to FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Krithivasan said AI is expected to be net accretive in the first year, with the aim of arresting the degrowth in traditional services.

risks_watch: BFSI client caution over interest rates, inflation and central bank actions.
Escalation of geopolitical conflict could cause supply chain disruption and affect travel and transportation and Middle East operations.
Wage increments (150-200 bps margin impact) and higher SG&A could limit margin expansion toward 26%.
AI-led deflation in renewals and existing business may offset AI revenue growth.
Utilities segment stress within ERU, and CPG and TTH North America declines within CBG.
HyperVault execution and capex funding, plus dependence on hyperscaler and model-company commitments.
Quarterly seasonality: management expects a stronger first half, which must be delivered.
532540|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q4 momentum, order book and FY27 outlook, while cautious on BFSI and macro. Management avoided quantifying FY27 growth and was evasive on how far SG&A will stay elevated.
key_quotes: We are very pleased to announce third consecutive quarter of sequential growth.
We delivered a strong 1.2% sequentially on a constant currency (CC) basis, in the backdrop of intensifying geopolitical conflicts and macro-economic uncertainty.

rows.label: New capex announcement
