tone.note: Management was confident on Q4 momentum, the $12B TCV, client additions and FY27 positioning, and cautious on BFSI and macro; analysts pushed on FY27 international growth, how long SG&A stays elevated (above 15%), and the margin hit from wage hikes, and management declined to quantify these.

532540|2026-06.headline: TCS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% YoY to ₹72,275 crore, but operating margin fell 130 bps QoQ to 24% on wage hikes.
532540|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹72,275 crore, up 2.2% QoQ and 13.9% YoY in rupee terms, and the fourth consecutive quarter of growth. In dollar terms revenue was $7,624 million, flat QoQ and up 2.7% YoY; constant currency growth was 0.4% QoQ and 3.2% YoY. TCV was $9.5 billion, including an $800 million mega deal with SKF. Operating margin fell to 24% (down 130 bps QoQ), with a 170 bps hit from annual salary increments partly offset by 40 bps of currency benefit and efficiencies. Management said clients deferred some projects amid geopolitical uncertainty and expects demand to improve sometime in Q2.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Delivered good growth across geographies; management remains optimistic on sustained BFSI growth.

segments.name: Technology, Software and Services
segments.commentary: Continued growth momentum with several large and mid-sized wins, including a multi-million-dollar ServiceNow deal.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Softness in auto; management expects a turnaround in Q2 based on net new wins including SKF, ABB and a Fortune 50 European firm.

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare
segments.commentary: Declined this quarter; management expects recovery, with some verticals showing an uptick.

segments.name: Consumer Business Group
segments.commentary: Pressured by inflation and geopolitics affecting discretionary spend; airlines in North America and non-essential retail under stress.

segments.name: CMI and ERU
segments.commentary: CMI saw modest growth amid industry headwinds; ERU declined slightly, with management positive on AI infrastructure, electrification and renewables.

segments.name: Regional Markets
segments.commentary: Growth driven by India, public services, and products and platforms.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or earnings guidance given; management expects demand to resume sometime in Q2 FY27 due to pent-up technology backlog.
Management aims to progressively move margins closer to at least FY26 levels, with an exit at 25% plus in the quarter and a target to achieve it sooner rather than later.
Management expects Manufacturing and Life Sciences to turn around in Q2, tech services to keep growing, and Consumer to recover once geopolitical sentiment improves.
Capital allocation policy unchanged; continued commitment to returning substantial free cash flows to shareholders.
Productivity pass-through to clients is about 10% to 15% on average, front-loaded in contracts, with the aim of offsetting it through new opportunities.
capex_capacity: Investing in AI capabilities, talent transformation, partner ecosystems, platforms, domain solutions and go-to-market capacity; no capex figures disclosed.
Launched TCS SovereignSecure Cloud for Europe to address data residency and sovereign cloud demand.
Launched a dedicated Global Value and Innovation Center business unit to build, operate, transform or divest global capability centers.
Anthropic partnership includes 50,000 licenses; TCS is first GSI partner for Mistral AI with a dedicated COE for industry solutions.
demand_pricing: Clients deferred some projects in Q1 as geopolitical uncertainty rose from March and continued through June; management is optimistic on a Q2 demand recovery.
TCV of $9.5 billion including SKF ($800 million, net new) and the sixth mega deal in five quarters; three mega deals announced in the last quarter per management.
AI revenue growth was lumpy: incremental AI revenue added was $75 million in Q1 versus $125 million in Q4, with management saying AI projects are often one- to two-quarter engagements.
Engagement models are shifting; agentic GBS deals saw more outcome-based commitments in F&A, HR and customer experience.
Productivity gains passed to clients are about 10% to 15% on average, typically offset by additional client work according to management.
Management said it sees no broad white-collar contraction and that total headcount rose in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much did macro and geopolitical uncertainty affect Q1, and what is the September quarter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said uncertainty rose from March and clients deferred projects; it is optimistic demand will resume sometime in Q2 on pent-up technology backlog, with no rate of change quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 16% YoY dollar increase in SG&A?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost categories were refined and the COR/SG&A split was removed; investments are in talent, partnerships and targeted areas, including some M&A-related charges.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-driven productivity deflating revenue, and how much has been passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to quantify; in most places productivity passed on is about 10% to 15%, and customers often give additional work in return.

qa_highlights.question: Why is incremental AI revenue lower QoQ, and is there seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI work is non-recurring and project-based, so quarterly revenue will be lumpy, though the trend is rising and client conversations are yielding opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall sharply across segments, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the 170 bps wage impact is the main driver across segments, with some vertical-level investment; TCS typically takes the Q1 headwind and aims to exit at 25%+ margin.

qa_highlights.question: How many freshers were hired and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14,000 campus graduates were onboarded last quarter, and hiring is ongoing with a focus on AI-native skills.

risks_watch: Whether the Q2 demand recovery materialises given ongoing geopolitical conflicts and project deferrals.
Margin recovery: the 170 bps wage impact and continued investment versus the stated goal of exiting at 25%+ and approaching FY26 levels.
Consumer and Life Sciences softness; management did not give a timeline beyond Q2 for consumer recovery.
AI revenue lumpiness (incremental $75 million in Q1 vs $125 million in Q4) and whether net-new AI deals convert to revenue quickly.
Productivity pass-through to clients (10% to 15%) could compress revenue per deal over time.

532540|2026-09.headline: TCS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 0.5% QoQ in constant currency to ₹73,188 crore; operating margin held at 24% amid higher subcontracting and investments.
532540|2026-09.overview: Constant-currency revenue grew 0.5% QoQ and 2.8% YoY, with international up 1.2% QoQ and India up 6% QoQ, though Regional Markets fell on an India project deferral. Growth broadened across BFSI, Manufacturing and Technology & Services, while Consumer and ERU declined. Operating margin was stable at 24% and net margin 19%, with management prioritising investment (higher bench, subcontractors, partnerships, M&A) over near-term margin expansion. Annualised AI revenue crossed $3.1 billion, over 10% of revenue, and TCV was $9.6 billion excluding Porsche and Best Buy deals.

financial_highlights.change: AI revenue grew ~19% per analyst question, not disputed

segments.name: Consumer Business
segments.commentary: -0.7% QoQ and -1% YoY; retail and consumer products hit by inflation, energy costs and insourcing, though QoQ decline improved versus prior quarter.

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare
segments.commentary: +0.3% QoQ, stable demand from compliance, clinical/research platforms and AI-enabled drug discovery.

segments.name: Communications and Media
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ; media and digital platforms offset by continued telecom pressure.

segments.name: Energy, Resources and Utilities
segments.commentary: -0.5% QoQ; management sees medium-term structural recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Will the international growth momentum continue in coming quarters?

qa_highlights.question: What caused the India revenue decline and client-count drop?
qa_highlights.answer: A project deferral in India caused the decline, expected to return in later quarters; the client drop below the $100 million band was a single account pushed below the threshold by currency movement.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin levers toward 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Samir Seksaria cited subcontracting cost reduction, investments starting to deliver, productivity, utilisation and non-employee expense control; long-term aspiration stays at 26%-28%.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI revenues margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: The $3.1 billion annualised AI revenue comes in at a much higher margin than the company average.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 40% YoY growth in delivery-related costs an upfront investment that will pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Samir said it is a combination of investment in capacity ahead of growth and partnership costs; subcontracting is an optimisation lever, and fees to external consultants carry incremental delivery cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America lagging, and how will Consumer and ERU play out in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects North America to recover soon based on TCV and client conversations; Consumer expected to improve medium term, ERU to recover structurally over medium term.

532548|2026-03.headline: Century Plyboards posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 1,492 crores (+24.5% YoY) with consolidated EBITDA margin ex-forex at 13.6%.
532548|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue of INR 1,492 crores, up 10.5% QoQ and 24.5% YoY, with consolidated EBITDA margin excluding forex losses at 13.6% versus 12.6% in Q3 and 12.1% a year ago. For FY26, revenue grew 19.2% and EBITDA ex-forex rose to INR 702 crores (13.0% margin) from INR 502 crores (11.1%), with PAT up 44% to INR 268 crores. Management has taken a 7% plywood price increase in April and an industry-wide 15% increase in MDF/particle board amid chemical and resin cost inflation, but gave no FY27 segment guidance, citing fluid geopolitical conditions. segments.commentary: Revenue fell to Rs 2,128 mn from Rs 2,261 mn. Cyclopam crossed Rs 200 crore (Rs 206 crore sales) and Cital and dental portfolio grew about 30%, but Febrex Plus, Oxipod and ATL degrew by a similar value.

segments.name: Regulated international markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 21.1% to Rs 1,109 mn: Europe up 23.5% to Rs 675 mn, US up 16.4% to Rs 391 mn, South Africa/Australia/NZ up 31.2% to Rs 43 mn.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 612 mn was broadly flat against Rs 618 mn. Roughly Rs 10 crore of Africa ophthal sales were divested, and management expects Rs 10-12 crore of impact to remain this year.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 4.6% to Rs 451 mn. Management said the business shows resilience and is strategically important for supply security.

segments.name: AnaCipher CRO and Indoco Analytical Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20.8% to Rs 82 mn from Rs 68 mn.

segments.name: Warren Remedies (toothpaste/OTC)
segments.commentary: Toothpaste division revenue was about Rs 36 crore in the quarter and is near breakeven after reduced advertising; about Rs 16 crore was spent on promotion in H1. Warren API is mostly internal consumption with no approvals yet.

guidance_outlook: Domestic formulations: high single-digit FY27 growth reiterated, with more predictable sales expected in H2; management said it would not revise guidance.
Emerging markets: expected to return to good double-digit growth, with Q4 typically strong; H1 growth about 8%.
Regulated markets: management targets 20%+ growth in Europe and UK over the next 1-2 years.
R&D expected to stay below 5% of topline; YTD at about 4%.
Capex to stay at bare minimum; no major capex expected in H2 FY27 or FY28.
FY27 debt repayment target reaffirmed; H1 repayment about Rs 65 crore at consolidated level.
Management said freight cost impact duration is uncertain, with consolidated other expenses slightly above the roughly Rs 150-160 crore guided range.
capex_capacity: Capex in H1 per cash flow was about Rs 60 crore, but management said actual PPE capex (land etc.) is under Rs 25 crore; the balance is capitalised intangibles (ANDA and dossier R&D). Company agreed to bifurcate disclosure between PPE and other intangibles.
Warren Remedies: recent API site and finished product site capex has been completed.
Warren API US FDA audit expected by Q2 next year; CEPs approved and DMFs filed.
Plant-1 Goa received a successful MHRA audit and ANVISA clearance for the RCRO AnaCipher.
Goa plant USFDA inspection received 7 observations; response submitted, with outcome expected by first week of December.
Management said the company can add shifts across plants if needed and can reach roughly 4X current international topline with existing infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Freight and material cost pressure: management cited around Rs 13 crore of additional freight impact in the quarter and COGS, RMPM, freight and handling costs up roughly 30%, weighing on gross margin.

Domestic weakness was attributed to an almost absent monsoon hitting seasonal acute and anti-infective/anti-cold categories; anti-infectives and respiratory were about 30% of domestic business, down from over 50% earlier.
Cyclopam prescriptions grew about 16%; Cyclopam, Cital and dental portfolio grew about 30%, while Febrex Plus was down about 20% and ATM down about 16%.
About Rs 100 crore MAT sales come from products launched in the last two years.
FPP (US) turned profitable in H1 with H1 revenue above Rs 100 crore; management flagged US generic price erosion and competition.
LATAM grew 57%; French West Africa growing at higher double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other and employee expenses rise this quarter despite earlier cost reduction and headcount cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the increase to about Rs 13 crore of freight cost, mainly in international business; employee costs fell a couple of percentage points as a share of sales, and consolidated expenses were slightly above the roughly Rs 160 crore guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic guidance be maintained and what drives H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated high single-digit growth for FY27, citing about Rs 65 crore Ophthal base impact and expecting more predictable H2 sales; it said weak rains hurt the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What explains H1 capex of about Rs 60 crore against guidance of about Rs 40 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the difference is capitalised intangibles from ANDA and dossier R&D; actual PPE capex is under Rs 25 crore, and no major capex is planned for H2 or next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a new subsidiary (Warren Life Sciences) registered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the OTC toothpaste and API businesses are very different and separate tracking is needed; it registered Warren Life Sciences with the intent of possibly separating the two businesses, not for funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US FDA outcome expectation for the Goa plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said responses have been submitted, with data updates sent to USFDA, and the company expects to know the outcome by the first week of December; none of the seven observations relate to data integrity or cleaning validation.

qa_highlights.question: Can Europe and UK regulated markets grow 20%+ for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that is the target, citing steady order positions and good offtake in Europe and UK.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin pressure from freight and raw material costs; duration of the geopolitical-driven cost increase is uncertain.
Domestic franchise: high single-digit FY27 guidance depends on H2 recovery in seasonal acute brands after a weak monsoon.
USFDA Goa plant response outcome expected by early December with seven observations.
Warren Remedies toothpaste losses and ad spend; API unit under-utilised with no approvals yet; Warren API US FDA audit targeted for Q2 next year.
Operating cash flow conversion weak: H1 OCF about Rs 50 crore against EBITDA of about Rs 80 crore (about 60-65%), versus 75-90% historically.
Emerging markets flat in H1 with Ophthal divestment impact of Rs 10-12 crore this year.

Management repeatedly blamed weather, freight and the Ophthal divestment, and declined to quantify several items (GC margins, launches, MMP savings, FPP breakeven).
key_quotes: Cyclopam has further strengthened its position as a flagship brand, crossing the Rs. 200 crore threshold and now at a sales of Rs. 206 crore and maintaining its number two position in the antispasmodics and anticholinergics market.
High single -digit is what I had promised. We are going to work very hard for it.
So, we are not talking of a branded business.
It is very foolish in these times to make any of these comments.

rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 9.2% from 12.4% YoY on about Rs 13 crore of extra freight and COGS, RMPM and handling costs up roughly 30%, and management said the freight-cost duration is uncertain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Europe and UK growth of 20%+ for 1-2 years

tone.note: Management was confident on regulated markets, the 20%+ Europe/UK target and the Goa USFDA outcome, but defensive on domestic weakness, margins and freight costs, blaming weather and the Ophthal divestment; analysts pushed on margins, capex classification and the Warren Life Sciences subsidiary.

532626|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 80% YoY to INR 932 crores and FY26 PAT rose 113% to INR 139 crores, with copper cathode capex of about INR 200 crores funded from internal accruals.
532626|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 production, sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with FY26 revenue of INR 2,939 crores (+45%) and EBITDA of INR 218 crores (7.4% margin). Q4 EBITDA was INR 61 crores and PAT INR 38 crores, with Q4 blended gross margin of 6.4% pulled down by a copper mix of about 40% and copper margins of about 3.5-4%. Operating cash flow was negative in FY26, which management attributed to about INR 265 crores of trade receivables, mainly an export shipment delayed by vessel movement that pushed INR 120-130 crores of collections into early April. Management also disclosed a 36,000 tpa copper cathode plant (Phase 1 of 18,000 tpa targeted for December 2026) and some trading volumes in Q4, which it said were opportunistic.

financial_highlights.change: more than doubled YoY; margin 7.4% vs 5.3% in FY25 (+212 bps)
Q4 consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT +78% / +124% / +126% YoY
Lead ~45 days; copper brought from ~70 days to around 50 days

financial_highlights.value: INR 5 per share (100% of face value)

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: FY26 production 104,481 MT and sales 100,727 MT (+11% each); value-added products were 65% of lead revenue. Q4 lead volumes dipped as management deliberately prioritised higher-margin products; EBITDA per ton was INR 19,739 in Q4.

segments.name: Copper
segments.commentary: Recycling capacity doubled to 12,000 MTPA in Q4 FY26, with ramp to 70% utilisation during FY27. FY26 copper volumes rose about 7x and sales about 11x to INR 673 crores, with EBITDA per ton of INR 39,896. Copper contributed about 40% of Q4 sales at a margin of about 3.5-4%.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Unit relocated and production started in March 2026 at the new location. Management said it is EBITDA and PAT positive as of now, but FY26 was largely negative; per-ton realisation not disclosed.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Little activity; management said it will look at it when the time is right.

guidance_outlook: FY27 lead volume guidance of about 125,000-130,000 MT (management said 70-75% utilisation of the 204,000 MTPA TKD lead capacity), with about 15% lead volume growth targeted for FY28; FY28 utilisation aspiration 80-90%.
FY27 copper volume of about 12,000 MT including cathode; FY28 copper volume of at least 24,000 MT on a conservative basis, with up to about 36,000 MT by end FY28 mentioned.
EBITDA per ton guidance: lead INR 17,000-19,000; copper recycling INR 35,000-40,000; copper cathode INR 60,000-70,000 (conservative), with blended FY28 copper around INR 60,000 cited as achievable.

Phase 1 of 36,000 MTPA copper cathode plant (18,000 MTPA each in two phases) targeted for December 2026, with Phase 2 about 6-7 months later; estimated investment about INR 200 crores funded through internal accruals.
Capex of INR 180-200 crores in FY27 and about INR 50-60 crores in FY28; management said no term loan planned and no new debt contemplated.

Long-term targets: 20% volume growth, 20% revenue and profitability CAGR, EBITDA margin above 8%, ROCE above 20%, value-added products above 60% of revenue. Other expenses guided at INR 20-25 crores per quarter going forward. Inventory days targeted below 45.
capex_capacity: TKD lead recycling capacity raised 55% to 204,000 MTPA (from 132,000); operated at about 65% in FY26, with ramp to about 75% targeted in coming quarters.
Copper recycling capacity doubled to 12,000 MTPA in Q4 FY26; over 3,000 MT produced in Q4 per analyst question; ramp to 70% during FY27.
Copper cathode plant: 36,000 MTPA at TKD, Tamil Nadu, using integrated pyrorefining and electrorefining to make LME grade A cathodes; Phase 1 of 18,000 MTPA by December 2026.
Mundra project expected to start up in FY27 (no detail given).
FY26 capex of about INR 49 crores; FY27 INR 180-200 crores; FY28 INR 50-60 crores.
demand_pricing: Imports made up about 73% of lead procurement, 61% of plastic and 98% of copper in FY26.

Lead premium: management did not give a per-ton premium figure, attributing high realisations to niche alloys where POCL is a single-point source for certain customers; an analyst's estimate of about $700/t was not confirmed.

Copper sourcing: shipping lead times up 10-15 days due to Middle East conflict; contracts are CIF, so payments are not affected, and procurement is being diversified to Southeast Asia and domestic sources. Outbound freight impact about $2/t.
Copper scrap formula: management said margins are protected through hedging of metal and FX, and that purchase and sale formulas move together.
Industry outlook: management expects copper consumption to rise from about 1.2 million tons to 3-3.5 million tons over 3-4 years, citing energy transition and infrastructure demand.
Trading: Q4 included opportunistic copper trading (about INR 122 crores of purchases of stock in trade), which management said is not the core focus and is not expected to be a regular feature.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory/goods rise in Q4 and is it repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 included a copper trading opportunity with better margins than usual; it cannot say it will recur, though some trading has always occurred. Focus remains on manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative despite strong profits, and what is the receivables split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the trade receivables of about INR 265 crores were a point-in-time effect from an export consignment delayed by vessel movement, with INR 120-130 crores received around April 5. Vijay Balakrishnan said receivables are all finished goods; inventory rose only about INR 36 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 180 crore capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will be funded through internal accruals with no term loan. Total reserves plus equity is about INR 800 crores, borrowings about INR 150 crores (all short-term), and there is no long-term debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall in Q4, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mark-to-market charge of about INR 7 crores in the prior quarter reversed in Q4, and efficiencies across power, fuel and environmental costs lowered costs. Other expenses are expected at INR 20-25 crores per quarter going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the copper EBITDA per ton after cathode integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cathode is targeted at INR 60,000-70,000 per ton versus INR 35,000-40,000 for current recycling, on a conservative basis.

qa_highlights.question: Lead volume outlook versus the 204,000 MT capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 lead volume target is about 125,000-130,000 MT, with the 70% utilisation referring to the new TKD plant; some lines are capacity-limited by product mix. New products and customers were added.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 blended margin lower than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lead margins remained above 8%, while copper (about 40% of sales) runs at about 3.5-4%, bringing the blended margin to 6.4% in Q4.

risks_watch: Negative FY26 operating cash flow driven by INR 265 crore receivables; watch Q1 FY27 collections and whether cash flow turns positive.
Q4 lead volume dip (deliberate mix shift) versus FY27 guidance of 125,000-130,000 MT; the delivery of volume growth depends on the new TKD lines ramping up.
Copper cathode commissioning (Phase 1 by December 2026) and the INR 60,000-70,000/t margin target are not yet supported by trial production data.
Middle East conflict causing 10-20 day shipment delays and rising logistics costs; management says CIF contracts limit payment impact.
Copper price and FX volatility; management says it hedges fully, but Q4 margins were squeezed by copper mix.
Plastics unit recently moved; PAT positive status is early and per-ton figures have not been disclosed.
Lithium-ion recycling: management is studying feedstock and chemistry, with battery stock expected around 2028, but no capex is committed.
key_quotes: FY26 stands as one of the most remarkable years in POCL's journey with the company delivering all -time high production and sales volumes, revenue, EBITDA, PAT and profitability margins.
And I cannot specifically say that it will continue, but definitely, there will be some trading, which has always been there.
This is only a short-term blip. It's not a big blip. It was a conscious decision.
So technically around April 5, we received close to about INR 120 crores to INR 130 crores in payment in that immediate next week.
Q1 is a forward-looking statement. There is always growth is there in the current quarter. That's what we can say. Beyond that, it's not correct on our part to reveal the numbers.

532626|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR931 crore and PAT 32% to INR36 crore, while lead volumes fell on supply-chain disruption.
532626|2026-06.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 56%, 30% and 32% YoY to INR931 crore, INR56 crore and INR36 crore, with EBITDA margin about 6%. Copper volumes more than tripled YoY to record levels and copper EBITDA per ton rose 66% to INR48,488. Lead volumes moderated as shipping delays via the Strait of Hormuz constrained scrap imports, and management chose to prioritise value-added products (85% of lead revenue), giving a record lead EBITDA of INR21,595 per ton. Management says demand is intact and the constraint is supply, not demand.

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: Volumes moderated due to supply constraints; value-added products were 85% of segment revenue. Export mix 55% of lead sales. Management guides sustainable lead EBITDA of INR18,000-20,000 per ton.

segments.name: Copper
segments.commentary: Production and sales volumes each rose more than 3x YoY to record levels (about 4,000 tonnes in the quarter per analyst); export mix 25%. Copper expected to be about 45% of FY27 revenue. Existing capacity about 75% utilised.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q1 with net profit of about INR15 lakh on about 800 tonnes of volume.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Small production of about 200 metric tonnes in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Lead value-added mix for FY27 targeted at 65-70% (FY26 about 63%).
Lead EBITDA sustainable at INR18,000-20,000 per ton as volumes rise; Q1 INR21,595 was driven by 85% value-added mix.
Copper EBITDA per ton before value-addition guided above INR40,000 (earlier guidance INR35,000-40,000); cathode blended EBITDA guided INR60,000-65,000 per ton.
Management reiterated earlier FY27 lead volume guidance of about 1.25-1.3 lakh tonnes, saying it expects to close near that level, though it did not give a revised number.
2030 roadmap: over 15% volume growth, 20%+ CAGR in revenue and profitability, EBITDA margin above 8%, ROCE above 20%, over 60% revenue from value-added products.
FY27 capex about INR175 crore: maintenance INR20-25 crore, balance INR140-150 crore for copper plant. Management did not give volume guidance for FY27/FY28 by product yet.
capex_capacity: 36,000 tpa copper cathode plant at Thervoy Kandigai, Tamil Nadu, total investment about INR200 crore, funded from internal accruals; about INR25 crore spent so far.
Phase 1 (18,000 tpa) on track for commissioning in December 2026, trial runs in Q4 FY27; machine installation from end-September, Phase 2 (18,000 tpa) targeted for Q3 FY28.
Incremental 6,000 tpa copper recycling capacity commissioned in Q4 FY26 (copper recycling total about 12,000 tpa, in Andhra Pradesh); about 75% utilised. Target utilisation about 75% through FY27.
New 72,000 tpa lead (TKD) capacity utilisation below 50% because of the focus on value-added pure lead.
CRISIL upgraded outlook to A positive from A stable, rating reaffirmed.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand softness; the constraint is delayed shipments and supply-chain disruption.
Lead exports go mainly to Southeast Asia, not Europe; Middle East procurement below 5% of sourcing, with the main issue being shipping routes via the Strait of Hormuz.
Lead sourcing about 97% international in Q1; domestic prices were too high for profitable domestic buying, though management has started looking at domestic procurement.
Copper pricing was supported by tight availability, enabling a premium on copper sales.
Copper sourcing: mostly imports, with plans for 25-30% domestic sourcing going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Can lead volumes reach the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance given the current run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of closing up to the committed numbers but will see how supply chains evolve over the next 1-2 months; no revision given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there demand softness in lead, given exposure to Western and Middle East markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand softness; exports are mainly Southeast Asia. Only supply delays are affecting volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 16% YoY and 44% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics is a small part; the major driver is fuel prices and some additive prices that rose over the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the record lead EBITDA per ton one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a sustainable level is INR18,000-20,000 per ton; Q1 was high because of the 85% value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 of about INR175 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance INR20-25 crore; the balance of INR140-150 crore is for the new copper plant.

qa_highlights.question: Copper EBITDA per ton outlook before value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects above INR40,000 per ton going forward, aided by capacity efficiencies and a premium in the current tight market.

qa_highlights.question: EPR credits and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: EPR benefit minimal this quarter as most purchases were imports; unmonetised EPR credits remain on the books. Working capital not stretched because payments are made about a week before arrival at port.

risks_watch: Lead volume shortfall from shipping disruption (Strait of Hormuz) could put the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance at risk; monthly production fell in May and early June.
Cost inflation from fuel and additive prices, with other expenses up 44% QoQ.
Copper cathode commissioning slipping beyond December 2026 would delay margin uplift; the cathode blended EBITDA of INR60,000-65,000 per ton is not yet proven.
Copper scrap security as global supply tightens and more countries retain scrap; reliance on imports for most copper sourcing.
Lead EBITDA per ton could normalise toward INR18,000-20,000 as the value-added mix falls from 85%.
Lead volumes fell sharply YoY, with analysts noting a much steeper decline than a competitor; management declined to comment.

Several answers were defensive or repetitive when pressed on FY28 copper volumes and recycling capacity.

532630|2026-03.headline: Gokaldas Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to about 12% (16% ex-tariff impact per management), with FY27 guided to a couple of points of margin improvement.
532630|2026-03.overview: FY26 was disrupted by US reciprocal tariffs that stayed near 50% for much of the year, with AGOA lapse hitting Africa, yet total income rose 4% to INR4,065 crores and the EBITDA margin was held at the prior-year level. Q4 standalone margins improved on volume-driven operating leverage and the post-February normalisation of the penal tariff, with no tariff refunds booked. Management guides to a Y-o-Y margin improvement of a couple of percentage points in FY27 and Africa revenue of about $115-120 million, while BTPL is being merged in and is expected to turn EBITDA positive in H2 FY27. Net debt rose by INR395 crores on capex, BTPL investment and working capital, and management targets a INR75-100 crore working capital reduction in Gokaldas and Atraco.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone operating EBITDA margin Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.value: about 12% (about 16% adding back tariff impact; about 15.5% excluding provision reversals)
financial_highlights.change: Improved Q-o-Q and Y-o-Y, per analyst read of 200-400 bps

financial_highlights.metric: Net discount to customers FY26 (tariff offset)

segments.name: India operations (Gokaldas standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 operations grew 2% Y-o-Y while Indian apparel exports fell 10%; FY26 India operations grew 10% Y-o-Y. Standalone volume was 10.19 million pieces in Q4 (8.6 million ex-Matrix at INR773 realisation) and 33.627 million pieces for FY26 at INR765.

segments.name: Africa (Atraco)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about $80 million; FY27 target $115-120 million, with H1 run-rate about $24-25 million per quarter. Q4 volume 5.63 million pieces at INR405; FY26 16.27 million pieces at INR420. Management expects H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10%.

segments.name: BTPL (Bombay Rayon, fabric)
segments.commentary: Merger initiated subject to NCLT approval, expected in Q3 FY27. Utilisation near 50 lakh meters/month against 70 lakh capacity, expandable to 100 lakh for INR50-60 crores capex. FY27 revenue guided above INR1,000 crores; EBITDA breakeven in H1 and about 6-7% in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Matrix and other Indian subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Had minor setbacks in Q4 as customers shifted business to other regions during the 50% tariff period; management expects reversal in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone Y-o-Y EBITDA margin improvement of a couple of percentage points, conditional on no new tariff disruption; H1 FY27 margins still absorb about 3% sharper pricing given on H1 orders.
Africa FY27 revenue target $115-120 million (worst case $115 million), with H2 FY27 Africa EBITDA margin of 8-10%.
Working capital to be reduced by INR75-100 crores in FY27 across Gokaldas and Atraco, excluding BTPL merger impact.
Medium-term (FY28 steady state, excluding new capacity drag): India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, India:Africa revenue split about 75:25 to 80:20; BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.
Management said FY27 revenue growth would be much more than 10-12% excluding U.K./EU FTA benefits, which are not factored in; it targets at least 15% growth.
Two new premium customers in India (one US, one European) and two in Africa (one US, one European) to contribute revenue from FY27, about 5% of revenue in year one.
capex_capacity: Africa capacity expansion completed in FY26; one factory running 2 shifts on 20-25% of its capacity, with a second-shift opportunity without major capex.

Karnataka (Kolar Gold Fields) half-factory ramp-up expected through Q1-Q2 FY27 to full utilisation; Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal) 1,000-machine unit expected at full utilisation by Q3 FY27 (Sept-Oct), adding about INR175 crores revenue at full capacity; Karnataka adds about INR125 crores at steady state.
Two further planned factories (about INR300 crores steady-state revenue) with capex of INR80-100 crores over two years; decision expected in the next quarter or so, with revenue mainly FY28.
Total capacity to reach 104 million pieces including 12 million added (India about 7.5 million, Africa about 4.5 million); India 52 million and Africa 40 million pieces currently, per management.
BTPL: 70 lakh meters/month capacity, expandable to 100 lakh with INR50-60 crores capex; captive fabric consumption by Gokaldas about 30-35%.
demand_pricing: Reciprocal tariff of about 50% (including penal 25%) on India until mid-February 2026; penal tariff withdrawn, then a 10% tariff applied until July 24, 2026. Section 301 tariffs may reset to about 20% for rest of world from late July; Africa not under Section 301 probe (Kenya stays at 10%).
Tariff rebates given during the penal regime were up to about 15% of order value, partly clawed back from the supply chain; sharper pricing of about 3% continues in H1 FY27 and is removed in H2.
AGOA extended to December 2026; US administration reportedly moving to country-by-country deals; Kenya FTA not expected by end-2026.
US retail sales grew 8% and UK 6% in CY25; US retailers pared imports from H2 CY25. Spring 27 orders being booked; customers ordering conservatively.

Input cost inflation from Middle East war (polyester, packaging, fuel, trims, cotton); pass-through being attempted in H2 orders, with partial recovery expected given customer resistance and competitor under-utilisation in SE Asia and China.
Hedging: about 80% of revenue hedged for the next two quarters at INR87-91/USD; 50% for the following two. Rupee depreciation benefit not yet in numbers, expected in H2.
Labour cost inflation in India: Haryana announced 35% wage increase from April 1 and UP 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 12% standalone margin be sustained, and what is the Africa margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Africa H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10% and operating leverage in India; Matrix and other subsidiaries were hit by pivoted orders in Q4 and should recover in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital reduce in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a reduction of INR75-100 crores in Gokaldas and Atraco, with BTPL's working capital to be added on merger; the INR200 crore increase reflected inventory build for Q1 orders (Chinese holidays) and year-end receivables.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to volumes if AGOA lapses again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it refused to share AGOA-related discounts last time and let volume fall; now it has a broader Africa customer base and can offer some AGOA-related support if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Were tariff refunds booked in Q4 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff reversals were factored in; the Q4 gain came from volume-driven operating leverage and no tariff discounts after mid-February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 margin outlook with BTPL included?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state FY28 India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Are the acquired entities meeting internal targets?
qa_highlights.answer: No, not in FY26 due to tariff disruption; management expects them to perform to plan in FY27.

risks_watch: Section 301 tariff reset from July 24, 2026 and whether India returns to about 20%.
AGOA expiry in December 2026 and timing of renewal; Kenya FTA uncertainty.
Cotton, polyester and fuel cost pass-through versus customer resistance in H2 FY27.
BTPL NCLT merger timing (Q3 FY27) and its loss-making run-rate (-4 to -5% EBITDA in Q4 FY26); integration working capital.
Labour cost inflation in North India (Haryana 35%, UP 25% wage increases).
Rupee hedges at INR87-91/USD could limit currency gains; debt rising with capex and net debt up INR395 crores.
Tax expense elevated at consolidated level because losses at overseas and new Indian subsidiaries get no tax credit.
532630|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the demand and margin recovery narrative, but cautious on H1 FY27 margins, tariff timing and AGOA renewal. Management repeatedly hedged FY28 and FY27 guidance with geopolitical caveats and declined to factor in pending FTAs.

It looks like the worst is behind us.
Africa is not under Section 301 investigation, giving further comfort.
Certainly, there is no rebate on top of it at all for the year.

rows.why: Management targets at least 15% FY27 revenue growth, with Africa at $115-120 million versus about $80 million in FY26 and Q4 India operations up only 2% Y-o-Y, so the step-up depends on the new capacity and customers landing.

rows.why: Two new premium customers in India (one US, one European) and two in Africa (one US, one European) contribute from FY27, about 5% of revenue in year one; no specific new product launches are named.

rows.why: Merger initiated subject to NCLT approval expected in Q3 FY27; BTPL revenue is INR190 crores in Q4 FY26 with EBITDA loss of about 4-5%, and FY27 revenue is guided above INR1,000 crores with EBITDA breakeven in H1 and about 6-7% in H2 FY27.

rows.why: Management targets INR75-100 crores reduction across Gokaldas and Atraco after a near INR200 crore FY26 build for Q1 orders and year-end receivables, though net debt rose INR395 crores.

rows.why: AGOA extended only to December 2026 and Section 301 may reset India to about 20% from late July; Africa FY26 revenue about $80 million, and management says it can offer AGOA-related support if needed.

532630|2026-06.headline: Gokaldas Q1 FY27: consolidated income up 21% YoY and EBITDA up 17%, with Africa up 45% and India up 16% amid a sector-wide 12% decline.
532630|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong, broad-based quarter, with consolidated income up 21% YoY and consolidated EBITDA up 17% (India EBITDA up 14%). India revenue grew 16% YoY against a 12% fall in Indian apparel exports, partly helped by the lower US tariff regime. Africa grew 45% YoY on AGOA renewal and a weak prior-year base, but Africa EBITDA margin was about 8%, below normal. Cost pressures from wages (Haryana minimum wage up 35% from April 2026), fuel, chemicals, logistics and freight were significant, partly offset by overhead control and a weaker rupee. BTPL (fabric unit) remains loss-making at the operating level, with merger expected in Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Target: double-digit by Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28

financial_highlights.metric: India wage cost increase in Q1
Other expenses cost hit (utilities and logistics)

financial_highlights.change: Mix-driven; management disputed the volume metric

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue up 16% YoY and EBITDA up 14%, versus a 12% decline in Indian apparel exports. Matrix plus stand-alone India ASP cited at INR 613 with about 1.53 million pieces for the old Gurgaon units. Central India plants running at about 85% utilisation; South India plants full.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Revenue up 45% YoY on AGOA renewal and a weak Q1 FY26 base. EBITDA margin about 8%, with management targeting double-digit by Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Utilisation at 80-85%; FY27 visibility of USD 112-115 million against a USD 120 million target.

segments.name: BTPL (fabric unit)
segments.commentary: Running at 50-53 lakh meters per month, with Q1 turnover around INR 170 crore and operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%. Targets EBITDA break-even in H1, EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27; merger expected in Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Growth: management said 15%-plus growth is 'straightforward' and it should do better; mid-to-high-teens was floated by the analyst, with management not confirming a number. Q2 FY27 revenue expected to resemble Q1; Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked.
Africa FY27 revenue visibility of USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, with a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.
Africa EBITDA margin expected back to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28.
ETR guided at 20-22% for FY27 as international operations contribute.
Wage, fuel and logistics cost pressure expected to partly ease in H2 if conditions improve; uncertainty remains. Pass-through pricing being applied to new orders.

Capex: about INR 80 crore mentioned in presentation; Jharkhand and Karnataka greenfield units total about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27), with steady-state revenue of about INR 350 crore from FY29. Bhopal second unit yields revenue from H2 FY27.
Potential 2,000-3,000 extra machines (about INR 200 crore revenue per 1,000 machines) to be decided within 3 months; larger spend in FY28.
capex_capacity: Bhopal second unit ramping up, expected to reach near full utilisation by Q4 FY27; adds about 3.5 million pieces and about INR 175-200 crore steady-state revenue.

Karnataka and Ranchi existing-factory machine additions (about 500-700 machines) are being commissioned in FY27; total of commissioned Bhopal Phase 2, Karnataka and Ranchi adds about INR 275 crore revenue potential.

New Jharkhand and Karnataka facilities: total investment about INR 100 crore, about 3.5 million pieces each, steady-state revenue about INR 350 crore combined; expected on stream H2 FY28, full potential FY29.
Africa: capacity already in place to deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue; second shift used for swing capacity; no significant Africa capex planned until existing options are exhausted.
BTPL capacity about 50 lakh meters per month, expected to grow about 30%; new customer onboarding with operations starting in Q2.
demand_pricing: US and UK end-consumer demand grew strongly through the first six months of CY26, though US growth slowed in June; EU and UK apparel imports declined through the first five months of FY27 per management.
US Section 301 tariff places India on par with competing sourcing countries, while China and Vietnam face 12.5%. India-UK FTA brings parity with Bangladesh and Vietnam in the UK.
Management says European buyers and US buyers are increasing inquiries and business towards India, extending beyond fashion and outerwear into shirts and bottoms; denim inquiries also rising.
Pricing: fabric cost pass-through is standard; some items (poly bags, cartons, fuel) were not priced into Q1 orders set in January and will be priced going forward.
Product mix: ASPs range from about USD 40-50 for high-value products to lower-value items; average realisation in India about INR 613 per piece for Gurgaon units.
UK is about 4-4.5% of total revenue; focus on larger UK players such as Marks & Spencer. Fibre mix about 65% cotton and up to 30% man-made (annual).

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth was only 3.4%, so where does India volume go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume is a misleading metric because Q1 and Q2 are high-value outerwear with 150-250 minutes of content per garment, versus about 22-25 minutes for a shirt; it added there is no YoY volume drop and growth is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Does the strong order book mean the mid-teens growth guide holds, or can growth be mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Spring '27 orders execute in Q3 FY27 and revenue traction for that period and beyond looks similar to Q1; 15%-plus growth was called 'straightforward' and it should do better.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa EBITDA margin recover to double digits from about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28, with H2 the differentiator; it cited AGOA expiring December with a 2-year extension passed by the Senate and awaiting the House and presidential assent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the visibility on shipping delays, and could they delay orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is the worst shipping environment; outbound FOB shipments can wait about 2 weeks for a vessel, and it expects easing over the next two quarters as the war and typhoon issues ease.

qa_highlights.question: How do India incentive cuts (RoSCTL) and the BTPL merger affect margins, and is the Africa margin base higher?
qa_highlights.answer: RoSCTL is about 3.5% and management's worst case is a halving to about 1.75%, which it expects to offset; BTPL should reach mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA after merger in Q3. Management said the EBITDA margin would be a bit higher than the analyst's base, and it sees the rupee weakness as a cushion (about 70% of dollars hedged at about INR 89).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 visibility, particularly for India?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 are booked; Q2 revenue should look like Q1. Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked now and the projection looks good despite US inflation concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Is India gaining share from China and Vietnam after the tariff change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2.5% advantage is not remarkable by itself, but European and US buyers are increasing inquiries for India across shirts, bottoms and denim, not just fashion and outerwear.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 35% minimum wage hike a larger hit, and how is it being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Haryana minimum wage rose 35% from April 2026 but overall wages for the Gurgaon/Manesar units rose only 14-15%; India wage cost increase in Q1 was about INR 20 crore, absorbed in the system. Karnataka increase was about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other expenses increase and the ETR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose by about INR 5-6 crore on utilities, gas, fuel and chemicals plus inbound and outbound logistics, partly expected to ease in H2; FY27 ETR is guided at 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BTPL Q1 performance and the break-even timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: BTPL had about INR 170 crore fabric turnover in Q1 with operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%; management targets EBITDA break-even in H1 (Q2), EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity plan, including Jharkhand, Karnataka and Bhopal?
qa_highlights.answer: Jharkhand and Karnataka together need about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27) for about INR 350 crore steady-state revenue, coming on stream H2 FY28; Bhopal Phase 2 adds about 3.5 million pieces and INR 175-200 crore revenue. Management also said it may add 2,000-3,000 machines with a decision within 3 months and larger spend in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Africa plan require more capex, and what is the Africa capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant Africa capex is planned until second-shift options are exhausted; capacity in place can deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue. FY27 visibility is USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indian business share, utilisation and product-wise breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Central India plants run about 85% utilisation and South India plants are full; Africa is at 80-85%. Management gave the old Gurgaon units at 1.53 million pieces at INR 613 ASP, while Matrix alone was about 1.5 million pieces at INR 613.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric mix and UK exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Cotton is about 65% or a little higher and man-made fibres up to 30%, on an annual basis per management. UK is about 4-4.5% of revenue, with focus on larger players such as Marks & Spencer.

risks_watch: Africa EBITDA margin (about 8% in Q1) must recover to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28; AGOA expires December 2026 and the extension is still awaiting House and presidential approval.
Shipping and logistics: container shortages, Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea disruption, and typhoon-related sailing delays; FOB outbound goods can sit about 2 weeks before boarding.
Wage and cost inflation: Haryana minimum wage up 35%, RoSCTL at about 3.5% with a possible halving to 1.75%, plus fuel, chemicals and poly bag/carton costs not priced into Q1 orders.
BTPL execution: operational EBITDA about -7.5% to -8% in Q1; break-even in Q2, EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27; merger expected in Q3 FY27.
India volume metric disputed (3.4% per analyst), with growth attributed to mix; Q2 revenue expected to be similar to Q1, and Q3/Q4 orders still being booked.
Demand: US import growth slowed in June, EU and UK apparel imports declined, and US inflation could affect retail demand.
key_quotes: The quarter was a strong one, and importantly, the strength was broad based.
So we can't put an estimate to it.
Our business booking for beyond December seems to be robust.
So when we say we see a strong growth possibility, we are looking at Spring '27 for now.
I think the worst is being experienced now. My sense is in the next 2 quarters, it should ease.

532633|2026-03.headline: Alldigi Tech FY26 revenue rose 9.6% to INR598.7 crore and EBITDA 25% to INR162 crore, with management guiding to mid-teens revenue growth in FY27.
532633|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR154.7 crore (+5.9% YoY, +1.3% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR43.7 crore (+24.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin for FY26 at 27.1% versus 23.7% in FY25. Tech & Digital (T&D) was the growth engine at +22.3% YoY in Q4, while BPM was flat YoY at INR110.4 crore as management deliberately exited low-margin domestic FTE business. Management said about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin BPM business, and guided to mid-teens revenue growth and a 1-2% margin improvement for FY27. Q4 PAT rose 49.7% YoY to INR28.9 crore, and FY26 PAT was flat at INR82.2 crore. This was the first call with new CEO Natarajan Laxsmanan, who joined about a month earlier.

segments.name: Tech & Digital (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR44.3 crore (+22.3% YoY, +14.5% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR156.2 crore (+16.5%). Q4 segment margin INR19.5 crore (44%); FY26 segment margin INR66.6 crore (+28.9%). Processed 49.9 lakh employee records in Q4 and 191.5 lakh in FY26; added INR40.1 crore new ACV.

segments.name: BPM (CXM)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR110.4 crore (+0.4% YoY, flat); FY26 revenue INR442.4 crore (+7.3%). Q4 segment margin INR15 crore (about 13.6%); FY26 segment margin INR62.3 crore (+16.8%). International share of BPM revenue 78% in FY26 (73% prior year). Added INR54.1 crore new ACV; international BPM revenue grew 8.7% YoY in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens, per the CEO, similar to the aspiration stated for FY26.
EBITDA margin expected to improve about 1-2% in FY27 (management said 1-1.5% annual margin growth is typical), but no absolute margin number was given.
BPM segment margin expected to hold around 13-14%; the Q4 QoQ dip was a one-off linked to a leave policy alignment with the holding company.
T&D growth expected to be slightly higher than BPM growth; international mix expected to keep rising.
Depreciation for FY27 expected to rise only modestly (management said a couple of crore from the new Chennai office), with a sub-10% increase implied on the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.
Management expects no significant negative currency impact on revenue; a weaker rupee is expected to add to margin.
FY27 existing-customer headcount expected to be flat, with no major positive growth in employee records anticipated.
capex_capacity: Office upgrade underway in Chennai (new office being built) and Noida, with about INR20 crore of investment for the Chennai facility.
Admin and facility capex typically runs INR20-25 crore a year.
Current depreciation run-rate is about INR58.6 crore; management expects only a small increase beyond the new office.
SP4 platform migration completed for India-based customers, targeted at about INR3 crore a year in efficiency gains for T&D.
HRMS Version 2 (integrated HRMS and payroll, AI-enabled) to be released in FY27; PulseHR.ai to automate inbound query handling and cut turnaround time.
demand_pricing: HRO international order book was about 48% of total order book as of March 31, 2026 (no comparable domestic figure given).
T&D ACV wins have consistently been more than 60% from international clients.
Pipeline of large BPM brands is in place, but timing is uncertain: client decisions were on hold due to macro conditions and the war, impacting healthcare clients.
RCM (revenue cycle management) entry: processing began about a quarter ago and has doubled in FTE; further expansion with the same client is in progress.
FY27 BPM focus verticals: healthcare and RCM, international insurance, and international collections.
Existing T&D customers have plateaued; about 90% of FY26 record growth came from new customers.
Deal closure: about 30% of deals closed at CHRO/CFO level; smaller deals (under 1,000 employees) close at HR level; CEO involvement is rare.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HRO revenue grow faster than payroll-process volumes, and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue is not directly proportional to employee numbers because of one-time change requests, year-end tax work, new wage code implementation, and currency benefits from international business. Higher revenue than headcount growth is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 growth was constant currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said 3.3% of FY26 growth came from currency depreciation and 6.3% from company efforts.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BPM headcount decline continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exit from low-margin business will continue through FY27; about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue CAGR below the mid-teens target, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the strategic exit from low-margin business and industry factors. It still sees mid-teens growth for FY27, which it said is slightly above industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to a new large BPM client and how will margins change after the exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline, citing a large pipeline and deals delayed by macro conditions. It said the low-margin exit will have minimal impact because it is only about 10% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Why do segment margins (about INR129 crore) differ from reported EBITDA (INR162 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said segment margins are reported at PBT level after depreciation and finance costs, net of unallocable items, other income and expenses. He offered to reconcile offline.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company win deals and what is the sales structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price, scale, platform flexibility, operational accuracy and turnaround time. International sales are now run by geography-specific teams with rainmaker and technology partners.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and depreciation outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain guided to admin/facility capex of INR20-25 crore a year plus about INR20 crore for the Chennai office, with only a small rise in depreciation from the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.

risks_watch: BPM growth depends on landing one or two large clients; none was onboarded in the last about 12 months, and timing is not guided.
Continued headcount decline in BPM as low-margin exits proceed; about 10% of the portfolio remains low-margin.
Flat existing-customer headcount; no major positive growth in employee records expected for FY27, so growth relies on new clients and one-time revenue.
Currency tailwind contributed about 3.3% of FY26 growth; management declined to comment on future FX effects.
AI could cut client headcounts; management called this both a challenge and an opportunity.
Segment margin reconciliation to EBITDA was not clear on the call; Vaibhav Chechani's query was left for an offline discussion.
Q4 FY26 BPM margin dip was attributed to a one-off leave policy alignment with the holding company, which is yet to be quantified.
532633|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on T&D momentum, margins and the FY27 mid-teens growth target. Cautious and vague on BPM large-client timing, which management declined to pin to a timeline, and avoided giving absolute margin numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided a 1-2% EBITDA margin improvement from the FY26 base of 27.1% (versus 23.7% in FY25), backed by SP4 platform savings of about INR3 crore a year and a weaker rupee, though BPM margin is guided to hold at 13-14%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No production capacity is being added; the only build is the Chennai admin/facility office (~INR20 crore) and management expects flat existing-customer headcount in FY27, so no new delivery capacity is signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects flat existing-customer headcount and no major positive employee-record growth in FY27, so volume growth depends on new clients and the RCM expansion (FTE doubled) while BPM headcount keeps falling as the ~10% low-margin book is exited.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at admin and facility spend of INR20-25 crore a year plus the Chennai office, with utilisation not disclosed and no new plant, land or board-level expansion plan mentioned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the mid-teens FY27 revenue guide and gave no absolute margin figure, with existing T&D customers plateauing and no large BPM client onboarded in about 12 months.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: BPM large-client wins are not guided and macro-delayed (healthcare decisions on hold), and FY26 PAT was flat at INR82.2 crore, so the mid-teens FY27 revenue target depends on new clients landing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: HRMS Version 2 (integrated HRMS and payroll, AI-enabled) is set for release in FY27, and the RCM service line has already begun processing with FTE doubling in a quarter.

rows.label: Large BPM client onboarding (healthcare / RCM, international insurance)
rows.why: Pipeline of large BPM brands is in place but no large client was onboarded in about 12 months and decisions are on hold, so the timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Currency tailwind and HRO revenue outpacing headcount
rows.why: 3.3% of FY26 growth came from currency depreciation and management expects a weaker rupee to add to margin, though it declined to comment on future FX effects.

rows.label: BPM low-margin exit continuing through FY27
rows.why: About 10% of the portfolio remains low-margin and the domestic FTE exit continues, which will lower BPM headcount while lifting mix (BPM FY26 segment margin INR62.3 crore, +16.8%).

tone.note: Management was confident on T&D momentum (+22.3% YoY in Q4), the mid-teens FY27 revenue target and a 1-2% margin gain, but was vague on BPM large-client timing and gave no absolute margin figure; analysts pushed on the segment-to-EBITDA reconciliation, which was deferred offline.
